matches.round: Round 9 (final round, Day 1): Fire Diao Chan against Wind Umbra Tristan

players.name: Z3US
players.deck: Fire Diao Chan aggro from Indonesia (Firebloom Flourish x3, Searing Rebuke x3, Fractal of Sparks, Shimmering Refraction, Ravenous Pyre, Ashwick Cremator, Necklace of Foresight, Fanatical Devotee, Acolyte of Cultivation, Wind Resonance Bauble, Grand Crusader's Ring, Spirit of Fire with alternate art; Scatter Essence x3-4, Safeguard Amulet, Blanche and Staggering Strike in the side)

players.name: Schwarzer
players.deck: Wind Umbra Tristan, a slightly different build than usual (Guan Yu, Prime Exemplar x2; Windmill Engineer; Windbless Lookout; Sadi; Spirit of Wind; Fairy Whispers; Surveil the Winds; Incapacitate; Reclaim; Innervate Agility; Shadow's Claw; Censer of Restful Peace; Slice and Dice; Staggering Strike x3, Blanche, Safeguard Amulet and Ensnaring Fumes in the side)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters think Schwarzer should bring in Blanche, Safeguard Amulet and Scatter Essence to deal with Firebloom Flourish, and the three Staggering Strikes to keep Z3US from a lethal line. They say cards like Ensnaring Fumes are too spell-based to matter, and even Guan Yu does little, because Diao Chan seldom fights a board. A printout issue with the sideboard list was sorted out by the judges before game two.
Z3US likes Necklace of Foresight, which glimpses four cards, to find his Firebloom Flourishes faster. The casters say Z3US may also bring in anti-Tristan tech such as Crystallized Essence.

games.summary: Z3US wins — an opening of triple Firebloom Flourish and Ravenous Pyre lets him dump his hand every turn, and Tristan dies at level one

beats.text: Schwarzer wins the die roll and goes first with Spirit of Wind, drawing seven cards. He opens with a Windmill Engineer and holds a Sadi and Innervate Agility, but the casters could not see a Reclaim. Z3US would have loved to go first with fire aggro.

Z3US plays Spirit of Fire and starts with two Firebloom Flourishes, the card that lets Diao Chan sit at low influence: at the beginning of the end phase, with four or fewer influence, he draws a card into memory and puts a glimmer counter on his champion. He dumps his hand each turn and goes from three up to five influence, always with six cards or more.

Z3US uses Shimmering Refraction for four damage and the triple Firebloom Flourishes ping for the rest. Schwarzer incapacitates one Searing Rebuke and the casters say he would have died a turn earlier without it, but there are too many fire damage sources. Tristan dies without leaving level one.

games.summary: Z3US wins — three Searing Rebukes, with Fractal of Sparks pinging himself, kill through Incapacitate and a Censer

beats.text: Schwarzer plays Spirit of Wind and a very interesting turn-one Blanche, Sheltering Saint, and holds a Reclaim to keep it protected. He then plays Fairy Whispers but drops to two cards in hand. Z3US sees the opening, and the first Firebloom Flourish and Blanche die to his damage.

Every card Z3US puts down is answered or taken off the board, but Fractal of Sparks deals one every turn, and the Necklace of Foresight digs for another Firebloom Flourish. Schwarzer materializes Shadow's Claw and passes, letting the Searing Rebuke damage come in; Z3US recovers four with a fast gear. Schwarzer has no Surveil the Winds to find the lethal opening.

Schwarzer keeps having to spend Incapacitate on a Searing Rebuke and cannot find the extra two damage for lethal. Z3US redirects an attack, plays Searing Rebuke in response to the Censer of Restful Peace, and has the Fractal of Sparks ping himself to trigger the Rebuke. The casters count three Searing Rebukes in the game, and Z3US wins 2-0, going 6-3 and into Day 2. Schwarzer finishes at 5-4.

matches.sourceNote: Cleaned broadcast transcript, Ascent Akihabara Day 1 Round 9 VOD (stream match). Casters call the players "Zeus" and "Schwarzer" (Omnidex usernames Z3US and Schwarzer). Result per Omnidex (Z3US 2-0). Card names are as called by the casters and may contain minor ASR errors; this was a smaller file so it was read with light sampling, and some play order within the games is uncertain.

matches.round: Round 9 (final round, Day 1, stream match) — win-and-in for both players: Wind Umbra Tristan against Water Ciel Nico level 1 allies

players.name: Silvercrowx
players.deck: Wind Umbra Tristan (Mastermind Scheme, Shadowstrike, Slice and Dice, Shadow's Claw, Windwalker Boots, Surveil the Winds, Sadi, Winbless Lookout, Windmill Engineer, Aesan Protector, Stifling Trap, Dream Fairy, Deflecting Edge, Blackmarket Broker, Incapacitate)

players.name: Limbo
players.deck: Water Ciel, Nico level 1 allies (Lily, Marine Castellan; Snow White, Weiss Queen; Nia, Mistveiled Scout; Corhazi Trapper; Song of Frost; Storm of Thorns; Freezing Hail; Frostbind; Castling Boon; Tariff Ring; Grand Crusader's Ring; Magebane Lash; Smoke Bombs)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters think Limbo boards in extra water cards, such as a Menzo-armour card, in favor of the Nico plan, and say both decks have Mandate of Honour in the side. They say Silvercrowx's side has no Shadow Reaper plan, so he cannot ensnare Limbo's board.

games.summary: Limbo wins — Storm of Thorns, taunt allies and Song of Frost keep Tristan from ever connecting

beats.text: Limbo opens with a three-attack hindered Seneschal on turn one, and Frostbind on the Blackmarket Broker's reclaim denies Silvercrowx his floating memory. The casters say two taunt allies are very hard to deal with, because swinging into one makes you swing into the other.

Limbo has Castling Boon and Corhazi Trapper in hand and nothing on his board dies. Lily returns cards each time he trades. Silvercrowx goes up to Tristan level one with three preparation counters, and the casters say it will be very difficult for him to come back.

Silvercrowx finds a Shadowstrike and Mastermind Scheme, goes up to 12 preparation counters and redirects with his shadows. Limbo holds a Storm of Thorns, a Song of Frost and other defensive cards, and every Tristan swing is stopped. The casters say Silvercrowx cannot close the game out.
Limbo returns to a full board of allies and Magebane Lash counters. Silvercrowx loses prep to every defensive card and Limbo wins game one by attrition.

games.summary: Limbo wins — Tariff Ring and Storm of Thorns undo Silvercrowx's preparation again and again, and the allies swing in

beats.text: Silvercrowx has a weak hand for the game: reclaiming Sadi makes no sense, and he has a Windmill Engineer and an Ancient Protector to play. Limbo uses the Grand Crusader's Ring and a Storm of Thorns, and Silvercrowx cannot clear the Corhazi Trapper's board.

Limbo uses Freezing Hail to bounce the Windmill Engineer and the Aesan Protector, and Silvercrowx must level up and loses another Aesan Protector. The casters note that Silvercrowx has three Aesan Protectors in the deck, and that his allies cannot swing past Limbo's Tariff Ring.

Silvercrowx is stuck in a loop where he builds his preparation counters and then loses them. The casters liken him to Sisyphus climbing a hill. Limbo's Lily and Corhazi Trapper return, and Limbo adds a Snow White to shut down attacks.

Silvercrowx swings his Windmill Engineer, Sadi and Winbless Lookout into Lily, but Limbo has more damage on board than he expected and finishes the game through the Aesan Protector. The casters say it was the ninth round and everyone was tired. Limbo has won an invite to Day 2.

matches.round: Round 10 (Day 2, Round 1) — Normal Rai (Arcane spell combo) against Fire Merlin

players.name: Muck1234
players.deck: Normal Rai (all-Arcane brew with about 30 Arcane spells: Careful Study, Power Overwhelming, Tome of Sacred Lightning, Arcane Blast, Erratic Bolt, Advent of the Stormcaller, Shattering Discharge, Peer into Mana, Crystallized Destiny, Topsy Decree)

players.name: ZeRoMagus
players.deck: Fire Merlin (Three of Hearts, Fluffy Shopkeep, Liminal Guide, four Dungeon Guides, Hasty Messenger, Backup Charger, Resolute Stand, Orb of Sealing)

sideboardNotes.text: ZeRoMagus boards Harmonious Mantra and uses Kongming’s Shifting Currents to support healing through Rai’s damage.

games.summary: Muck1234 wins — level 12 from Enlightenment counters, then Erratic Bolt and two Arcane Blasts for 18

beats.text: ZeRoMagus starts with Three of Hearts and plays Orb of Sealing, which flips all Muck1234's banished Arcane cards face down. The casters say this is the problem card for Rai: Muck1234 must play an Arcane Sight to break the Orb and turn them face up. Muck1234 stays at level 2 and does not find a Dungeon Guide.

Muck1234 puts three Arcane cards into memory and levels to three. He keeps his hand up with Enlightenment counters, plays Tome of Sacred Lightning and banishes Arcane cards every turn. With Power Overwhelming he reaches level 12, then 13, and he sculpts the top of his deck with Careful Study.

Muck1234 keeps two Arcane Blasts on top of the deck and throws nine banished cards into Erratic Bolt. Nine damage plus two Arcane Blasts is 18, and ZeRoMagus, on Merlin, has no answer. The casters say that this is the most extreme version of a Rai turn they have seen.

games.summary: Muck1234 wins — 21 damage through Merlin's board, with Advent of the Stormcaller and Erratic Bolt

beats.text: ZeRoMagus has a better game than game 1. Fluffy Shopkeep on turn one, then Liminal Guide and a Backup Charger, with more than seven influence.

Muck1234 draws with Peer into Mana but runs low on influence. ZeRoMagus levels to three; the casters anticipate four Dungeon Guides and two Hasty Messengers. Muck1234’s Topsy Decree interrupts the Guide sequence, leaving ZeRoMagus low on influence.

Muck1234 plays Enfeebling Orb to stop two plays, which pops Crystallized Destiny, and plays Tome of Sacred Lightning and a 13 to 15 level turn. Advent of the Stormcaller and Erratic Bolt add up to 21 damage, and the casters count that ZeRoMagus is dead even with Harmonious Mantra.

matches.sourceNote: Cleaned broadcast transcript, Ascent Manila Day 2 VOD, Round 10 (the first round of Day 2). Casters call the players "Mark/Muck" (Omnidex username Muck1234) and "Zero Magus" (ZeRoMagus). Result per Omnidex (2-0). Card names are as called by the casters and may contain minor ASR errors.

matches.round: Round 11 (Day 2, Round 2) — Fire aggro Guardian against Fire Oblation level 3, with Top 8 on the line

players.name: Tsu
players.deck: Fire aggro Guardian (CL, level 1: Omen stacking and new fire Guardian attack cards: Arthur, Young Heir; Veteran Blazebearer, Inverted Pyroslash, Heated Vengeance, Intensified Pyre, Impact Hammer, Blazing Throw, Cinder Geyser, Ignis Deus, Smoke Bombs, Censer of Restful Peace)

players.name: Over9000
players.deck: Fire Oblation (CL, level 3 — Baleful Oblation, Liminal Guide, Dungeon Guide, Advent of the Stormcaller, Resolute Stand, Crystallized Destiny, Fluffy Shopkeep, Gentle Respite, Cremation Ritual)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters see Orb of Sealing and Restorative Flame in Tsu's sideboard. Orb of Sealing hurts a level 3 Oblation deck. Restorative Flame heals six and can save Tsu from a Baleful Oblation kill, and the deck lists are open, so Over9000 knows it is there.
Over9000 plans to side out some of the extra Spirits. The casters say he also wants cards that stop Omens, and that Crystallized Destiny and Resolute Stand could have done more work in game 1.

games.summary: Tsu wins in about 8 minutes — Arthur, Veteran Blazebearer and Inverted Pyroslash pressure Over9000 before he can level

beats.text: Tsu levels to CL level 1 and gets Omen stacking immediately. Over9000 also levels to level 1. Veteran Blazebearer has steadfast, so it is a taunt on turn one, and Tsu plays Hasty Messenger, discarding Gentle Respite, and Fluffy Shopkeep to draw a card into memory.

Arthur, Young Heir comes down on turn two and Tsu attacks with Arthur and the Blazebearer. His fire Guardian attack cards, Inverted Pyroslash and Blazing Charge, hit for three or five with Impact Hammer, and they cost less with Omens. Over9000 loses influence each time he must play a card to survive, and Censer of Restful Peace stops his Gentle Respite from giving him a plus one.

Over9000 cannot level to Umbra level 3 because Tsu keeps up the pressure. The casters say Over9000 has Resolute Stand in hand but nothing else. He shakes his head when asked for a response, and the attack resolves for lethal.

games.summary: Tsu wins — Over9000 has a slow hand of level-three cards, and Heated Vengeance, Blazing Throw and Intensified Pyre end the game

beats.text: Over9000 goes first with Liminal Guide and Cremation Ritual, but his hand has Dungeon Guide, Liminal Guide, Baleful Oblation, Advent of the Stormcaller and Resolute Stand and few cheap plays. The casters say this slow start is as dangerous as it gets against fire aggro.

Tsu plays Arthur, Young Heir and a Veteran Blazebearer again, and they deal six damage per turn. Over9000 uses Resolute Stand and loses a Baleful Oblation card, and the Dungeon Guide level-up comes too late. Over9000 only has two influence for the Fluffy Shopkeep intercept, and Tsu removes it with Smoke Bombs.

Tsu plays Fire Resonance Bauble to draw more cards and puts Over9000 at 11, then 14, with attacks. Heated Vengeance comes in for seven. Blazing Throw and Intensified Pyre add the rest of the damage with Cinder Geyser, and Over9000 is dead before he reaches level 3.

matches.sourceNote: Cleaned broadcast transcript, Ascent Manila Day 2 VOD, Round 11. Casters call the players "Two" (Omnidex username Tsu) and "Over 9,000" (Over9000). Result per Omnidex (Tsu 2-0). Card names are as called by the casters and may contain minor ASR errors; the champion line for both decks is shown only as "CL" in the captions.

matches.round: Round 12 (Day 2, Round 3) — Wind Tristan against Wind Luxom Zander, both at 8-2-1 and fighting for Top 8

players.name: HenkieTheGoat
players.deck: Wind Tristan (double Mastermind Scheme, Topsy Decree, Dungeon Guide, Sadi, Assassin's Ripper, Shadowstrike, Shadow's Claw, Incapacitate, Windwalker Boots; about 23 Wind and 29 Normal cards)

players.name: Zefier
players.deck: Wind Luxom Zander (Lightweaver's Assault, Luxem Sight, Gleaming Cut, Vanish from Sight, Juggle Knives, Backup Charger, Turbo Charge, Unmake Duality, Prismspire Scepter, Creative Shock, Regal Inquisition)

matches.result: HenkieTheGoat wins 2-1 (game 2 awarded to Zefier by a game loss for an illegal play)

sideboardNotes.text: HenkieTheGoat boards out his Dream Fairies, which do little against Luxom. The casters name Tempest Downfall, a fast-speed three damage spell, as a way to finish a Spirit of Serene Fire release on the stack.

Zefier has another Excalibur, three Regal Inquisitions, Resolute Stand and extra Vanish from Sights in his sideboard. The casters expect the Regal Inquisition to come in, because it takes the Tristan player's key cards, and say that a few extra Vanish from Sights would have helped him survive game 1.

games.summary: HenkieTheGoat wins — double Mastermind Scheme doubles his preparation counters to 24 and Shadowstrike deals 29

beats.text: Zefier opens with Backup Charger into Turbo Charge and the Unmake Duality draw engine, but he finds no floating memory. HenkieTheGoat plays Topsy Decree, which removes Zefier's floating memory and a Gentle Respite, and a triple Dungeon Guide line. Purifying Thurible is of little use because Zefier's graveyard is small.

Zefier levels up and starts to put Lightweaver's Assaults on HenkieTheGoat (he is at 19 maximum life). He reveals three Lightweaver's Assaults and a Luxem Sight with Prismspire Scepter, so HenkieTheGoat must put four cards in memory. Gleaming Cut adds damage and Zefier has 12 damage on HenkieTheGoat. The casters say Zefier is in a strong position.

HenkieTheGoat plays Windwalker Boots and Surveil the Winds, then a double Mastermind Scheme with Innervate Agility, which takes his preparation counters from six to 12 and then to 24. He keeps an Incapacitate for the Lightweaver's Assault and another for Vanish from Sight. Zefier has no answer to a Shadowstrike with Shadow's Claw, which deals 29 damage in one instance.

games.summary: Zefier wins by a game loss — HenkieTheGoat makes an illegal play after a back-and-forth game

beats.text: Zefier takes three Luxom cards off a Glimpse six. The casters say HenkieTheGoat's Topsy Decree put Zefier far behind in game 1, so Zefier keeps his influence as high as possible. He has Regal Inquisition and Incapacitate available after boarding.

HenkieTheGoat attacks with a Winbless Lookout and an Aesan Protector, and Assassin's Ripper adds nine, which leaves Zefier only 11 damage from death. Zefier uses Dungeon Guide and Mercenary's Blade to send Sadi back to HenkieTheGoat's hand. HenkieTheGoat goes to Tristan level 1 and plays Topsy Decree again.

Zefier recovers with a Luxem Sight and Lightweaver's Assaults and takes control of the tempo. A judge is called for an illegal play. The casters later confirm HenkieTheGoat receives a game loss, not a match loss, and the match is 1-1.

games.summary: HenkieTheGoat wins — Regal Inquisition battle and Zefier's own Regal makes HenkieTheGoat draw into his answers

beats.text: HenkieTheGoat starts as Tristan with Backup Charger and gets level 1 on turn two. He materializes the Windwalker Boots first, uses Exploit Vulnerability to draw, and has Weighted Accord and an Incapacitate in his hand. Zefier has several Incapacitates but cannot level safely.

HenkieTheGoat goes through Dungeon Guide to Shadowdancer and plays Shadow's Claw. He sends in his allies fast and hits Zefier for damage. Zefier levels up to level three with Backup Charger, but HenkieTheGoat uses Unmake Duality to draw two and the game stays close.

Regal Inquisition wars start: Zefier's Regal takes HenkieTheGoat's Shadowstrikes, and HenkieTheGoat shows back his own Regal. Zefier loses all four of his Lightweaver's Assaults, a Gleaming Cut and a Luxem Sight, and the Resolute Stand. The casters say Regal Inquisition was the win condition for both players.

Zefier has Vanish from Sight, but he lost his threats to the Regal Inquisition. HenkieTheGoat keeps the lead and wins the game. The casters say that even in a good matchup, players need some luck at this stage of an Ascent.

matches.round: Round 13 (Day 2, Round 4 — final Swiss round) — Fire Lorraine Crux Knight against Fire Vanitas "horses and taxes"

players.name: Egg
players.deck: Fire Lorraine, Crux Knight (Clarent, Fluffy Shopkeep, Resolute Stand, Crystallized Destiny, Ghosts of Pendragon, Inert Sword, Sword Saint's Vow, Hone by Fire, Rending Flames, Creative Shock)

players.name: lancelim0210
players.deck: Fire Vanitas "horses and taxes" (Brisk Windtrotter, Extortion Scheme, Unmake Duality, Smoke Bombs, Dream Fairy; a late change from Fire aggro, built to level Vanitas fast)

matches.result: Egg wins 2-0 (game 1 won by Egg before the VOD segment starts, per the casters; game 2 shown in full)

games.summary: Egg wins — Fluffy Shopkeep with Resolute Stand blocks Vanitas's taxes, then Hone by Fire and Rending Flames deal 22

beats.text: lancelim0210 builds toward Vanitas with Brisk Windtrotter, which gives his horses buff counters. He holds a card that stops prevention effects, so Egg's Crystallized Destiny and Resolute Stand cannot stop his attack that turn. The casters say a Lorraine level 1 player must also pay the tax for the sword, so Egg is wary of leveling.

Egg plays Fluffy Shopkeep and uses Resolute Stand to protect it. The Shopkeep intercepts every turn and lancelim0210 cannot attack past it, because Smoke Bombs need a card in memory. Egg shows he is the best at avoiding the tax by taking it slow and playing the sword he needs.

Egg banishes swords with Fluffy Shopkeep and brings out Ghosts of Pendragon and an Inert Sword. lancelim0210 draws Dream Fairy, which removes the Shopkeep, but he now has one card in hand. Egg is rich enough that he no longer materializes anything.

Egg uses Creative Shock to dig and gets exactly two fire cards for Rending Flames. Hone by Fire and Rending Flames deal 22 damage, a large overkill, and lancelim0210 cannot respond. The casters say Vanitas runs out of steam when Intercept and taunt cards stop his taxes.

matches.sourceNote: Cleaned broadcast transcript, Ascent Manila Day 2 VOD, Round 13. The segment starts partway through the match: the casters say Egg already won game 1, and only game 2 is shown. matches.round: Top 8 — Quarterfinal (featured match, table 4): Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia against Fire Suzaku Guo Jia

players.name: Abbey
players.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (Singapore; exalted-heavy Normal build with no allies except Royal Oathguard: Lost Providence, Incandescent Reliquary, Ducal Seal, Beseech the Winds, Byakko's Command, Seiryuu's Command, Harness Lightning, Arcane Blast, Innervate Agility)

players.name: DuoDuo
players.deck: Fire Suzaku Guo Jia (Malaysia, higher seed, chooses to go first: Suzaku's Command, Vermilion Decree, Blazing Throw, Intensified Pyre, Impact Hammer, Sword of Seeking, Coiled Fatestone, Fluffy Shopkeep, Resolute Stand, Baby Green Slime, Stifling Trap, Tariff Ring)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters think Abbey brings in Blanche, Sheltering Saint and Nullifying Lantern, which deny fire cards for Kindle and for Suzaku's revival. They also name Tricastles of Lucenia, which stops the fire player's burn plan, but Abbey has only a few Normal cards and no spare influence.

DuoDuo has Fiery Interference, Smoke Out and Restorative Flame in the side. Fiery Interference stops Innervate Agility, Smoke Out removes stealth, and Restorative Flame heals six against a lethal Arcane Blast.

games.summary: DuoDuo wins — Suzaku's Command is unblockable and burn spells finish through Royal Oathguard

beats.text: DuoDuo goes first and levels Guo Jia. Abbey sits on one card and levels to Guo Jia level 1 with a Beseech the Winds start, aiming for 10 quest counters as fast as possible. Lost Providence lets him draw into Seiryuu's Command, and he flips the Seiryuu after the Vermilion Decree gives him two quest counters.

DuoDuo plays Tariff Ring, Intensified Pyre and Baby Green Slime, and Suzaku's Command goes over the Seiryuu because it is unblockable. Abbey has 7 damage counters. Resolute Stand resolves, but Abbey still takes the full 19 and has to rely on effect damage because of the Royal Oathguard intercept.

Suzaku revives with three fire cards banished, but cannot revive twice. Abbey cannot find enough for his Arcane Blast and double Harness Lightning, and he uses Stifling Trap on the Suzaku and tries Innervate Agility. DuoDuo plays Blazing Throw for four and Spark Alight, which is unpreventable, and Intensified Pyre take Abbey to 23 damage, which is lethal.

games.summary: DuoDuo wins — a Fluffy Shopkeep and Tariff Ring buy time, and Restorative Flame beats Abbey's 11-damage Arcane Blast

beats.text: Abbey gets a double command hand with Beseech the Winds and levels fast. Abbey plays Topsy Decree, which forces random discards, but DuoDuo throws two fire cards away, which fuels Suzaku with Coiled Fatestone. Abbey finds a Dungeon Guide only to go to level two. Abbey's hand is full of advanced cards and Byakko's Command that he cannot play yet.

DuoDuo plays Fluffy Shopkeep with Creative Shock and Liminal Guide. The Shopkeep protects him from a Blanche swing and Dream Fairy, Vermilion Decree and Tariff Ring slow Abbey, who has 5 and then 7 quest counters. The casters point to the same Fluffy Shopkeep pattern as in round 13.

Abbey uses Lost Providence to go up to five cards, and has Seiryuu's Command and Byakko's Command, but DuoDuo's Tariff Ring has kept him from using them. He does not find the answers he needs. Abbey flips the Seiryuu and attacks, and generates and empowers an Arcane Blast for 11 damage, which puts DuoDuo one damage counter short of lethal.

DuoDuo uses Restorative Flame to heal six, banishes the fire cards in his graveyard and swings Suzaku in. The Seiryuu is gone and Abbey has no second Arcane Blast. Suzaku's Command, a swing and another swing is the lethal line, and DuoDuo moves into the semifinals.

matches.round: Top 4 — Semifinal 2 (featured match, untimed): Fire Lorraine Crux Knight against Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia

players.name: Egg
players.deck: Fire Lorraine, Crux Knight (spirit-ruler build: Cheshire Cat, Fluffy Shopkeep, Clarent, Sword Saint's Vow, Hone by Fire, Rending Flames, Ghosts of Pendragon, Spirit Blade: Dispersion, Dungeon Guide, Creative Shock, Cremation Ritual, Topsy Decree, Crystallized Destiny)

players.name: Raylam
players.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (winner of Ascent Akihabara: Portentous Tanggu, Beseech the Winds, Lost Providence, Seiryuu's Command, Byakko's Command, Harness Lightning, Arcane Blast, Dungeon Guide, Baby Green Slime, Fairy Whispers, Stifling Trap, Topsy Decree, Fabled Azurite Fatestone, Ducal Seal)

matches.result: Raylam wins 2-1 and reaches back-to-back finals

sideboardNotes.text: The casters note Crystallized Destiny in Egg's side to protect against Seiryuu's Command, and they expect him to keep a Spirit Blade: Dispersion plan. Egg removes a Backup Charger from the material deck in game 3.

games.summary: Raylam wins — Seiryuu's Command and Byakko's Command remove 10 quest counters for exact lethal

beats.text: Raylam has the higher seed and goes first. He opens with Beseech the Winds, Portentous Tanggu, and flips Guo Jia into the Seiryuu in the main phase. Egg is not at Lorraine level one, so the Cheshire Cat deals only three damage.
Egg plays Dungeon Guide, Cheshire Cat and a Fluffy Shopkeep, and takes Raylam to 12 damage counters.

Raylam finds the line: Lost Providence refills his hand to six cards and he uses Clarent's counter math to find exactly 20 damage. He removes 10 quest counters for the Seiryuu's Command, and Byakko's Command adds the rest. The casters call it insane math, and it shows why this combination is so scary.

games.summary: Egg wins — Spirit Blade: Dispersion for eight kills Raylam on the stack before the Seiryuu can swing

beats.text: Egg uses Hone by Fire, Dungeon Guide and Creative Shock to accelerate and plays Cheshire Cat with Sword Saint's Vow. Raylam goes first with Beseech the Winds and Tanggu and levels to Guo Jia level two, losing a Harness Lightning and a Seiryuu's Command to the level-up.

Raylam sees Egg at 28 max life with one damage counter, a Pendragon and a four-attack sword on his board, and a Seiryuu that has 17 damage ready. He decides that Egg cannot deal 12 to his dragon, and he flips the Seiryuu.

Egg plays Ghosts of Pendragon with exactly one card left in hand, and Spirit Blade: Dispersion deals eight damage from nowhere. That puts Raylam at lethal before the Seiryuu can swing. The casters say Raylam would have had lethal next turn with a 32-damage Seiryuu's Command combo.

games.summary: Raylam wins — Egg runs out of answers and scoops to a Seiryuu's Command

beats.text: Raylam uses the same curve for the third time: Beseech the Winds into Tanggu and level one. Egg has the tempo with Cheshire Cat, Sword Saint's Vow and Fluffy Shopkeep as intercept, and levels to Lorraine with Spirit Ruler. Raylam uses Fairy Whispers, Lost Providence and Baby Green Slime to answer the Shopkeep.

Egg burns his Rending Flames with another fire card in the banish pile, and it looks like a mistake from his face. Raylam's Sunblessed Gazelle meets Egg's Cheshire Cat, and Egg uses Hone by Fire and Baby Green Slime tricks. The casters say Egg has to find an answer to the Gazelle or take a lot of damage.

Raylam plays carefully with Ducal Seal and Harness Lightning, then Topsy Decree on Egg, who has three cards in hand. Raylam holds Seiryuu's Command, which can empower for 32 damage. Egg has nothing to stop it, and he scoops to Seiryuu's Command. Raylam goes to back-to-back finals.

matches.round: Grand Finals (featured match, untimed): Wind Tristan, Shadowreaver against Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia

players.name: Mike0615
players.deck: Wind Tristan, Shadowreaver "thief" build (Hong Kong; two Mastermind Schemes, Windwalker Boots, Surveil the Winds, Shadow's Claw, Shadowstrike, Slice and Dice, Heavenly Guide, Dungeon Guide, Sadi, Incandescent Reliquary, Innervate Agility; steals cards with Shadowreaver and levels up and down for free)

players.name: Raylam
players.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (Hong Kong; defending Ascent Akihabara champion: Portentous Tanggu, Lost Providence, Dungeon Guide, Dream Fairy, Harness Lightning, Byakko's Command, Resolute Stand, Incapacitate, Crystallized Destiny, Ensnaring Fumes, Regal Inquisition, Sunblessed Gazelle, Royal Oathguard, Windmill Engineer, Stifling Trap, Baby Green Slime, Spellward Scepter, Ducal Seal)

matches.result: Mike0615 wins 2-1 and is Ascent Manila champion

sideboardNotes.text: The casters expect Raylam to keep his Ensnaring Fumes plan: if the Tristan player has Ensnaring Fumes, Raylam does not flip the dragon, and he uses Regal Inquisition to check for it. They also note that Crystallized Destiny and Incapacitate are the cards that stop the Commands.
After the 40-minute second game the casters say Regal Inquisition changed the matchup, because the first player to cast it sees the whole hand of the other player.

games.summary: Raylam wins — the dragon sticks because Mike0615 never draws Ensnaring Fumes, and the Seiryuu's Commands finish the game

beats.text: Raylam opens with Portentous Tanggu and a materialized Guo Jia through the fate stone, and flips the Seiryuu early. The casters say Tristan is generally favored in this matchup, because Seiryuu is slow and allies swarms can run it down. Mike0615 starts with two Mastermind Schemes in hand.

Mike0615 plays an influence game at level one and two. He does not hit his Dungeon Guide, and Raylam keeps Dream Fairy, Harness Lightning, Byakko's Command and Resolute Stand in his hand. The Seiryuu grows to a 10-attack body with vigor, and Mike0615's allies cannot trade into it.

Mike0615 levels up and down with Heavenly Guide and Shadowreaver to draw cards, and plays double Mastermind Scheme to reach 20 preparation counters. A Shadowstrike would be lethal, and the casters expect it, but Raylam answers with an Incapacitate and Resolute Stand and keeps the taunt on board.

Mike0615 does not draw one of his Ensnaring Fumes, so the dragon stays on the field. Raylam's attacks come in and Mike0615 goes down. The casters say sometimes the dragon simply cannot be removed. Raylam is one game from back-to-back titles.

games.summary: Mike0615 wins — a 40-minute grind where Regal Inquisition and Mike0615's army of shadows outlast Raylam

beats.text: Mike0615 starts with a Dungeon Guide and Heavenly Guide hand, and the casters explain that Heavenly Guide only works when the top of the lineage was reached with Dungeon Guide. Raylam answers with Dream Fairy, which locks away an ally, and he levels up with the fate stone.

Raylam finds a triple Surveil the Winds before recollection and quests quickly. He forgets his Lost Providence for one turn, which the casters note as a normal mistake at this level, and the fate stone and Incandescent Reliquary keep his hand full. Mike0615 has no Mastermind Scheme and no Windwalker Boots flip, so his preparation counters stay low.

Regal Inquisition goes off first for Mike0615, which shows him Raylam's whole hand. The dragon dies to the Slice and Dice and the shadows without any Ensnaring Fumes. Raylam answers with a huge Sunblessed Gazelle and Royal Oathguard, and the Spellward Scepter blocks Mike0615's plan until the Windwalker Boots are popped.

Mike0615 builds an army of shadows on the board. The casters cannot count them all and say they have never seen so many at once. His Shadow's Claw makes each shadow swing for two, and Innervate Agility lets him keep drawing. Raylam keeps Resolute Stand and Crystallized Destiny and survives for many turns.

After about 40 minutes Mike0615 swings his panda into the army of allies, and Raylam packs up when Baby Green Slime shows the final card. The casters say Regal Inquisition made the difference: the first player to cast it sees the whole hand. The match goes to game 3.

games.summary: Mike0615 wins — he finds the right line and Raylam does not use his Spellward Scepter in time

beats.text: Raylam opens with a Windmill Engineer and a Stifling Trap. Mike0615 has a hand that includes Incapacitate, Slice and Dice and Mastermind Scheme, and the casters watch Raylam's face as he reads the hand. Mike0615 remembers his Lost Providence this time.

Mike0615 is slow to find a Mastermind Scheme and has only four preparation counters. A judge looks at a missed draw, and the game state is accepted. Raylam's Gazelle grows too large and blocks Mike0615's face attacks, and Raylam holds up the Commands.

Mike0615 levels up and down with Shadowreaver and Shadowdancer to draw cards and builds more shadows. Raylam throws away cards he cannot use and keeps filtering. Mike0615 reaches the damage he needs with a Shadowstrike plan and the shadows.

Raylam does not use his Spellward Scepter in time to stop the final attack, and Mike0615 wins the game and the Ascent Manila title. Mike0615 receives the Gauntlet slot and the first place Kaz spirit, and the casters praise his creative Heavenly Guide and Shadowreaver lines.

matches.round: Championship Sunday — Semifinal 1: Wind Luxom Zander against Wind Krux Lorraine

players.name: Jett
players.deck: Wind Luxom Zander (TM32 build; Lightweaver's Assault x3, Luxem Sight, Gleaming Cut, Heavenly Guide, Dungeon Guide, Poisoned Dagger, Assassin's Ripper, Slice and Dice, Sadi, Veiling Breeze, Nullifying Mirror, Incapacitate, Ensnaring Fumes, Fairy Whispers, Benediction Angel, Candlelight Hourglass)

players.name: TheRainGoddess
players.deck: Wind Krux Lorraine (Spirit Blade: Retribution, Spirit Blade: Ascension, Prismatic Edge, Ghosts of Pendragon, Fluffy Shopkeep, Aesan Protector, Dungeon Guide, Imperious Galebind, Verdigris Decree, Lost Providence, Stifling Trap, Clarent, Reimagined)

matches.result: Jett wins 2-1 and reaches the final

sideboardNotes.text: The casters note that TheRainGoddess has Heavenly Guide and another Stifling Trap in the side. They expect him to think about how many free reveals the Luxom player gets.

games.summary: TheRainGoddess wins — Spirit Blade: Retribution with swords and Dungeon Guides in banishment deals exactly 10

beats.text: TheRainGoddess starts with Dungeon Guide stacked on Fluffy Shopkeep and gets Prismatic Edge onto the board through Spirit Blade: Ascension. Jett has a Stifling Trap to play around and keeps Veiling Breeze for an early save.

Jett puts a Windmill Engineer on board and takes one damage, and TheRainGoddess answers with a reclaim. Imperious Galebind takes Jett's cards, and a Prismatic Edge reveal shows Spirit Blade: Retribution in memory, so the casters warn about big damage next turn.

TheRainGoddess powers Spirit Blade: Retribution with Dungeon Guides and swords he banishes, which makes at least seven damage and up to ten. Jett has no Luxom card to play and no answer, and 10 damage is exactly lethal. TheRainGoddess takes game one.

games.summary: Jett wins — he opens with Luxem Sights and Lightweaver's Assaults and the Retribution race ends one card short

beats.text: Jett has the opening hand he wants: a Windmill Engineer, two Luxem Sights and two Lightweaver's Assaults. He cannot play Fluffy Shopkeep and Windmill Engineer together but he is the first to the board, and TheRainGoddess plays Fairy Whispers and the Verdigris Decree.

TheRainGoddess plays Fluffy Shopkeep for the third time and levels Lorraine, Blademaster to two. Neither player draws a Heavenly Guide or Dungeon Guide, the Ghosts of Pendragon cost four to play through Stifling Trap, and TheRainGoddess counts 11 cards in the banishment for a 14-damage Retribution.

Jett keeps the Veiling Breeze for exactly this moment and has a Nullifying Mirror on board. A third Lightweaver's Assault gives 4 plus 4 damage, which is still short, but TheRainGoddess cannot find the final points. The casters note that the game has been going for an hour and a half and it goes to game three.

games.summary: Jett wins — a very long grind where Veiling Breeze, Nullifying Mirror and Incapacitate hold off Retribution, and Assassin's Ripper with Slice and Dice finishes

beats.text: TheRainGoddess goes first and Jett starts with a Windmill Engineer. Verdigris Decree, Calming Breeze and Spirit Blade: Ascension arrive, and TheRainGoddess levels Lorraine to two. The casters wait for Jett to find his Dungeon Guide and note he has not yet hit Zander level one.

TheRainGoddess reaches a position that is two damage from winning the semifinal, but Jett's reveals show seven wind cards and the Lightweaver's Assault is not lethal. The casters say TheRainGoddess is despondent and worry about a game loss when a judge reviews an Ensnaring Fumes resolution.

Jett plays defensively with Veiling Breeze, Nullifying Mirror and Incapacitate and gets Sadi back with Ensnaring Fumes. TheRainGoddess needs a Spirit Blade: Retribution for twelve, but a Candlelight Hourglass makes it cost more, and Jett has nine cards in hand. The casters say the longer the game goes, the more Zander's Blinding Steel chips away.

Jett swings Sadi, bounces it and swings again, and recovers with a Lightweaver's Assault. TheRainGoddess holds Clarent, Reimagined for prevention, but Jett uses Assassin's Ripper and Slice and Dice for the lethal damage. Jett wins after more than an hour in game three and goes to the final.

matches.round: Championship Sunday — Semifinal 2: Wind Krux Lorraine against Wind Luxom Zander

players.name: Zero0000000000
players.deck: Wind Krux Lorraine (Hong Kong; he switched from his usual Krux elements to Wind to play second; Spirit Blade: Retribution, Ghosts of Pendragon, Prismatic Edge, Aesan Protector, Windmill Engineer, Sadi, Scout the Land, Regal Inquisition — the only copy brought to the quarterfinals or semifinals)

players.name: Lifdrasyl
players.deck: Wind Luxom Zander (TM32; higher seed; Lightweaver's Assault, Luxem Sight, Surveil the Winds, Fairy Whispers, Veiling Breeze, Nullifying Mirror, Incapacitate, Windmill Engineer, Sadi, Serro operative)

matches.result: Zero0000000000 wins 2-0 and reaches the final

games.summary: Zero0000000000 wins — Spirit Blade: Retribution with banished allies deals 15 to a Lifdrasyl who cannot find his Veiling Breeze

beats.text: Lifdrasyl goes first as the higher seed and opens with Fairy Whispers and a Surveil the Winds, which the casters call a great start. Zero0000000000 shows Backup Charger and holds a hedge deck, because TheRainGoddess was expected on Razor Gale and TeamTrueCaban on fractals.

Zero0000000000 plays Aesan Protector with a reclaim and Windmill Engineer, and loses allies to Lifdrasyl's Serro operative but keeps banishing the high-power allies. The casters say Ghosts of Pendragon is the pressure and that Prismatic Edge threatens three damage a turn.

Spirit Blade: Retribution comes for 15 damage with a sword added, compared with seven against TheRainGoddess, because the high-power allies are in banishment. Lifdrasyl has only nine life at Zander level two and needs a Veiling Breeze off a surveil, but he finds a Luxem Sight, and Zero0000000000 takes game one.

games.summary: Zero0000000000 wins — Regal Inquisition reveals the hand and a zero-cost Retribution for 16 beats one Veiling Breeze

beats.text: Zero0000000000 uses Regal Inquisition to remove Lifdrasyl’s Dungeon Guide and Luxem Sight, leaving the Incapacitates. Lifdrasyl draws Turbo Charge and Lightweaver’s Assault, but struggles to reach level three without his Guide.

Lifdrasyl never gets a big influence start. He has Windmill Engineer, Sadi and Incapacitate, and a Veiling Breeze helps him survive one turn by preventing seven, but he sits on three cards while Zero0000000000 recovers influence with Windmill and Sadi bounces.

Zero0000000000 takes Spirit Blade: Retribution from the graveyard at zero cost for 16 damage, and a free one-use Ghosts of Pendragon swings are added on top. Lifdrasyl loses, which ends the last Southeast Asia and North America hope in the final, and Zero0000000000 meets Jett. The casters call Zero0000000000 the player with a 0 percent win rate against everyone in Hong Kong.

matches.round: Championship Sunday — Grand Finals (best of 5, untimed): Wind Luxom Zander against Wind Krux Lorraine

players.name: Jett
players.deck: Wind Luxom Zander (TM32; Lightweaver's Assault, Luxem Sight, Gleaming Cut, Turbo Charge x3, Heavenly Guide, Dungeon Guide, Poisoned Dagger, Assassin's Ripper, Slice and Dice, Sadi, Veiling Breeze, Nullifying Mirror, Incapacitate, Purifying Thurible, Benediction Angel, Fairy Whispers, Lost Providence)

players.name: Zero0000000000
players.deck: Wind Krux Lorraine (Hong Kong; Spirit Blade: Retribution, Spirit Blade: Ascension, Prismatic Edge, Ghosts of Pendragon, Aesan Protector, Windmill Engineer, Scout the Land, Dungeon Guide, Imperious Galebind, Verdigris Decree, Regal Inquisition, Clarent, Reimagined)

matches.result: Jett wins 3-2 and is the 2026 Grand Archive World Champion

sideboardNotes.text: The casters see Zero0000000000 swap one card from his sideboard before shuffling for game three. They guess it is a response to the Stifling Trap from the last game.

games.summary: Zero0000000000 wins — Jett goes first and clears the board with Lightweaver's Assault, but Prismatic Edge and Spirit Blade: Ascension take his cards

beats.text: Jett goes first and plays Fairy Whispers twice, which the casters link to his teammate Lifdrasyl's loss. He feels safe on Spirit and materializes value regalia, and keeps Purifying Thurible to remove Zero0000000000's floating memory. Zero0000000000 rests Fluffy Shopkeep so it cannot retaliate, and Jett returns Sadi.

Zero0000000000 plays the first Spirit Blade: Ascension of the match and Prismatic Edge enters. It reveals memory and takes Jett's Gleaming Cuts and a Luxem Sight. Zero0000000000 then uses Dungeon Guide to level to three, and Jett's Veiling Breezes are dead because he has no wind cards in hand.
Jett plays a Lightweaver's Assault early to clear the board, but it is not enough. Zero0000000000 takes game one. In the interview Jett says the first game was a struggle.

games.summary: Jett wins — Turbo Charge off the top and a Slice and Dice swing tie the final at 1-1

beats.text: Jett goes first in game two. Turbo Charge comes off the top, which the casters call an unbelievable draw, and he plays three Turbo Charges in the deck. Zero0000000000 reveals Scout the Land to dig for more and holds back Ghosts of Pendragon.

Jett fires an early Incapacitate, and the casters note he can pick it up again later. A Dungeon Guide takes out his Windmill Engineer and Zero0000000000 is hands down, so Jett rockets to level three with a Luxem Sight, Blinding Steel and Lost Providence.
Zero0000000000 plays Aesan Protector for an Ayella trigger and needs to fight for the board. Jett swings with a three-damage ally, then Slice and Dice deals the last damage. Jett ties the match 1-1.

games.summary: Jett wins — a long, tight game where Turbo Charge and Veiling Breeze buy time and a Luxem Sight into Slice and Dice closes it

beats.text: Zero0000000000 goes first and Jett drops Sadi, Blood Harvester for two damage and starts to build preparation counters. Jett uses Turbo Charge early, saying the deck feels better when it rips one off early, and digs with the Purifying Thurible for a Dungeon Guide.

Zero0000000000 finds only a guide card, not an army of ghosts or a Spirit Blade, and has to push damage. Jett buys another turn easily with Veiling Breeze, and two Clarent activations raise the pressure on his side. The casters note that the grand finals are untimed.
Jett reveals many wind cards, recovers three with Luxem Sights and puts eight cards down. A Slice and Dice shows up, and Jett steals the game. He is up 2-1.

games.summary: Zero0000000000 wins — a zero-cost Spirit Blade: Retribution ultimate attack forces a fifth game

beats.text: Zero0000000000 goes first and plays Turbo Charge to build influence and level fast. Jett needs to win one game to become champion and plays more aggressively, going to Zander with a prepared Scout. The casters say this will be an absolute banger.

Zero0000000000 goes zero to sixty with the dungeon guide displace line and passes priority to Jett. Jett's Calming Breeze prevents the damage from the Dungeon Guide's attack, but Zero0000000000 now knows what Jett has. Jett gets an Incapacitate back with a small hand.

Zero0000000000 uses Spirit Blade: Retribution, the Lorraine ultimate, to win. The commentators say Zero0000000000 uses the same line that beat Lifdrasyl, and Krux is fine. The final goes to a fifth game.

games.summary: Jett wins — Lightweaver's Assault and Gleaming Cut fuel the final push; Assassin's Ripper, Windmill Engineer and Aesan Protector close the match

beats.text: Zero0000000000 drops a Windmill Engineer on the first turn for early damage, as Jett did in game three. Jett answers with Aesan Protector, which returns the Benediction Angel, and a train of value. A Surveil the Winds miss is a devastating moment for Zero0000000000.

Jett levels to Zander one to turn on his class bonuses, pops the Poisoned Dagger and swings with everything through a possible Veiling Breeze. He keeps the Heavenly Guide to wait for Zero0000000000's Dungeon Guide. Zero0000000000 stays alive and brings back the Drawn Blade with Lorraine, and a Verdigris Decree comes down.

Zero0000000000 rebuilds influence with Ghosts of Pendragon and plays Regal Inquisition. Jett responds with Lightweaver's Assault, revealing two Gleaming Cuts to draw four cards and dealing eight damage despite Clarent. Jett then swings with Assassin's Ripper for three, taking Zero0000000000 to 23 damage. Windmill Engineer and Aesan Protector provide the last five damage, making Jett the 2026 world champion.

matches.round: Round 10 (Day 2, Round 1) — Alice/Merlin Spectre against Water Aetherwing Diana

players.name: Novephilion
players.deck: Alice, Distorted Queen into Merlin, Kingslayer (Spectre package: Merlin, Memory Thief, Mantle of the Abyss, four Unyielding Wraithguard, four Imperial Countermeasure, Fireball, Ghosts of Pendragon)

players.name: Noel
players.deck: Water Aetherwing Diana (Cheshire Cat, Krustallan Archer, Frostsworn Paladin, Ranger Strides, Diana, Haunt Reminiscence, Aquamirage Whisper)

sideboardNotes.text: Noel brings in Aetheric Reforging to answer the floating memory Nov feeds the graveyard. The casters also float Dissuading Aether, since Nov retaliates with taunters.

Nov has Crystallized Destiny in the sideboard for the big Diana attack, and the casters raise Lavastorm as an option against the ally board. Nov says in the interview that Feast of the Forgotten is also in his side, for slow water decks.

games.summary: Nov wins — Lineage Release and Imperial Countermeasure stop a 15-damage Diana swing, then a double Fireball

beats.text: Noel wins the roll and goes first. Diana, Haunt Reminiscence and Inert Sword build the board, Nov's Undying Dreams brings back an Unyielding Wraithguard to keep a taunter in the way, and Nov debuts Alice, Distorted Queen on stream. Noel's glimpse for four mills a floating memory.

Nov plays Merlin, Memory Thief to eat Noel's floating memory and levels into Dungeon Guide for Merlin, Kingslayer. Ghosts of Pendragon is negated by an imbued Cerulean Decree, and Noel does not take the 17-damage line because Nov would be low on influence.

Nov holds the line with Tariff Ring, Quickstep Treads and Unyielding Wraithguard. A turn of Ghosts of Pendragon (the second copy resolves), Sword of Seeking on the Cheshire Cat and two more bodies draws six cards, with Fireball among them.

Noel goes all in: two Cheshire Cats sacrificed for ranged, Boots and Ranger Strides put Diana at ranged 13 for a 15-damage swing. Imperial Countermeasure prevents four, Quickstep Treads taxes the response, and Alice's Lineage Release recovers two. Nov is left at 25 damage, three short.
Nov punishes the all-in with a double Fireball for exact lethal. The casters say Noel had the math but forgot about the Lineage Release.

games.summary: Noel wins — patient glimpses, then a double Cheshire Cat swing with Inert Sword

beats.text: Noel goes first with two Frostsworn Paladins, Krustallan Archer and Cheshire Cat in hand. Inert Sword on the Cat swings for three early, but Noel has no Aether Charges to load the Whisper.

Nov plays Evercurrent Raider on the level up, Alice, Distorted Queen, and a Dungeon Guide. Merlin, Memory Thief eats every floating memory Noel puts in the graveyard, so Noel must pay two cards for each one. Nov's hand is stacked with Ghosts of Pendragon and Fireball, but he must reach Kingslayer first.

Noel glimpses with Undercurrent Vantage and Aetheric Calibration for Charge the Soul, Frostbind and a second Cat. A weak Merlin card means Nov has to take a draw turn off, while Noel sets up Ranger Strides and a double Cat swing. Noel stops a lethal check one card short and passes with Frostbind up.
Nov levels to Merlin, Kingslayer through a hard three-card level. Noel keeps Frostbind for the Ghosts of Pendragon, so Nov holds his cards and uses Fireball defensively on the Paladin.

With Quickstep Treads taxing Nov's responses, Noel swings Cheshire Cat and Frostsworn Paladin to 24, sacrifices a Cat for ranged, plays the second Cat, and Diana swings with Inert Sword for lethal. The match is 1-1.

games.summary: Nov wins — Mantle of the Abyss, Wraithguard and Ghosts of Pendragon, then Fireball

beats.text: Nov goes first with a dream hand: Creative Shock, Crystallized Destiny, Imperial Countermeasure and Dungeon Guide. Noel's Aetheric Reforging banishes the floating memory, and the level up costs Nov a Crystallized Destiny. Mantle of the Abyss lets Nov sacrifice a Spectre ally and banish it for influence.

Noel plays Krustallan Archer off a floating memory and Aetheric Calibration to find a Backup Charger, but Merlin, Memory Thief keeps Diana's graveyard empty. Noel burns cards and Backup Charger and Tactical Retreat with no pressure to show for it.

Dungeon Guide levels Nov to Kingslayer. Ghosts of Pendragon is not Frostbound, returns The Looking Glass and kills the Archer. Nov's Tariff Ring is popped and Noel's Backup Charger becomes a power cell token, but neither stops the board. A second Ghosts of Pendragon and an Unyielding Wraithguard make two taunters.

Noel cannot find the line through two Wraithguards. Charge the Soul on a Wraithguard, Cat, Archer and Diana would be enough, but the hand lacks one card. Noel uses a second Archer to remove one Ghosts of Pendragon and passes hoping for no Fireball.
Nov draws the extra Kingslayer card, deals 11 with Dungeon Guide, three with Ghosts of Pendragon and 17 with Merlin, and Fireball ends the game. Nov moves to 8-1-1.

matches.round: Round 11 (Day 2, Round 2) — Fire Tristan combo against Alice/Merlin, a rematch of the Round 10 winner

players.name: Matt
players.deck: Fire Tristan "Erupting" combo (Direquium into Volcanic Crescendo into Fireball, Agility 3 from Tristan, Incapacitate, Crystallized Destiny, Torching Reach, Increasing Danger)

players.name: Novephilion
players.deck: Alice, Distorted Queen into Merlin, Kingslayer (Spectre package: Unyielding Wraithguard, Mantle of the Abyss, Imperial Countermeasure, Palvor Sword, Nullifying Lantern)

sideboardNotes.text: Nov brings in Nullifying Lantern (Matt banishes fire cards for the combo) and two Crystallized Destiny for protection. The casters also float Regal Inquisition.

Matt has Discordia, Harp of Malice (plus level for Fireball, minus level on the opponent so Blanche cannot be fast-activated), Spurn to Ash and extra answers for the Lantern and Palvor Sword. The casters expect more of his draw package to stay in.

games.summary: Matt wins — Direquium, Volcanic Crescendo and Fireball for over 20 in one turn

beats.text: Matt opens with a double Increasing Danger and Return to the Archive (a turbo start that gives Nov a pile of cards too). Fire resonance bobbles, Hasty Messenger and Creative Shock fill his graveyard, with Ignis Deus held to level at fast speed in case Merlin tries to take the float.

Nov plays Three of Hearts, takes Evercurrent Raider to level Alice, Distorted Queen, and sacrifices Unyielding Wraithguard to put Mantle of the Abyss out for an ephemeral taunter. Both players hold a full hand because of Increasing Danger.

Matt pays the floating memory for Blinding Orb, then Ignis Deus levels Tristan for Agility 3, so he can hold Incapacitate and still cast Fireball. Backstep makes Torching Reach a Creative Shock, and Direquium's direwolf clears the Wraithguard.

Matt plays Volcanic Crescendo, harmonized, banishing eight fire cards for eight damage to each champion and an 11-point empower. Fireball follows. Nov's Crystallized Destiny is not enough and Matt pays two to get past a null spell for lethal, more than 20 damage in one turn.

games.summary: Matt wins — Ignis Deus blows out a Sudden Steel, then Volcanic Crescendo through the Lantern

beats.text: Matt starts with a draw-heavy hand: Creative Shock pitches a Liminal Guide, Cremation Ritual, Hasty Messenger and bobbles, and Backstep enables Torching Reach. He has the Fireball and melody in hand within two turns.

Nov finds Dungeon Guide and puts Palvor Sword on the board to banish Matt's graveyard face down, pairing it with Mantle of the Abyss and Rile the Abyss. Then Nullifying Lantern lands, so Matt has both a Sword and a Lantern to remove.

Nov goes for lethal at level one with Sudden Steel and Palvor Sword swings. Matt answers with Ignis Deus, which banishes the float, takes Tristan for four extra life and Agility 3, draws two from Liminal Guides, and makes the attack not lethal. Nov is hands down and has no interaction left.

Matt finds Spurn to Ash for the Sword and a second copy for the Lantern, then Discordia, Harp of Malice for a plus level. A Volcanic Crescendo (not harmonized) banishes the whole graveyard for a single huge Fireball. Matt moves to 10-1 and locks a top 8 seat.

players.deck: Fire Spirit CL Oblation Omen (Baleful Oblation, nine 15-cost omen cards including Golden Checkmate, Manxome Armoire, Lost Providence, Feu Awakening, no Serene Spirit)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters expect DuckHats to add Innervate Agility (spell shroud against CL's spell trigger), Stifling Gyre against Dungeon Guide, Obscured Offering to protect the Orb of Sealing and Crystallized Destiny.
Bocol123 has Nocturne's Oblivion, Expel the Departed and Blanche as options for the Orb of Sealing, Essence Crucible and Razorgale Calling. Expel the Departed and Blanche both appear in game 2.

games.summary: DuckHats wins — Orb of Sealing blanks every Oblation, a double Razorgale Calling forces Bocol123 to fire

beats.text: Bandit, Gaze Leader misses on its six-card look, so DuckHats has no second raccoon. Bocol123 sets up two Baleful Oblations with Angelic Channeling and levels into CL. DuckHats plays Orb of Sealing from the start, a main-deck answer that flips the Omen face down whenever Bocol123 tries to fire.

Bocol123 omens Golden Checkmate and a second 15-cost card, but every omen is face down while the Orb is active, so each Oblation would deal zero. Manxome Armoire and Lost Providence give Bocol123 buttons to swap a face-up card in, and a Golden Checkmate in the graveyard is bait for the Bandit.

DuckHats brings out Essence Crucible early (Bocol123 has no main-deck way to remove it) and then Arisanna. Aesan Protector hits for three each turn and two Distilled Waters put two counters on the Crucible, but DuckHats cannot find a Razorgale Calling with Cyclical Breeze and Fairy Whispers and has to hold up interaction.

Bocol123 holds two Baleful Oblations and Umbra Sight. Topsy Decree, imbued, gives him spell shroud for the turn, so Razorgale Calling can only hit DuckHats. Devouring Malice is answered by Skirting Step, and Chalice of Blood draws more cards.

Bocol123 sits at 21 damage with Razorgale Calling in play, so any wind card is lethal. Oblation, Manxome Armoire for two unpreventable, and the Orb flip chain back and forth. DuckHats keeps seven influence open and Veiling Breeze answers the last Oblation. Bocol123 is one short.

games.summary: DuckHats wins — a 20-plus influence Crucible, and three Veiling Breezes survive the all-in

beats.text: Bocol123 takes the first turn and passes, and DuckHats digs with Fairy Whispers but has no Razorgale. Another Bandit, Gaze Leader misses, and Bocol123 draws only clunky fire cards and a non-imbued Angel Attendant.

Windmill Engineer, Reclaim and Backup Charger give DuckHats a huge hand. Stifling Gyre names Dungeon Guide, so Bocol123 has to level on his own cards. Bocol123's Expel the Departed removes Razorgale Calling and Cyclical Breeze brings it back.

Angelic Channeling loses the Blanche to the banishment. Cremation Ritual on the Liminal Guide draws three. Bocol123 reaches level three and puts his own Orb of Sealing out to flip the cheap omens face down and swap the Golden Checkmate back in with Manxome Armoire.

DuckHats builds the Crucible to three counters, so every wind card is four damage, and stays patient. Chalice of Blood fires at 20 damage and Bocol123 draws two. Bocol123's all-in sequence uses Manxome Armoire, Baleful Oblation and Topsy Decree for spell shroud, but the Orb flips the Checkmate again and three Veiling Breezes answer it. DuckHats moves on.

matches.round: Round 13 (Day 2, Round 4 — final Swiss round) — Fire Oblation CL against Fire Suzaku Guo Jia, a win-and-in for Top 8

players.name: 1wisp
players.deck: Fire Spirit CL Oblation Omen (Baleful Oblation, Golden Checkmate, Manxome Armoire, Feu Awakening, Lost Providence, Resolute Stand, Library Witch, Cremation Ritual, no Orb of Sealing)

players.name: Mechsniper
players.deck: Fire Suzaku Guo Jia (Avatar of Suzaku, Fabled Ruby Fatestone, Peppered Chef, Impact Hammer, Vermilion Decree, Blazing Throw, Three of Hearts, Liminal Guide value build)

sideboardNotes.text: Mechsniper brings in Infernal Vessel (healing to turn off Wisp's damage trigger), Crystallized Destiny against the Oblation combo, Nullifying Lantern to stop Suzaku returning, Resolute Stand and perhaps Shatter the Brittle.
Wisp has Blanche, Sheltering Saint in the side, but the casters say it cannot stop the Fatestone's quest counter. Wisp's Resolute Stand is already in the main deck.

games.summary: Wisp wins — a defensive Feu Awakening chain machine-guns Mechsniper out

beats.text: Wisp goes first and levels into CL with Library Witch as an interceptor. Cremation Ritual and Creative Shock dig for a 15-cost card, and a Dungeon Guide takes CL to level three through a quiz and Lost Providence.

Mechsniper plays Vermilion Decree for quest counters, Fiery Interference on the Dungeon Guide and Enfeebling Orb, reaches six quest counters, and flips Suzaku, the Vermilion Phoenix. Mechsniper hurts himself with Fabled Ruby Fatestone, which puts Wisp's Oblation in range at four damage.

Wisp plays Tariff Ring, but Mechsniper pops it and attacks with Impact Hammer, Suzaku and a Peppered Chef that sacrifices Suzaku and returns it ready, getting to 13 damage on Wisp. Blazing Throw sits in hand to finish.

Wisp has only about four total influence, so he discards his whole hand to Feu Awakening, which makes two omens that kill the Peppered Chef. Manxome Armoire then swaps Feu Awakening back so each omen shoots again. The chain deals the last damage and ends the game.

games.summary: Mechsniper wins — Avatar of Suzaku start, Wisp's Feu Awakening line is one damage short

beats.text: Mechsniper plays Avatar of Suzaku on turn one, Fabled Ruby Fatestone and Searing Strike for two quest counters, and reaches five quest counters while Wisp tries to level. Wisp uses Angelic Channeling, banishing two Golden Checkmates, and holds two Dungeon Guides.

Impact Hammer and Sparklight add unpreventable damage and Suzaku attacks for four. Wisp uses Resolute Stand to level to CL, but Infernal Vessel is on the board, which makes Baleful Oblation a dead card. Wisp reaches level three with Dungeon Guide and Grand Crusader's Ring.

Wisp plays Manxome Armoire and a second Resolute Stand to survive, then a Feu Awakening double line with Lost Providence to bring the Armoire back. Mechsniper plays around a possible Feu Awakening by discarding Restorative Flame, and Wisp is one damage short of lethal.

With Wisp hands down and out of influence, Mechsniper swings with Suzaku and Impact Hammer. The Chalice of Blood is Wisp's only source of cards, and Enfeebling Orb sends them back. A final turn is enough to finish Wisp, and the match is 1-1.

games.summary: Mechsniper wins — Fiery Interference stops an Abnegation, then Avatar of Suzaku flips the Phoenix

beats.text: Wisp goes first with Cremation Ritual, Creative Shock and Resolute Stand in a keepable hand. A Liminal Guide level up and Cremation Ritual for value show Wisp is playing a low-influence game, with Wisp one level up while Mechsniper plays Three of Hearts and Fabled Ruby Fatestone.

Wisp levels to CL level three with Dungeon Guide and omens Advent of the Stormcaller, putting Baleful Oblation in the 15-damage range. Wisp holds Resolute Stand and Abnegation. Mechsniper holds only reactive cards, two Vermilion Decrees and Ember Crypt Burn.

Mechsniper commits: Impact Hammer, Avatar of Suzaku, Liminal Guide and Three of Hearts attack for 20, putting Wisp at 20 damage while Mechsniper falls to 11. Wisp holds back Resolute Stand to bait the all-in.

Blazing Throw goes to Wisp's face, Wisp responds with Abnegation and Mechsniper answers with Fiery Interference, taking Wisp to 24 and then 28. The last two cards activate Avatar of Suzaku for the final quest counters, Suzaku flips and ends the game. Mechsniper wins 2-1 and locks Top 8.

matches.round: Round 9 (Day 2, Round 1) — Fire Krux Lorraine against Wind Tristan

players.name: TeamTrueIsaac
players.deck: Fire Krux Lorraine (a 5-2-1 record entering the round; Clarent, Prismatic Edge, Ghosts of Pendragon, Flame Sweep, Devastating Blow, Staggering Strike, Sword of Seeking, Creative Shock, Hasty Messenger, Three of Hearts, Resolute Stand, Regal Inquisition)

players.name: Tress
players.deck: Wind Tristan, Shadowreaver (Slice and Dice, Mastermind Scheme, Shadow's Claw, Sadi, Veiling Breeze, Ensnaring Fumes, Nullifying Lantern; a Spirit of Wind plan with prep counters and shadows)

sideboardNotes.text: TeamTrueIsaac has a lot of sideboard cards: one extra of every dig card for whatever he wants to fix in the matchup. The casters say Penumbra Waltz is less useful for him if he does not plan to put swords in the banishment, and he brings in Staggering Strike for the Tristan player.

games.summary: Tress wins — shadows and Slice and Dice deal 15 and TeamTrueIsaac concedes

beats.text: TeamTrueIsaac uses Creative Shock to put a Liminal Guide in the graveyard, goes up to Lorraine level one and brings out Ghosts of Pendragon. He plays Clarent and banishes extra cards for attack power on the Krux Knight, and he returns Sadi before dropping his allies.
Tress builds prep counters and shadows. The casters say he loses some allies to Sadi, and he does not try to stop the attacks going to the face. His hand has Veiling Breeze and a normal card.
TeamTrueIsaac draws Flame Sweep off the Hasty Messenger trigger. Tress attacks for six and then nine for 15 total damage, and TeamTrueIsaac extends his fist to concede and move to game two.

games.summary: TeamTrueIsaac wins — the Sensor slows Tress and a Resolute Stand holds the line before the swing for lethal

beats.text: TeamTrueIsaac keeps a Resolute Stand in his hand and has plenty of floating memory, but a Sensor stops his Reduce to Ash for a while. He drops a Stalwart Shieldmate and leaves it up, feeling unthreatened with only one damage on him.

Tress has four damage on board, and 15 with Slice and Dice. The casters call this a shields-down moment. He has Shadow's Claw and Shadow Reaver out and is greedy, and a Resolute Stand holds him to 12 damage, which leaves Tristan, Shadowreaver more than dead.
TeamTrueIsaac counters with Ghosts of Pendragon and Regal Inquisition effects that take Tress's hand. Tress is out of gas and the match goes to game three.

games.summary: TeamTrueIsaac wins — Devastating Blow with Sword of Seeking's true sight is lethal because Spirit of Wind has too little life

beats.text: TeamTrueIsaac starts with two Dungeon Guides and a Liminal Guide in his opening hand, ready to level up quickly. A Tera Ring is used on the level up, and the Sensor on board means his own Reduce to Ash also loses the floating memory.

Tress has to find a way to kill TeamTrueIsaac first and pushes in all his damage. He has to banish from hand and loses a Slice and Dice. He thinks about the Nullifying Lantern and an Ensnaring Fumes that could have saved the board.

Devastating Blow, with true sight from the Sword of Seeking, deals lethal damage and Spirit of Wind does not have enough life. A Zephyr would have cancelled the attack, but Tress does not have one. TeamTrueIsaac wins the match 2-1 and keeps his top 8 hopes alive.

matches.round: Round 10 (Day 2, Round 2): arcane Advent deck against Ciel Heavy Swing

players.name: Hyouka
players.deck: Arcane Advent deck (Advent of the Stormcaller, Summon Gale, Disorienting Winds, Arcane Elemental, Mnemonic Charm, Quicksilver Grail, Fluffy Shopkeep; a well-oiled machine whose sideboard the casters have seen many times)

players.name: TeppeSlorn
players.deck: Ciel allies (Heavy Swing, Liminal Guide, Fluffy Shopkeep, Tariff Ring, Dungeon Guide, Resolute Stand, Regal Inquisition, Scry the Skies, Flame Sorcery; first Ascent, playing a new Ciel build)

matches.result: Draw — one game win each plus a timed-out game 3

sideboardNotes.text: The casters expect TeppeSlorn to be more careful after seeing the Advent plan, with extra negates and a Regal Inquisition to take Hyouka's arcane cards.

Both players know the other's list. The casters discuss whether Hyouka will keep making the same plan or slow down, because he was punished in the previous game for banishing his arcane cards to level up.

games.summary: Hyouka wins — Advent of the Stormcaller with a full arcane banishment

beats.text: TeppeSlorn gets the Ciel level one Liminal Guide back as an ephemeral, then follows with Heavy Swing for seven damage in a turn. He swaps a card from hand with a card in his omens, which the casters say is normally a level three trick.

Hyouka tries to get as many arcane cards as possible into the banishment and goes in with Dungeon Guide. The casters like his Fluffy Shopkeep play and his all-purpose negate with no conditions, and he banishes a Quicksilver Grail to use the Tome of Knowledge.
Hyouka reaches level 15, which is enough for a second Advent of the Stormcaller, with another Advent in hand. The casters say that plan ends the game, and game one goes to Hyouka.

games.summary: TeppeSlorn wins — he fights through the negates and Dungeon Guides, and Hyouka misses a Heavy Swing answer

beats.text: TeppeSlorn plays more carefully, having seen the Advent plan. His Dungeon Guide is negated in game one, but he powers out the Dungeon Guides this time. A Tariff Ring is on the board and he plays the Scry the Skies as a negate.
Hyouka banishes the Demonic Charm, which is a massive risk with a full grip. He has two big islands in hand and is ready to negate again. He banishes a Tariff Ring and does not want to be attacked.

Hyouka misses the Heavy Swing, which was top-decked, and the arcane spell shield would have been insane for him. The casters say the game lined up exactly the way TeppeSlorn wanted. TeppeSlorn takes game two.

games.summary: Draw — time runs out while Hyouka tries to assemble the combo turn

beats.text: TeppeSlorn follows the same plan as the previous game. The casters expect a Fluffy Shopkeep up for defense, and they say a Dungeon Guide at level two would be needed to keep Hyouka from his Advent plan. Hyouka plays a slower approach and has his cards negated.

Hyouka has three arcane cards in banishment and has the Mnemonic Charm out. The casters count 11 or 12 from the arcane side and wonder if the combo turn is coming. He pays two to swap for the Heavy Swing, and the Resolute Stand prevents another three, which is not enough.
Hyouka has less than two minutes to finish his game and is stretching to do it properly. The turn limit arrives and the match ends as a draw.

matches.round: Round 11 (Day 2, Round 3): fire Merlin mirror

players.name: Perfy
players.deck: Fire Merlin, Prismatic Edge (Majestic Spirit x4, Incarnate Majesty, Ghosts of Pendragon, Spirit Blade: Ascension, Fireball, Crystallized Destiny, Creative Shock, Undying Dreams, Drawn Blade, Cheshire Cat, Inert Sword, Stalwart Shieldmate, Resolute Stand)

players.name: Guruthos
players.deck: Fire Merlin, Prismatic Edge (a mirror build with Majestic Spirit, Incarnate Majesty, Ghosts of Pendragon, Spirit Blade: Ascension, Fireball, Undying Dreams, Drawn Blade, Crystallized Destiny, Nullifying Lantern in the side)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters list sideboard cards for the Merlin mirror: regalia for some matchups, and Nullifying Lantern, which has some use in the mirror. They also explain why players run four Majestic Spirit copies: the spirits protect each other from the same prevention effects.

games.summary: Guruthos wins — he gets a slight damage lead and uses Spirit Blade: Ascension and the Drawn Blade free through Undying Dreams

beats.text: Perfy plays Swift Recruit and reclaim, and both players hold a Majestic Spirit and an Incarnate Majesty. Guruthos banishes Undying Dreams and is lucky with his draws. The casters note that Majestic Spirit is a prevention effect that players must play around.

Guruthos is slightly up on damage, seven dealt against six, and takes the Drawn Blade for free with Undying Dreams, which is very impactful. He has the Spirit Blade: Ascension as well, and the memory of Perfy is revealed. Perfy loses a Resolute Stand and a Stalwart Shieldmate.
Guruthos has two Fireballs in hand and pops the Crystallized Destiny line. The casters say the game went clearly to one player once he hit level three. Guruthos wins game one.

games.summary: Perfy wins — a Cheshire Cat with the Inert Sword and a Merlin level two put Guruthos on the back foot

beats.text: Perfy plays a Cheshire Cat with an Inert Sword, which takes care of the Three of Hearts alone. The casters say Guruthos is on the back foot, unlike in game one, and a level two Merlin banishes a non-floating Flame Rune Swordsman.

Guruthos has two floating memory cards that should have gone away anyway. Perfy keeps a Fireball and has dealt 10 damage, and has a way to find lethal. Guruthos has the Crystallized Destiny, but the Inert Sword gets through even if he reaches level three.
Perfy finishes game two. The casters say that both games went clearly to one person or the other once the level three point was hit, and there is nothing Guruthos can do at that point.

games.summary: Perfy wins — Ghosts of Pendragon decide the matchup and Guruthos is left on two life when Perfy's Fireballs and Sudden Steel arrive

beats.text: The casters say Perfy had the Ghosts of Pendragon and that decided the matchup. Perfy levels up quickly with level counters and ascension value, and a Creative Shock is the only fire card in the back of his hand.

Guruthos plays Blanche, a very bold play. He is forced to lose a card and an influence for the level up because the Merlin level two locks out the floating memory option. Perfy cannot draw off the on-enter of the Prismatic Edge because Guruthos has no cards in hand.

Perfy's Fireballs add up to 16 damage, which is not quite enough, but a Sudden Steel is still in hand. The casters say Guruthos is left on about two life in the best case and in a precarious position. Perfy wins 2-1 and is close to a guaranteed top 8 spot.

matches.round: Round 12 (Day 2, Round 4 — final Swiss round): Wind Tristan against Astra Arisana

players.name: Asuna
players.deck: Wind Tristan (Windmill Engineer, Sadi, Slice and Dice, Shadowstrike, Mastermind Scheme, Ensnaring Fumes, Incapacitate, Crystallized Destiny, Scout the Land, Turbo Charge, Tempest Downfall and Zephyr in the side)

players.name: AuraBomb
players.deck: Astra Arisana (Cosmic Bolt, Stellaria Shower, Astral Seal, Polaris, Fertile Ground, Lunar Conduit, Wisdom's Reprise, four Three Visits, Penumbra Waltz, one Zephyr, one Innervate Agility, Art of War in the side)

matches.result: Asuna wins the round (game 1 win and a timed-out game 2)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters talk through Asuna's side: Tempest Downfall, which is fast and breaks a spell, and the Zephyr, which does little in this matchup. They say the extra Shadowstrike protects him against Regal Inquisition.

games.summary: Asuna wins — a long, patient game where Incapacitate and negates outlast AuraBomb's Cosmic Bolts

beats.text: AuraBomb plays Fertile Ground and Polaris and keeps four Three Visits, which the casters call unusual. The Arisana level two is a pseudo-Merlin that draws a card every two turns. AuraBomb plays defensively without interacting with Asuna much.

Asuna commits more to the board with Windmill Engineer and Sadi, which is never a real commitment. He does not pop his Polaris yet. A Sadi swing, Slice and Dice, and Ensnaring Fumes follow, and AuraBomb has Incapacitate to find through.

AuraBomb sets up star calls for the Cosmic Bolt, but Asuna has another Incapacitate in his hand. AuraBomb must find multiple pieces of interaction, and the Lunar Conduit and other cards do not save him. The casters think AuraBomb knows there is no time to win game two, so he goes last-ditch in this game. Asuna wins game one.

games.summary: Draw — both players hit the turn limit with Asuna ahead one game

beats.text: Asuna starts with a Turbo Charge in his hand and wants to win as soon as possible, rather than as slowly as in game one. He reclaims his Winbless Lookout and glimpses into a third Astride card. Tristan is only level one, so there is no huge tempo.

AuraBomb has a Cosmic Bolt in his hand and few herbs, and the casters note that hard-activating it would leave him with one card. If he finds the Hearty Counter, the damage could add up. Asuna answers with Crystallized Destiny and Astral Seal questions.
AuraBomb passes with a full hand and does not level up. He is on turn two of three when both players hit the turn limit. The game ends in a draw and Asuna takes the round.

matches.round: Top 8 — Quarterfinal: Fire Merlin against Wind Razor Gale Kongming

players.name: Perfy
players.deck: Fire Merlin, Prismatic Edge (Spirit Blade: Ascension, Ghosts of Pendragon, Dungeon Guide, Fireball, Crystallized Destiny, Cheshire Cat, Inert Sword, Chilling Touch; Nullifying Lantern in the side)

players.name: Xenadrael
players.deck: Wind Razor Gale Kongming (first seed; Razor Gale x3, Ardent Cloudstriker, Favorable Winds, Zephyr, Tempest Downfall x2, Veiling Breeze, Cyclical Breeze, Calming Breeze, Windmill Engineer; eight Veiling Breezes in all with the cyclical ones)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters expect Perfy to bring in everything he has after a very quick and scary first game, including the Nullifying Lantern. They discuss that Razor Gale calling would be great if a card modified the elements of the cards.

games.summary: Xenadrael wins — a fast allies start with Ardent Cloudstriker overwhelms Perfy

beats.text: Xenadrael opens with a fast allies start. An Ardent Cloudstriker, a five-cost three-four, is intimidating by itself, because it can take care of all the two-three allies. The casters say Perfy's early game is not impressive and he is not in a good position.

Perfy plays Chilling Touch and Cheshire Cat, but Xenadrael's cloud striker goes for the Cheshire Cat and adds three more damage. The casters say the game was very close to over twice already, and that if the Cloud Striker had stuck the game would have ended sooner.
Xenadrael closes out the quick game one. The casters say it was so fast and so aggressive that it looked like an allies deck.

games.summary: Xenadrael wins — Zephyr and two Tempest Downfalls recycle for the last seven damage

beats.text: Xenadrael goes to level two and plays favorable winds, which cost one and draw cards. He reveals a card to prove he cannot take more than three damage this turn. The casters say this game shows why a Razor Gale deck is still a threat.

Perfy keeps the Spirit Blade: Ascension up until Xenadrael's turn, which is smart. The casters say losing a card to the ascension is very painful. Perfy has Dungeon Guide and Ghosts of Pendragon in hand and plays safe with his Veiling Breeze instead of putting down cards.
Xenadrael has Zephyr and two Tempest Downfalls in hand, each dealing five damage, and the cards recycle so he only needs seven more damage. Xenadrael wins game two and the quarterfinal.

matches.round: Top 4 — Semifinal: Astra Arisanna against Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia

players.name: Fruitcake
players.deck: Astra Arisanna (Polaris, Twinkling Cauldron; Cometfall; Cosmic Bolt; Fertile Grounds; Ingredient Pouch; Spellshield: Astra)

players.name: Bratus
players.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (Fabled Azurite Fatestone; Harness Lightning; Byakko's Command; Seiryuu's Command; Dungeon Guide; Trained Hawk; Baby Green Slime; Beseeched Fatestone; Regal Inquisition; generated Arcane Blast)

sideboardNotes.text: Fruitcake brings in Suspicious Concoction, which the casters identify in game two.

games.summary: Bratus wins — Fruitcake concedes after his planned Polaris and Cometfall damage falls short of the buffed Seiryuu

beats.text: Bratus pressures Fruitcake with a Forest Cake-boosted Trained Hawk, then uses Dungeon Guide to reach level three and transform Fabled Azurite Fatestone. Byakko’s Command lets Seiryuu attack again and adds a buff counter.

Fruitcake’s planned Polaris activation for eight plus Cometfall would deal 12 damage, one short of the buffed Seiryuu’s 13 life. The casters initially describe the damage resolving, then question whether Polaris was sacrificed before Fruitcake concedes.
Fruitcake concedes game one. The casters explain that he cannot survive the threatened Arcane Blast on the next turn.

games.summary: Bratus wins — Seiryuu attacks through Resolute Stand and Arcane Blast closes the match

beats.text: Fruitcake starts with Fertile Grounds and brings in Suspicious Concoction, then sets up Polaris. Bratus pressures him with Trained Hawk and Shimmercloak Assassin.
Bratus reaches level three with Dungeon Guide. Portentous Tanggu supplies the tenth quest counter, letting him transform Fabled Azurite Fatestone and play Seiryuu’s Command.
Fruitcake finds Resolute Stand, but Seiryuu’s attacks still push damage through. Bratus follows with Arcane Blast to win game two and the match 2-0.
