matches.round: Grand Finals: Wind Razor Gale Kongming against Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia

players.name: Xenadrael
players.deck: Wind Razor Gale Kongming (Canada; Razor Gale, Eternal Magistrate, Ardent Cloudstriker, Train Hawk, Beastbond Boots, Zephyr, Tempest Downfall, Cyclical Breeze, Veiling Breeze, Innervate Agility, Scout the Land, Beseeching Fatestone, Favorable Winds; a non-meta deck choice)

players.name: Bratus
players.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (Canada; Seiryuu's Command, Harness Lightning, Arcane Blast, Dungeon Guide, Baby Green Slime, Stifling Trap; the casters note Bratus said he had never played this matchup before)

matches.result: Xenadrael wins 2-0 and is the Ascent Niagara Falls champion, the first Canadian winner

sideboardNotes.text: The casters point out that the Eternal Magistrate stopped Bratus in the first game, and say Bratus plays carefully for someone who has never played the matchup. Xenadrael says in the interview that he won game one without the sideboard cards, with no Ensnaring Fumes.

games.summary: Xenadrael wins — a close game where Razor Gale triggers, Veiling Breeze and Beastbond Boots hold on and Bratus runs out of ways to deal the last six damage

beats.text: Xenadrael builds with Eternal Magistrate, which prevents things leaving the material deck in the main phase but not extra materialization. The casters say the thing to see is the Razor Gale itself, and that Xenadrael is looking at a Seiryuu's Command in Bratus's hand and arcane blasts as the danger.

Bratus plays Dungeon Guide and puts Xenadrael to 18 damage. The casters say Xenadrael's influence is too low to win this turn. A Tempest Downfall and a Cyclical Breeze fight over the same damage, and Xenadrael plays his Innervate Agility in response to the Tempest Downfall.

Xenadrael is down to two life after the Innervate Agility, so he has to win. He keeps Veiling Breeze, Beastbond Boots and Scout the Land, and every card he activates deals one damage to the Razor Gale, but the Boots prevent it. Both players are really close to death, and Bratus cannot find the last six damage. Xenadrael wins by the skin of his teeth.

games.summary: Xenadrael wins — a more convincing game where the Eternal Magistrate does not stop him this time

beats.text: Xenadrael has a better start in game two. He plays the Eternal Magistrate with the Magistrate not blocking his own plays, and draws cards with Favorable Winds. The casters say the card draw is usually the best option in this deck.

Bratus is out of gas with his Cyclical Veiling Breeze and the Baby Green Slime. The casters note the Eternal Magistrate is a timing restriction, not an effect restriction, so you can materialize something like a Grand Crusader's Ring in response. A buffed Ardent Cloudstriker arrives for Xenadrael.

Xenadrael finishes game two without shortcutting. The first Canadian winner of an Ascent in his own country takes the title, and the casters call it an amazing deck choice and fun to see a non-meta deck win. Xenadrael qualifies for Worlds in Singapore.

players.name: Xelomage
players.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (classic Seiryuu list: Seiryuu's Command, Byakko's Command, Harness Lightning, Lost Providence, Dungeon Guide, Benediction Angel, Heavy Swing, Vanish from Sight, Topsy Decree, Regal Inquisition and Incapacitate in the side)

players.name: Qbone
players.deck: Ciel toolbox deck (Heavy Swing, Manxome Armoire, Topsy Decree, Vanish from Sight, Dungeon Guide, Incapacitate; the casters call it a toolboxy deck that loops good cards)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters talk through Xelomage's side. They say Regal Inquisition from the side could come in and Incapacitates may replace cards that are weak in the matchup, but the deck has few spare slots.

games.summary: Xelomage wins — he disables Qbone's turns and a Seiryuu's Command line finishes

beats.text: Xelomage suppresses Qbone's plays and does not need a lot of influence, which the casters call the dream of the Seiryuu deck: disabling the opponent. Lost Providence draws him a card after he opens with an awakening line.

Qbone swings in with Heavy Swing for six including the mastery. The casters count 19 with allies in play, so Harness Lightning with Seiryuu's Command is a lethal line, and both players have to decide when to send it.
Qbone is one short of lethal, but Xelomage plays it so that Qbone does not have it. Xelomage takes game one with the classic Seiryuu list.

games.summary: Xelomage wins — he plays around Qbone's Manxome Armoire and Topsy Decree and ends with a generate-empower-empower line

beats.text: Xelomage goes for an aggressive Dungeon Guide into level two. The casters say he sets up so that level three would let him combo the following turn, and the Benediction Angel he activates sets Qbone back out of range.

Qbone throws down four cards for a Heavy Swing and holds a big hand. He pops the Manxome Armoire to trade for a Topsy Decree, and a Vanish from Sight is played in response. The casters stress that the order of triggers matters and are surprised by the exact line.

Xelomage goes to Guo Jia level three and recovers three again, shrugging off all the chip damage. He finishes with a Seiryuu swing and a generate-empower-empower sequence. The casters say he drew everything and executed well, and Xelomage wins 2-0.

matches.round: Round 2 (Day 1): fragmented Merlin against Water Nico

players.name: TatPap
players.deck: Fire fragmented Merlin (Merlin, Brilliant Vestige; Spirit Blade: Terminus; Sparkling Adornment; Angel Attendant; Steel Shot Strike; Dungeon Guide; Fracturize; Ghosts of Pendragon; Ravishing Finale as the key finisher)

players.name: Ne3tra
players.deck: Water Nico (Magebane Lash, Nullifying Mirror, Frostbind, Storm of Thorns, Fracturize, Frostsworn Paladin; builds lash counters for an Icebound Slam; Song of Frost and Snow Fairy in the side)

matches.result: Draw 1-1 — no time for a decider

sideboardNotes.text: The casters discuss Ne3tra's side: two Snow Fairies and Song of Frost, plus Staggering Strike to handle the preparation counters that fuel the Merlin plan, and a Frostbinder Apostle as a way to deal with an attacker.

games.summary: TatPap wins — fragmented memory and sheen counters give a Ravishing Finale-sized finish

beats.text: TatPap imbues a card for free and plays Angel Attendant and an ally with three fours as base values. The casters say the idea is to get sheen counters, and he needs one more fragmented card in memory so Merlin, Brilliant Vestige gets its on-enter. He is already on seven counters in the fragments.

Ne3tra uses Frostbind on the Dungeon Guide, because TatPap pays for it but does not have quite enough influence, and a Storm of Thorns surprises TatPap. Ne3tra tries to get Magebane Lash and Saber out, but TatPap has the faster clock.
TatPap reaches eight sheen counters and plays Spirit Blade: Terminus with an attack. The casters say that is game over for Ne3tra, and TatPap takes game one.

games.summary: Ne3tra wins — Nico lash counters and an Icebound Slam deal 11 while TatPap is without his Ghosts of Pendragon

beats.text: TatPap plays the careful route because his influence dropped so low. He uses Tweedle D to remove a Dungeon Guide, which the casters say feels bad. Ne3tra knows TatPap put a Fracturize in memory but still goes for the Nullifying Mirror.

Ne3tra materializes Magebane Lash with a floating memory and stacks sheen counters for Nico. He puts five lash counters on his champion, generating six lash counters for an Icebound Slam. TatPap's two Incapacitates are gone, and Ghosts of Pendragon is in the graveyard, not in hand.

TatPap has to survive one more turn against 11 damage, which the casters think is impossible. They say that if he had the Ghosts of Pendragon that he milled he could have finished the game. Ne3tra wins game two and time runs out, so the match is a draw.

players.deck: Wind Razor Gale (Veiling Breeze, Calming Breeze, Blanche, Sheltering Saint, Stifling Trap, Dream Fairy, Purifying Thurible, Orb of Sealing, Expel; a player who comes from Tristan)

players.deck: Fire Slimes (Storm Slime, Ethereal Slime, Eruption, Liminal Guide, Portentous Tanggu, Dungeon Guide, Cremation Ritual, Horn of Beastcalling, Distilled Water; seven raccoons instead of six)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters say players often put Stifling Trap in and name Dungeon Guide, but against slimes they like a different plan. They note the Blanche needs to prevent only a small amount of damage.

games.summary: Asuna wins — a controlling board and Veiling Breeze keep the slimes from a kill

beats.text: sungorio puts three slimes on board and an ephemeral Liminal Guide, and Asuna keeps Veiling Breeze, Blanche and the Orb of Sealing ready. The casters say it is hard to argue with Asuna's results, and that the deck comes down to whichever side finds its pop-off.

Asuna plays a raw Dream Fairy for damage and laughs about it, then gets the Purifying Thurible out and stops sungorio from gaining influence. He uses Expel to get rid of a Stifling Trap and keeps Asuna's board up.
The casters say Asuna must find the Razor Gale to finish while sungorio looks for a kill line. Asuna controls the game and wins the first game.

games.summary: sungorio wins — an Ethereal Slime swings in for lethal and Eruption finishes with three damage

beats.text: sungorio wants a kill line and notes there are two fire slimes and several non-fire slimes in the graveyard. He uses a floating memory from a reclaim and keeps the Essence Crucible out of play.
Asuna has built up a board and controls much of what sungorio does, but may run out of options. He needs to respond to sungorio's plays to survive.
The Ethereal Slime swings in for lethal and Slime Eruption banishes the last cards in response. The three damage is dealt and game two goes to sungorio.

games.summary: sungorio wins — Cremation Ritual and Portentous Tanggu build the slime board, and Asuna finds the Veiling Breeze without enough influence

beats.text: sungorio uses Cremation Ritual to draw more cards and keeps the floating memory with a Liminal Guide in play. He counts three cards in hand, and the next turn is an easy Portentous Tanggu with a Dungeon Guide.

He hits the slimes he needs and plays seven raccoons instead of six, a change that matters for the odds. Asuna can only put down so many cards for a Veiling Breeze, and Calming Breeze together with it is not enough.
Asuna finds the Veiling Breeze but does not have enough influence for it. The round goes to sungorio on Fire Slimes, 2-1.

matches.round: Round 5 (Day 1): Wind Krux Lorraine against Water Genbu

players.name: FTWwings
players.deck: Wind Krux Lorraine (Spirit Blade: Ascension, Prismatic Edge, Spirit Blade: Retribution, Imperious Galebind, Crux Sight, Dungeon Guide, Exalted cards in the side for Prismatic Edge reveals)

players.name: Yoroi
players.deck: Water Genbu (Engulf, Frostsworn Paladin, Conniving Plans, Fractal pullers, Revitalizing Cleanse, Nullifying Lantern-style denial; many negates and decrees)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters like FTWwings's idea of keeping all-exalted cards in the side, because at level three Prismatic Edge can reveal them for three damage. They also mention Shade-Mist Priestess as a possible way to reach level three for Spirit Blade: Ascension.

games.summary: Yoroi wins — negates and Engulf keep FTWwings from getting value, and Genbu's pressure finishes

beats.text: FTWwings pushes damage early, which is what you want to do against Genbu, and plays a free four-power ally that draws a card. Both players have a spell like Excalibur in hand. FTWwings tries to level to two to clear the Fatestone with a buff counter.

Yoroi strips FTWwings's hand of negates and decrees early. Another fractal puller ends in his graveyard, and FTWwings plays Calming Breeze but Yoroi's Engulf answers it, and FTWwings cannot do anything about the Engulf.
Yoroi levels, uses Prismatic Edge-proof timing and Genbu's protection, and wins game one. The casters say the deck makes it feel like you are on the losing end whatever you try.

games.summary: Yoroi wins — FTWwings cannot play his Spirit Blade: Ascension in time

beats.text: FTWwings uses Purifying Thurible to remove Yoroi's floating memory and goes to level one, which turns his material deck face up. A Gale Bind effect and a Crux Sight are shown, and he has another Gale Bind card in hand and may use Dungeon Guide.

Yoroi goes for Engulf immediately so that FTWwings gets no value from Spirit Blade: Ascension, and suppresses two Frostsworn Paladins. The casters see a possible trap if Yoroi activates Conniving Plans, but he plays carefully. The casters say Calming Breeze and the other negates do not help FTWwings.
FTWwings activates Spirit Blade: Ascension but the effect does not do enough, and Yoroi has everything he needs. The casters call it an unfortunate game two for FTWwings. Yoroi wins 2-0.

matches.round: Round 6 (Day 1): Ciel against Diana

players.name: TeamTrueCaban
players.deck: Ciel anti-meta build (Snow White, Weiss Queen; Heavy Swing; Blade Rift Seer as a fourth copy from the side; Tweedle D; Aquamirage Whisper; Inert Sword; Bandit; Frostbind)

players.name: Sebastian
players.deck: Diana comfort deck (Aetherwing Diana; Unbroken Mustang, Ranger Strides, Take Aim, Cheshire Cat, Backup Charger; zero-cost taunt that comes back when it dies)

sideboardNotes.text: TeamTrueCaban plays anti-meta cards and brings in a fourth Blade Rift Seer, a two-three-for-three ally with level one plus true sight, which clears the cat. The casters call the card good right now as a three-four body that needs no extra input.

games.summary: Sebastian wins — he keeps TeamTrueCaban's influence low and always has the right answer

beats.text: Sebastian puts out Spirit of Water and uses Unbroken Mustang to clear a sensor. The casters say Sebastian knows TeamTrueCaban's deck well, so he does not worry about mysteries. He focuses on keeping his opponent's influence as low as possible and makes TeamTrueCaban work for each play.

TeamTrueCaban commits to the board and cannot interact on Sebastian's turn. He levels to Ciel level one and looks to find another Heavy Swing to start chunking damage at Diana. A Frostbind, Snow White and the Tweedle D keep Diana rested.

TeamTrueCaban went far down on influence and has one card in hand. Sebastian swings in with a loaded-up Aquamirage, with seven from the Ranger Strides and four more from Take Aim, which goes over the top of the three-damage prevention. Sebastian takes game one.

games.summary: Sebastian wins — TeamTrueCaban is always one answer short, and Ranger Strides makes Diana distant

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban plays Blade Rift Seer and an Inert Sword, with Snow White staring at Diana. He keeps the Bandit in hand and levels to Ciel to keep Diana rested so she cannot pull her ability. Sebastian has to find a way to clear the Snow White.

Sebastian glimpses for a floating memory and finds a distant enabler to set up his powerful cards. The casters say it is unacceptable for Diana to become distant, and a Ranger Strides is popped before Sebastian knows if another unique human ally is coming to turn the Tweedle D back on.

Sebastian always has the right answer and keeps pressing distant. TeamTrueCaban never gets a free turn to find the extra damage he needs, and his Heavy Swing from game one does not show up. Sebastian wins 2-0 and is in for Day 2.

players.deck: Wind Krux Lorraine (Lorraine, Spirit Ruler; Ghosts of Pendragon; Prismatic Edge; Clarent, Reimagined; Sword of Seeking; Drawn Blade; Creative Shock; Dungeon Guide; Spirit Blade: Ascension; Gale Bind; Orb of Sealing)

players.name: PewPewStan
players.deck: Fire Luxem Zander (Spirit of Serene Fire; Lightweaver’s Assault, Striking Illuminance, Luxem Sight, Regal Inquisition, Angelic Channeling)

games.summary: PewPewStan wins — MaruX concedes at 27 damage

beats.text: MaruX opens with a hand that is hard to use: the casters say it is a choice between holding a whole hand of good cards or leveling. He draws many cards with Creative Shock to look for Dungeon Guide, and has Clarent, Reimagined on the board to protect his allies.

PewPewStan plays cautiously and uses Imperious Galebind, a Dream Fairy that goes the distance every time, and a Corhazi insignia for preparation counters so Striking Illuminance can deal real damage. Ayella suppresses MaruX's Prismatic Edge. The casters say the deck with the draw-focused start has a big advantage in this matchup.

PewPewStan finds Striking Illuminance and double Lightweaver's Assault, plus a Regal Inquisition, while MaruX has Lorraine, Spirit Ruler and a Prismatic Edge out. A rules question about the Drawn Blade that Sabella put into play is explained to the players.

games.summary: Draw — time expires

beats.text: MaruX takes the first turn and baits out the Purifying Thurible. He plays Sword of Seeking, which had been replaced by the distortion versions for a while, and a Gentle Respite comes down for PewPewStan to get influence. There are no more preparation counters for MaruX.

MaruX plays Aesan Protector for three and follows up with Spirit Blade: Ascension. He uses a Clarent instead of the Sword of Seeking to kill the Dungeon Guide. PewPewStan keeps Resolute Stand, Vanish from Sight and two Luxem Sights in hand.

Ghosts of Pendragon and a second Ghosts of Pendragon in MaruX's hand build a big board, but it is MaruX's last turn in the overtime procedure. PewPewStan needs 27 damage on his final turn while at Zander and cannot get there. Time is called; the recorded match result is a draw. The casters say that one more turn for MaruX would have made a huge difference.

matches.round: Round 8 (final round, Day 1) — win-and-in for Day 2: Water Aetherwing Diana against Fire Jin

players.name: Noel
players.deck: Water Aetherwing Diana (tried-and-true list that Noel also played at Las Vegas Nationals; Cerulean Decree, Undercurrent Vantage, Pearl Prayer, Regenerate, Song of Frost and Thronekeeper Bullfrog from the side, a Cheshire Cat and Krustallan Archer)

players.deck: Fire Jin (Frostsworn Paladin plan, Backup Charger, Lost Providence, Berserker's Blade, Relentless Outburst, Regal Inquisition, damage-counter burn)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters expect Noel to bring in the Songs of Frost and the Thronekeeper Bullfrogs to stay safer against the Jin burn plan.

games.summary: Noel wins — she survives the burn plan with Pearl Prayer and Regenerate and finishes through Regal Inquisition and Cerulean Decree

beats.text: DjieDjoen reaches Jin level three and clears the Frostsworn Paladin. He plans to draw with Lost Providence and to activate Backup Charger for Berserker's Blade. The casters say Diana has only 19 life, so he does not need many damage counters for an enraged lethal.

Noel is very durable. Pearl Prayer and Regenerate replace themselves and recover six damage, and Relentless Outburst is only a board clear because Noel can go distant. A Cerulean Decree, mistaken for an Undercurrent Vantage by the casters, stops a big swing.

DjieDjoen swings with a plus two, plus four attack for 19 and tries not to overkill. Noel has all her influence left. Because DjieDjoen cast Regal Inquisition before anything else, Noel puts the damage counters on him perfectly and wins game one.

games.summary: Noel wins — Song of Frost and the queens on her board frustrate DjieDjoen, and a Krustallan Archer swings for the win

beats.text: Noel sideboards the Songs of Frost and Thronekeeper Bullfrogs, and plays Cheshire Cat as an ally that puts on pressure. The casters note the contrast with game one, where Noel tried to survive without dealing too much damage.
The queens on Noel's board are very annoying to deal with, and DjieDjoen's frustration is visible. A Krustallan Archer swings in for four and another attack for eight, and Noel wins the round 2-0.

beats.text: shokoouo uses Surveil Possessions mastery and Angelic Channeling to banish a strength card and a Carter. The casters say Angel Attendant punishes any first attack from an Aetherwing, which has to waste a turn or wait for the Inert Sword. He has Resolute Stand and a stacked hand.

baniRien has a Cerulean Decree for minus three and a negate, and the casters note a cursed strength that cannot be negated will deal four damage. Carter and the Liminal Guide come out and he runs low on cards.
shokoouo gets another omen at the end of the turn and has three cards in hand, so he can use the Manxome Armoire and do it again. baniRien knows it and concedes game one.

games.summary: baniRien wins — a conservative Snow White with an aggressive ally on the board is the key

beats.text: baniRien uses Weaving Manastream greedily at the cost of the Crystallized Destiny, and Shokoouo throws down Creative Shock instead of being greedy. baniRien finds the Quickstep Treads and a floating memory, and is in a good position.

baniRien plays Snow White with an aggressive ally on board and stays conservative. shokoouo is made to discard and banish two cards from his graveyard, and a Liminal Guide hit by a banish is one less draw.

baniRien's four new cards include three floating memories, and a Resolute Stand with a tax question is explained. The casters count nine blocked and an 18-damage attack, which is game over for shokoouo, who needs the awakening to win and cannot find it. baniRien wins 2-1.

matches.round: Round 10 (Day 2, Round 2) — Europe against North America: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia against Water Aetherwing Diana

players.name: Xelomage
players.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (France; Seiryuu's Command, Byakko's Command, Lost Providence, Incandescent Reliquary, Imperial Countermeasures, Benediction Angel, Dungeon Guide, Ayella, Auspicious Manifestation, Displace, Refreshing Charge; many sideboard cards)

players.name: Sebastian
players.deck: Water Aetherwing Diana (Frostsworn Paladin, Krustallan Archer, Quickstep Treads, Ranger Strides, Smoke Bombs, Frostbind, Cerulean Decree, Resolute Stand, Besiege-style sensor plan; nothing to sideboard)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters say Xelomage has a lot to sideboard while Sebastian has nothing to change. They discuss Reforging, Expel and the nullifying cards as weak in this matchup, and say Incapacitate could stop Sebastian's Tactical Retreat. The casters later say the sideboarding took his power level back.

games.summary: Xelomage wins — a double Byakko's Command turn and Ayella suppression carry the dragon through Sebastian's Imperial Countermeasures surprise

beats.text: Sebastian flips Spirit of Water and puts out a Looking Glass, and the casters say that with Diana you know what you are up against. A forest cake gives Xelomage a cycle and a draw, and Sebastian deals three damage with a swing.

Xelomage goes for the aggressive play, banishing his level-up cards carefully. A double Byakko's Command turn flips the dragon, and Ayella gives him a free suppress on the forest cake. He holds the Lost Providence and Incandescent Reliquary to extract as much as he can.
Sebastian is surprised by Imperial Countermeasures preventing his damage. Sebastian cannot get enough through, and Xelomage wins game one with the Seiryuu.

games.summary: Sebastian wins — he gets a fast Frostsworn Paladin start and Frostbind with Cerulean Decree stops the dragon

beats.text: Sebastian goes first with Quickstep Treads on a distant Diana. The casters note a skill check: when Resolute Stand can exist in the list, he must double-load the Aetherwing on turn two so it hits. Xelomage does not have an end-of-turn Angelic Channeling to get Dungeon Guide to three.

Xelomage holds Displace and asks when to flip the dragon. Sebastian plays the game slowly with a four-damage weapon from three Aether charges, and distant Diana forces Xelomage's hand. The casters say that when Diana is distant, the Treads can be ignored.
Sebastian has a Cerulean Decree and a Frostbind in hand and plays both. The Besiege the Winds is banished, which scoops the dragon plan, and game two goes to Sebastian.

games.summary: Sebastian wins — a fast Frostsworn Paladin start and Ranger Strides make the lethal before Xelomage can flip his dragon

beats.text: Xelomage has a hand with a Dungeon Guide and a Benediction Angel and besieges to one, but the casters say he needs a nice opener and cannot find the Auspicious Manifestation he needs. He reaches six quest counters and draws, taking the counters.

Sebastian plays the Frostsworn Paladins and Krustallan Archers to deal steady damage. The casters note he has nothing to sideboard while Xelomage had a lot, and that Xelomage's sideboarding might have taken his power level back.

Sebastian hits the floating memory with Diana and uses Ranger Strides for a 12-damage swing: at 19 damage with a five heal it is still lethal. The casters say it was way too fast, and a pause follows while the judges confirm the play. Sebastian wins 2-1.

players.deck: Wind Krux Lorraine (Lorraine, Spirit Ruler; Drawn Blade; Pallor Sword; Prismatic Edge; Sword of Seeking; Spirit Blade: Ascension; Queen Cinder Hog; Beseech the Winds; a sideboard card to protect his life total and allies)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters point to a CasuaL sideboard card he adds to keep his life total safe and to protect the few allies he activates at level three.

games.summary: Horinti wins — Heavy Swing pressure and a second Dwaying clear CasuaL's Aella and his Krux plan

beats.text: CasuaL's Lorraine list is very different from the usual one. He gets the Drawn Blade and Pallor Sword out with Lorraine, Spirit Ruler. The casters say Horinti's deck puts threats on board while squeezing the opponent's influence, and that Snow White prevents prevention.

Horinti uses Fairy Whispers and Displace to keep Ayella safe and plays Sabella, which can bring the Drawn Blade out if banished again. The second Dwaying swings into Ayella and takes it out, putting CasuaL in a dicey position.

CasuaL turns the Drawn Blade into a Prismatic Edge to clear some of the board, which disables the Dwaying unless Horinti finds another unique human ally. The casters say CasuaL has more cards available than expected, but Horinti takes the first game.

games.summary: Horinti wins — Heavy Swing, an interceptor in response and the Manxome Armoire loop finish a fast game

beats.text: CasuaL takes the first turn and passes entirely down. The casters say Horinti goes to level one, hits with Heavy Swing for six and then for seven with an omen, and that this is big pressure.

Horinti cannot redirect the Heavy Swing, but in response he plays the Rose, so an interceptor is in play when the swing resolves. CasuaL uses Spirit Blade: Ascension on the Sword of Seeking into the Prismatic Edge and plays Queen Cinder Hog for three damage.

Horinti gets out the Manxome Armoire and sets up to return Heavy Swing to hand after attacking. CasuaL's hand is entirely down, and Horinti wins game two and the round to be one win from the Top 8. The casters say it was very quick.

matches.round: Round 12 (Day 2, Round 4 — final Swiss round): Water Aetherwing Diana mirror

players.name: HenkieTheGoat
players.deck: Water Aetherwing Diana (Aether charges, Charge the Soul, Quickstep Treads, Backup Charger, Frostsworn Paladin, Cerulean Decree, Frozen Dismissal, Reforging in the side; the casters say he plays an all-in send-it style)

players.name: Noel
players.deck: Water Aetherwing Diana (Unbroken Mustang, Fracturize, Quickstep Treads, Backup Charger, Krustallan Archer, Cheshire Cat, Flash Grenade, Ranger Strides, Tactical Retreat, Snow White in the main board, Weaving Manastream, Aquamirage Whisper, Refreshing Charge)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters explain that Snow White in the main board is much better against a Jin or Ciel deck than into another level one Diana deck, and discuss Reforging, an Aether charge that banishes a card from a graveyard and loads it for one attack.

games.summary: Noel wins — Unbroken Mustang and a fast influence start beat a Hanky hand that lacks an Aetherwing

beats.text: Noel goes first, and the casters say whoever goes first has the advantage in the mirror. He does not level up and has no distant enabler, so he goes for Backup Charger, and HenkieTheGoat does have the enabler. Noel keeps Tactical Retreat in hand in a mirror, so he does not take damage from the Aetherwing.

HenkieTheGoat needs two Frozen Dismissals to stop Noel, who has six cards in hand, and cannot find them. The casters say his hand without an Aetherwing in play is not very good, but with an Aetherwing it would have been amazing, with Charge the Soul and a couple of other Aether charges.

Noel pops the Flash Grenade to prevent the damage from distant units and plays Quickstep Treads and Fracturize. The casters say the Unbroken Mustang was the key to victory, because it got rid of the Aquamirage Whisper early. Noel takes game one.

games.summary: Noel wins — a sacrifice swing for one more than lethal beats HenkieTheGoat's tight Cerulean Decree hand

beats.text: Noel plays a Cheshire Cat, with Charge the Soul loaded into the Aquamirage Whisper, and Krustallan Archer for four damage and a card. The casters say Snow White could lock the Diana champion for a turn, but Noel goes for tempo. A shuffle mix-up on glimpsed cards is caught and fixed immediately.

HenkieTheGoat leans back and stays relaxed. He holds a couple of Cerulean Decrees, but a Cerulean Decree costs one more than he has to keep a Frozen Dismissal up. The casters count that two Aether charges, being distant, the Whisper and Ranger Strides add up to a lethal amount.

Noel writes a 20 on his notepad and sacrifices a unit and the cat to swing for one over lethal, with the Flash Grenade ready. HenkieTheGoat cannot pay for multiple negates, and Noel wins the match 2-0 and moves into the Top 8.

matches.round: Top 8 — Quarterfinal 1 (all-EU pairing): Wind Razor Gale Arisana against Wind Wake Up allies

players.name: Asuna
players.deck: Wind Razor Gale Arisana (two Razor Gale, Veiling Breeze, Scout the Land, Fairy Whispers, Dream Fairy, Spellshield: Wind, Nullifying Mirror, Tariff Ring, Distilled Water; Tempest Downfall in the side; only 15 life at level one)

players.name: KidDelicious
players.deck: Wind Wake Up allies (Purse, Cheshire Cat, Ranger Strides, Second Wind, Evasive Maneuvers, Take Aim, Tariff Ring, Wind Resonance Bauble, Backup Charger, Windmill Engineer, Scatter Essence)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters look at both sideboards. They say both players have a good amount of sideboard cards, and mention Berry Whisperers and extra Veiling Breezes for Asuna to survive the seven-damage swings.
The casters think Asuna may side in Tempest Downfall, and KidDelicious needs a way to protect Purse.

games.summary: KidDelicious wins — Purse, Ranger Strides and Evasive Maneuvers swing through Asuna's Veiling Breeze

beats.text: The casters think the Wake Up deck has the favor in the matchup. KidDelicious plays a Backup Charger for a power cell, a Tariff Ring and a Purse that can protect anything on the board. Asuna plays Veiling Breeze early and respectfully.

KidDelicious puts four damage counters on Asuna's Razor Gale-level champion and threatens a distant swing for eight after the next aim counter. With a double Ranger Strides, sacrificing the Cheshire Cat, he can swing for ten. Asuna's Veiling Breeze prevents four.

Asuna needs 11 damage through four prevented, and the casters note that an Evasive Maneuvers on the swing with Purse and Ranger Strides makes the numbers work. KidDelicious wins a tight, back-and-forth game one.

games.summary: Asuna wins — Razor Gale triggers on every wind activation, and the Nullifying Mirror stops the held Veiling Breeze

beats.text: Asuna has no influence generation without a turn-one Razor Gale and works to get the herbs off the boards. He sees the Distilled Waters and goes for the damage play. Scout the Land digs for the second Razor Gale.

KidDelicious has everything on board for a 20-damage swing from one Purse if it all goes through. Asuna still has a Razor Gale in play and deals damage with every wind activation. A Wind Resonance Bauble comes out for KidDelicious.

Asuna deals his damage before recollecting, and KidDelicious is left with exactly two cards in hand. The Nullifying Mirror will negate any held Veiling Breeze, and Asuna has two fast-speed wind cards in hand, one too many for KidDelicious to answer. The match goes to game three.

games.summary: Asuna wins — a long game decided by a missed trigger and a deck-cut ruling, with the Razor Gale finishing

beats.text: KidDelicious brings back a Windmill Engineer and builds a wide board, but the casters say the board is vulnerable. Asuna has not found a Dream Fairy and has a second Scatter Essence, and the Tempest Downfall in the side forces KidDelicious to protect Purse.

KidDelicious plays Second Wind and wakes up, and Asuna has only 15 life. He plays the Three Visits pre-recollection, which denies some damage. A gather trigger is missed when Asuna moves into the main phase, and the casters say it is gone.

Asuna hopes for a second Razor Gale. An extra-cards penalty is checked when Asuna cuts the deck, and both players become a little tilted from missed interactions. Asuna digs for the cyclical Veiling Breeze and finishes the game and the match, 2-1.

matches.round: Top 4 — Semifinal (featured match; rematch of a prior Day 2 loss for Cabin): Water Ciel allies against Water Aetherwing Diana

players.name: TeamTrueCaban
players.deck: Water Ciel allies (all three Weaving Manastream, one Fluffy Shopkeep in the main, Corhazi Trapper, Unyielding Wraithguard, Snow White, Nia, Frostbind, Freezing Hail, Storm of Thorns, Sense of Restful Peace, Topsy Decree swapped in for Cerulean Decree for the Diana matchup, Fracturize in the side)

players.name: Sebastian
players.deck: Water Aetherwing Diana (Quickstep Treads, Ranger Strides, Cheshire Cat, Refreshing Charge, Tactical Retreat, Smoke Bombs, Frozen Dismissal, Flash Grenade, Backup Charger; Unbroken Mustang, Drown Aether and Eight of Spades in the side)

matches.result: TeamTrueCaban wins 2-1 and qualifies for Worlds

sideboardNotes.text: TeamTrueCaban told the casters that after testing he felt so confident into Diana that he swapped his main-deck Cerulean Decrees for Topsy Decrees. A Topsy Decree banishes floating memory and also gives a spell shroud, which helps against other decks. He keeps two Cerulean Decrees.
Sebastian brings in the Unbroken Mustang and Drown Aether to deal with Cabin's board, and may bring in the Eight of Spades for more things to do.

games.summary: Sebastian wins — a tactical retreat and a distant swing for seven finish a TeamTrueCaban who has lost his strong resources early

beats.text: Sebastian puts the Inert Sword out, which tells the casters a Cheshire Cat is on the way. TeamTrueCaban has a Dwaying in hand but needs a unique water human ally to turn it on. Sebastian uses Tactical Retreat to end combat, take no damage, set up a float and go distant.

TeamTrueCaban uses Storm of Thorns on a Frostsworn Paladin, but his floating memory is not enough. The casters say Sebastian, who made five misplays in a row in an earlier match, keeps the Fracturize for Quickstep Treads or Ranger Strides.

TeamTrueCaban holds a Frostbind but would have to put down his whole hand to use it. Sebastian fires off a distant attack: three from the Paladin and two from the game, plus two for distance, is seven and lethal. Sebastian takes game one.

games.summary: TeamTrueCaban wins — a Wraith Guard wall and a wide ally board win the war of attrition

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban thinks for a long time on the first turn about two or three turns ahead, so that he is not stopped as hard as in game one. He plays a Sensor and a Backup Charger for a power cell, and the one Fracturize in hand gives a floating memory for the level up.

Sebastian brings in Fracturize and the Drown Aether, and the casters say he keeps drawing cards that are good for the matchup. TeamTrueCaban resolves the Unyielding Wraithguard, and Sebastian has only two cards left in hand and cannot Frostbind it.

TeamTrueCaban builds a huge, wide board protected by other allies and keeps turning allies sideways. Sebastian's counters run out of steam, and the casters say having three Weaving Manastreams in the top nine cards is not what Sebastian needs. TeamTrueCaban ties the match 1-1.

games.summary: TeamTrueCaban wins — he wears out every Frozen Dismissal and a Freezing Hail finishes

beats.text: Sebastian passes his first turn and TeamTrueCaban develops a Corhazi Trapper. TeamTrueCaban's Frostbind banishes Sebastian's Refreshing Charge, which denies a float and forces Sebastian to commit two more Aether charges to attack with Diana.

TeamTrueCaban's Snow White rests the Diana so she cannot attack, and Sebastian has to play something. Sebastian plays Fracturize in response, which removes the Inert Sword line, and he holds a Nullifying Mirror in a board state that is hard for TeamTrueCaban.

TeamTrueCaban keeps wearing out Sebastian's negates until Sebastian has no Frozen Dismissal. A Nia hits the board and turns on the Dwaying, and a Freezing Hail from the top of the deck gives the lethal attempt. TeamTrueCaban wins and advances to the final, which locks his slot for Worlds. The casters call it a true war of attrition.

matches.round: Top 8 — Quarterfinal 1: Water Ciel allies against Wind Krux Lorraine

players.name: TeamTrueCaban
players.deck: Water Ciel allies (EU Nationals winner; Nia, Mistveiled Scout; Fluffy Shopkeep; Cheshire Cat; Frostsworn Paladin; Cerulean Decree; Storm of Thorns; Frozen Dismissal; Nullifying Mirror; Veiling Breeze; Extricating Touch; Song of Frost in the side)

players.name: TheRainGoddess
players.deck: Wind Krux Lorraine (Lorraine, Wandering Warrior; Lorraine, Blademaster; Ghosts of Pendragon; Spirit Blade: Ascension; Prismatic Edge; Dungeon Guide; Lost Providence; Fairy Whispers; Windmill Engineer; Aesan Protector; Dream Fairy; Sword of Seeking)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters guess that TeamTrueCaban brings in Safeguard Amulet, Snow White and Song of Frost, and they think only a small number of the Songs of Frost go in. They add that a second Snow White would constrain the opponent when his first one is not followed up.

games.summary: TheRainGoddess wins — he is behind for the first half, then Ghosts of Pendragon, Spirit Blade: Ascension and Prismatic Edge turn the game

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban opens with Fluffy Shopkeep and a Windmill Engineer line and Nia, Mistveiled Scout names Lorraine, Blademaster, so Lorraine cannot level on time. The casters say no Wind Krux deck has levelled to Lorraine as its first materialization all weekend, and that TheRainGoddess must find a way to stop the early pressure.

TheRainGoddess uses Calming Breeze as his only saving grace and plays Gale Bind with an Exalted Heart. A Nullifying Mirror turns off the elements in his memory, but he builds a strong hand with Lost Providence and Spirit Blade: Ascension, and the casters say the odds flip back to him.

TeamTrueCaban plays a Frostsworn Paladin to remove the Ghosts of Pendragon, and TheRainGoddess finds an Ascension that returns Prismatic Edge to the material deck and draws two more. The casters call the top-deck backbreaking. TeamTrueCaban has no hand left, and TheRainGoddess deploys five damage and swings in.

games.summary: TheRainGoddess wins — a long, careful game where Ghosts of Pendragon finally arrive and Spirit Blade: Ascension finishes the fight

beats.text: TheRainGoddess goes second and draws the extra card. He plays Aesan Protector to bring back his Dream Fairy and keeps pressure on a TeamTrueCaban hand that is not what he wanted. The casters note that TeamTrueCaban notes down the cards to play around, and that he has only one Frostsworn Paladin, a Cheshire Cat and a few other two-three allies.

TeamTrueCaban plays Nia first and then the swing, which plays around the Storm of Thorns. The Tweedle D and his Extricating Touch let him see TheRainGoddess's memory, and TheRainGoddess holds two Spirit Blade: Ascensions and keeps the third in memory. The casters say TheRainGoddess has not found a Ghost of Pendragon all game.

TeamTrueCaban's relentless attacks, Frozen Dismissal and Song of Frost from the side keep TheRainGoddess on the back foot. The casters say Frozen Dismissal should have been held up and note TheRainGoddess is down to a single hope: a Spirit Blade: Retribution that puts the whole graveyard in banishment.

TheRainGoddess plays Ghosts of Pendragon, which returns a sword and draws two, and finds Cruxite and a fire card. TeamTrueCaban plays every out, but TheRainGoddess finds the damage and wins 2-0. In the interview he says he tested every deck and did not expect to make the quarterfinals.

matches.round: Top 8 — Quarterfinal 2: Fire Vanitas "horses and taxes" against Wind Luxom Zander

players.name: Noel
players.deck: Fire Vanitas "horses and taxes" (higher seed; Brisk Windtrotter, Sadi, Dungeon Guide, Searing Rebuke, Poisoned Dagger, Angelic Attendant, Radiant Origins, Sense of Restful Peace, Flagrant Guide, Beseech the Winds; new inclusions for this version)

players.name: Lifdrasyl
players.deck: Wind Luxom Zander (one Fluffy Shopkeep in the main, Windmill Engineer, Sadi, Purifying Thurible, Nullifying Mirror, Dream Fairy, Incapacitate, Lightweaver's Assault, Luxem Sight, Blinding Steel, Surveil the Winds, Slice and Dice; Ayella-style card flow)

games.summary: Lifdrasyl wins — he reaches Zander level three through Noel's taxes and wins the damage race

beats.text: Noel has the first turn as the higher seed and goes for Sense of Restful Peace to disable abilities. Lifdrasyl has to banish Flagrant Guide to level up, which makes his turn awkward with the Vanitas tax on materialization.

Lifdrasyl plays Windmill Engineer and uses the draw to build influence, then Sadi and a Purifying Thurible for card flow. A missed Death Executioner trigger is ruled on and the casters note it is a card that is often missed in the heat of play.

Lifdrasyl reaches level three with seven influence even after paying all the taxes and plays Blinding Steel. Noel's damage is not unpreventable and the pressure comes too late. The casters say that getting the horse out earlier might have won Noel the damage race.

games.summary: Noel wins — Vanitas, Shizun of the Ash and a Poisoned Dagger swing the damage race back

beats.text: Noel goes first and plays carefully while Shizun of the Ash and the new Radiant Origins card enter. A game-state problem on a materialization is fixed by the media team and the judges, and the casters ask the players to stop touching memory.

Lifdrasyl finds a Serro operative and a Nullifying Mirror, and sits on six influence with a hand full of allies and Lightweaver's Assaults. He has an Incapacitate and a Dream Fairy, and he responds to everything Noel does.

Noel takes damage in a back-and-forth race: Lifdrasyl deals 19 damage and the pendulum swings every turn. Noel's Vanitas swings with a strong Brisk Windtrotter, and a Searing Rebuke and Poisoned Dagger line gives her the win.

games.summary: Lifdrasyl wins — surveil lines find Slice and Dice and the lethal damage through Noel's Searing Rebuke

beats.text: Noel levels to Vanitas one and puts all her faith in the top of her deck. The casters count eight guides and two Beseeches, and she brings Sadi back to the board and takes out an ally.

Lifdrasyl keeps a couple of cards in hand and replays Fluffy Shopkeep as an interceptor. His surveil lines dig deeper, and he loses an Ensnaring Fumes but sits on a solid memory. Vanitas does not connect, so there is no taxation and Noel's Poisoned Dagger comes out for free.

Lifdrasyl has the influence advantage and bullies Noel. His attacks push through 11 damage, and Slice and Dice closes the game as Noel's Searing Rebuke cannot stop it. Lifdrasyl moves to the semifinals.

matches.round: Top 8 — Quarterfinal 3: Wind Krux Lorraine against Umbra Oblation Ciel

players.name: Zero0000000000
players.deck: Wind Krux Lorraine (Lorraine, Spirit Ruler; Drawn Blade; Ghosts of Pendragon; Spirit Blade: Ascension; Prismatic Edge; Sword of Seeking; Windmill Engineer; Lost Providence; Nullifying Mirror; Purifying Thurible)

players.name: Asuna
players.deck: Oblation Ciel with an unexpected Umbra pivot (Baleful Oblation, Fractal of Rain, Library Witch, Angelic Channeling, Gentle Respite, Liminal Guide, Creative Shock; Mirage's Grave for unpreventable damage; Resolute Stand, Blanche, Sheltering Saint and Stifling Trap in the side)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters say Resolute Stand has to come in for Asuna, because the Krux deck is full of small attackers with less than three power. They name Stifling Trap and Blanche, Sheltering Saint as other strong options, and note Baleful Oblation would kill the allies anyway.

games.summary: Zero0000000000 wins — Ghosts of Pendragon and a row of Windmill Engineers deal lethal before Asuna reaches level three

beats.text: Asuna surprises the casters with an Oblation Ciel pivot built to return Baleful Oblation to the top of his deck once he reaches level three. Zero0000000000 starts with Drawn Blade into banishment, which the casters call very important because Lorraine, Spirit Ruler needs it to get a sword back.

Zero0000000000 uses Spirit Blade: Ascension to deny Asuna's level-up cards and brings out Prismatic Edge with Sword of Seeking. Asuna has no Dungeon Guide to help, so leveling puts only two cards in memory and Ascension can banish one of them.
Zero0000000000 pushes in every ally, with Windmill Engineers back to back, and takes Asuna to 30 damage counters. The Ghosts of Pendragon deal lethal, and Zero0000000000 goes 1-0 up.

games.summary: Zero0000000000 wins — Asuna is shut out of every element and never levels

beats.text: Asuna uses Angelic Channeling and Library Witch to find cards. The casters say Zero0000000000 will not let Asuna find an answer. Zero0000000000 plays Lorraine, Spirit Ruler and Drawn Blade, and keeps the Ghosts of Pendragon in reserve.

Zero0000000000 taps the Nullifying Mirror so Asuna cannot use his spirit cards, and uses Lost Providence to refill. Asuna keeps four Baleful Oblations in hand but cannot reach level three and play them, and he is shut out of wind, water and fire.

Zero0000000000 plays with correct materializations and holds up durable and Ascension. Asuna's Liminal Guide does one point of damage and the Library Witch is not enough. Zero0000000000 wins 2-0 and reaches the semifinals.

matches.round: Top 8 — Quarterfinal 4: Wind Krux Lorraine against Wind Luxom Zander

players.name: GlenyBoi
players.deck: Wind Krux Lorraine (Ghosts of Pendragon x3, Clarent, Reimagined, Prismatic Edge, Spirit Blade: Ascension, Drawn Blade, Fluffy Shopkeep, Aesan Protector, Windmill Engineer, Sadi, Dungeon Guide, Lost Providence, Imperious Galebind, Stifling Trap)

players.name: Jett
players.deck: Wind Luxom Zander (TM32 build; Lightweaver's Assault x3, Luxem Sight, Gleaming Cut, Blinding Steel, Heavenly Guide, Dungeon Guide, Slice and Dice, Poisoned Dagger, Veiling Breeze, Calming Breeze, Ensnaring Fumes, Surveil the Winds, Fairy Whispers, Incapacitate)

sideboardNotes.text: Jett brings three cards into his main deck. In the interview he says his version is built to be easier to play, and that he plays only three Luxom sights, two in the main and one in the side. He says his deck is pre-boarded, so his main deck holds the cards he wants to play.

games.summary: Jett wins — a free Zander level-up with Blinding Steel and a Lightweaver's Assault line beat GlenyBoi's greedy Pendragon turn

beats.text: GlenyBoi opens with Dungeon Guide and Aesan Protector, the high-pressure start a Wind Krux deck needs. Jett keeps Ensnaring Fumes and Veiling Breeze, and the casters note he has Heavenly Guide to re-use.

Jett plays Stifling Gyre naming Ghosts of Pendragon, making GlenyBoi pay four extra cards to resolve its on-enter draw. GlenyBoi levels to Lorraine, Wandering Warrior and brings out Sword of Seeking; Verdigris Decree is his potential answer to the Gyre.

GlenyBoi uses Imperious Galebind to take the Lost Providence, the Poisoned Dagger and the Drawn Blade, and has three Ghosts of Pendragon to play for nine damage. He then plays Prismatic Edge instead of Clarent, Reimagined, which the casters call a little too greedy.
Jett suppresses the Ghosts and calms the damage with Calming Breeze. His Poisoned Dagger for one and a revealed Lightweaver's Assault deal eight damage to the face, and Jett wins game one.

games.summary: Jett wins — a Veiling Breeze for one keeps him alive for exactly one more turn, then Lightweaver's Assaults finish

beats.text: Jett brings in three cards and plays Sadi back from the banishment with only three cards in hand. GlenyBoi has no Stifling Trap to snipe Sadi on its return. Jett swings face rather than into the Aesan Protector and Scout the Land for a better position.

GlenyBoi uses Fluffy Shopkeep again and sends Clarent to the banishment. Jett uses Heavenly Guide to go up to level three and the casters say it is juicy, because GlenyBoi has no Stifling Trap. The Ensnaring Fumes, with a floating memory, are a big blowout.

The casters count 12.5 percent to find a Luxom card and Jett finds a Luxem Sight. GlenyBoi has two Veiling Breezes and a Retribution in hand. Jett has ten cards in hand and could play a raw Slice and Dice into Lightweaver's Assaults, and a Veiling Breeze for one barely keeps him alive for one more turn.
Jett finishes with Lightweaver's Assaults and the damage stays just above GlenyBoi's reach. Jett wins 2-0 and moves to the semifinals against TheRainGoddess, a Wind Luxom against Wind Krux match.

matches.round: Round 10 (Day 2) — Wind Wake Up mirror, two different builds, with a Top 8 spot at stake

players.name: CasuaL
players.deck: Wind Wake Up (stays at level 0: Perse, Relentless Raptor, Liu Bei, Oathkeeper, Mad Hatter, Cheshire Cat, Concealed Marksman, Enfeebling Orb, Verdigris Decree)

players.name: V41N
players.deck: Wind Wake Up (Lorraine level 1 build with no Perse: Beseech the Winds, Ranger Strides, Mad Hatter, Concealed Marksman, Dream Fairy, Skirting Step, Second Wind, Draught of Stamina)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters expect V41N to bring in Yuan Shao, Crown General. Pride stops Perse from using her ability and disables most of CasuaL's allies. They also expect Dream Fairy from the sideboard, to answer Perse. The casters say that if Yuan Shao stays on the board, CasuaL has a very bad time.
CasuaL has a second Verdigris Decree available. It suppresses an ally and gives another ally plus two attack, which combines well with Draught of Stamina and Second Wind.

games.summary: CasuaL wins — Perse controls Ranger Strides, then Liu Bei and Second Wind deal 16 damage

beats.text: V41N opens with Beseech the Winds and puts Ranger Strides into play on turn one, so the Mad Hatter cannot hit it. The casters say the key card in this mirror is CasuaL's Perse: when another unit becomes distant, she can become distant too, and she rests to suppress an ally, item or weapon.

CasuaL puts Perse and an Inert Sword into play and removes the Mad Hatter. V41N uses Skirting Step and Backstep to keep his champion distant and digs with Fairy Whispers, but his half of the deck that gives distant does not find any ally to attack with.

V41N uses Tariff Ring during CasuaL’s recollection phase to tax attacks. CasuaL makes Liu Bei distant, gives him additional range with Ranger Strides and attacks for eight. Second Wind wakes Liu Bei for eight more damage and the win.

games.summary: CasuaL wins — Second Wind lets Perse stop a lethal attack, then Cheshire Cat, the champion and Liu Bei finish the match

beats.text: V41N plays Concealed Marksman and Dream Fairy. Ranger Strides makes the Marksman a major threat whenever it becomes distant, while Perse gives CasuaL a way to suppress it.

CasuaL cannot go past level 0, so he must hold cards to make Perse distant each turn. He uses Skirting Step and Evasive Maneuvers to make Perse distant and suppress the Concealed Marksman, and plays Enfeebling Orb to deny V41N more interaction. A Cheshire Cat and an Inert Sword start to push damage onto V41N.

V41N threatens lethal with an eight-damage Mad Hatter attack. CasuaL digs with Backstep, then uses Second Wind to wake Perse and suppress Mad Hatter. He still holds Cry for Help as further interaction.
Cheshire Cat attacks for three and CasuaL’s champion adds pressure. Liu Bei comes down with a distant enabler to supply the finishing damage, giving CasuaL the match 2-0.

matches.round: Round 11 (Day 2) — Fire Diao Chan aggro against Fire Aetherwing Diana, with a Top 8 spot at stake

players.name: DinkyDane
players.deck: Fire Diao Chan aggro (Firebloom Flourish, Fanatical Devotee, Fractal of Sparks, Searing Rebuke, Scathing Seminary, Everflame Staff, Smoke Bombs)

players.name: DJNoVa
players.deck: Fire Aetherwing Diana (Phantom Monarchs-powered build: Aether charges, Manaflare Barrage, Ignition Draw, Flash Grenade, Charge the Soul, Flickering Cinder, Palvor Sword)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters think DinkyDane will bring in Safeguard Amulet and Crystallized Destiny to survive big hits, and they also like Staggering Strike for the extra three damage in the matchup. They warn that DJNoVa's many small, cheap damage sources can pop Crystallized Destiny before it reaches seven damage.
The casters say DJNoVa has few cards to swap in a fire mirror. They name Ignis Deus and a few Dissuading cards as the likely changes.

games.summary: DJNoVa wins — a huge Aether charge turn and a Flash Grenade stop DinkyDane's Searing Rebuke

beats.text: DinkyDane levels to Diao Chan and plays Firebloom Flourish before turn two, then plays a Fanatical Devotee with exactly four influence. With the Diao Chan class bonus on, the attacks deal extra damage and DJNoVa takes damage from Fractal of Sparks and the board.

DJNoVa plays Manaflare Barrage for three memory to deal two damage to every unit except his champion, then Ignition Draw to look at six cards and banish up to two Aether charges. The Aether ring fills, and Charge the Soul and other Aether charges add small damage sources that DinkyDane cannot easily stop.

DinkyDane keeps four Glimmer counters and sets up Scathing Seminary and Smoke Bombs. The casters count that DinkyDane needs a Searing Rebuke and a way to survive the Aether ring damage. DJNoVa answers with Backstep and Flash Grenade, which cancels every point of damage from Searing Rebuke, and he wins at exact damage.

games.summary: DJNoVa wins — he sends the final attack through a Tariff Ring and a Flickering Cinder is exact lethal

beats.text: DinkyDane is on the play and must win this game to keep his Top 8 hopes (he and CasuaL are the last two European players in the race). His hand has no Fractal and no Firebloom Flourish. He draws Fiery Interference and holds a Glowering Conflagration, and the casters worry that he is short of cheap spells.

DJNoVa uses Ignition Draw each turn, but finds only one Aether charge from six cards. The casters explain that Diana's range is an inherited effect, so an Inert Sword attack also gets range and extra damage. He plays Palvor Sword and Inert Sword, and a Blazing Throw is a surprising card in the deck.

DinkyDane tries to stay alive with a Safeguard Amulet and Crystallized Destiny and a Tariff Ring that taxes DJNoVa's attack. He puts two Glimmer counters on his champion, so DJNoVa must play around Searing Rebuke.

DJNoVa uses Aetheric Calibration and decides to send it, whatever DinkyDane holds. Flickering Cinder, a one-cost fast guard that also deals one damage, is exactly lethal after the Tariff Ring tax. The casters say DinkyDane could not have won next turn even with Searing Rebuke.

matches.round: Round 12 (final Swiss round, Day 2) — Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia against Wind Tristan, a Top 8 spot at stake

players.name: DuckHats
players.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (turbo Seiryuu build: The Looking Glass, two Turbo Charge, Backup Charger, Dream Fairy, Aesan Protector, Reclaim, Displace, Regal Inquisition, Harness Lightning, Byakko's Command, Seiryuu's Command)

players.name: Dragowil
players.deck: Wind Tristan (defensive build: Zephyr, Sadi, Dungeon Guide, Incapacitate, Ensnaring Fumes, Veiling Breeze, Slice and Dice, Mastermind Scheme, Windwalker Boots, Innervate Agility)

matches.result: Draw, 1-1 (Dragowil wins game 1, DuckHats wins game 2, the round times out before game 3)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters expect Dragowil to bring in cards against a turbo Seiryuu: Terra and Safeguard Amulet, Regal Inquisition, Heavenly Guide and Blanche, Sheltering Saint. They say Heavenly Guide lets Dragowil keep his influence and answer the opponent's Dungeon Guide.

DuckHats adds a scepter to his material deck for the Incapacitate fight. The casters say this is the only change they see. They add that DuckHats must play much faster, because game 1 took more than 40 minutes.

games.summary: Dragowil wins — Slice and Dice at 22 preparation counters takes out the Seiryuu

beats.text: DuckHats plays The Looking Glass and Turbo Charge into Backup Charger on turn one, then Baby Green Slime and Forest Cake for an influence game. Dream Fairy hits Dragowil's Ominous Shadows. Dragowil answers with Fairy Whispers and holds Incapacitate and Winbless Lookout.

Dragowil levels Tristan and uses Zephyr in response to the Dream Fairy trigger. The Aesan Protector leaves play, so the trigger fizzles. He also plays Windwalker Boots and a Dungeon Guide to count towards a Shadowstrike line, which can reach about 25 damage at level two.

DuckHats plays Displace on the Dungeon Guide and holds up Regal Inquisition (he has three in hand across the game), Innervate Agility and Ensnaring Fumes. He gets one Regal Inquisition to resolve and takes an Ensnaring Fumes away from Dragowil. The casters say Dragowil's stolen Veiling Breeze and spare Ensnaring Fumes make it hard for DuckHats to flip the Seiryuu safely.

Dragowil plays Mastermind Scheme for a free play with Innervate Agility, then Sadi and Assassin's Ripper, and builds 22 preparation counters on Tristan. His redirect keeps Seiryuu attacks on his Ominous Shadows. DuckHats had expected an attack at his face. Dragowil instead hits the Seiryuu with a prepared Slice and Dice for 12 damage and removes it. Veiling Breeze only protects a champion, so DuckHats cannot recover.

games.summary: DuckHats wins — Harness Lightning and Byakko's Command wake the Seiryuu for 10 damage twice with seconds left on the clock

beats.text: Dragowil reveals Ensnaring Fumes on the first Windmill Engineer. DuckHats plays Stifling Trap and Reclaim returns the Windmill Engineer to hand, so the Stifling Trap fizzles. Dragowil plays Candlelight Hourglass, Sadi and Windwalker Boots to build preparation counters, and DuckHats puts out an Aesan Protector.

DuckHats plays Scout the Land, Baby Green Slime and Forest Cake for card draw and influence, and keeps the pressure on. Dragowil, who plays safe, has only two-cost answers and cannot replay Sadi or Stifling Trap with his low influence, and the game swings in DuckHats's favour.

DuckHats uses Displace on the Dungeon Guide to reach level three and flip Seiryuu with a Regal Inquisition in hand. Dragowil has an Ensnaring Fumes in memory, which he cannot play, and no Incapacitate. DuckHats chooses not to attack and passes with a full hand, then draws more cards with Purifying Thurible and a Dungeon Guide.

With seconds left in the round, DuckHats plays Regal Inquisition (hitting nothing), then Harness Lightning for plus four power on the Seiryuu and Byakko's Command for a buff counter. He wakes the Seiryuu and deals 10 damage twice, which is lethal. The clock runs out before game 3, so neither player concedes and they take the draw.

matches.round: Top 8 — Quarterfinal (untimed): Water Aetherwing Diana against Water Diao Chan fractals

players.name: Fallinbuu14
players.deck: Water Aetherwing Diana (aggro: Cheshire Cat, Inert Sword, Ranger Strides, Krustallan Archer, Frostsworn Paladin, Aquamirage Whisper, Carpsong Coda, Take Aim, Weaving Manastream, Backup Charger, Captivating Opulence)

players.name: TeamTrueCaban
players.deck: Water Diao Chan fractals (Fractal of Insight, Fractal of Intrusion, Fractal of Refreshment, Fractal of Snow, Shimmering Refraction, Refracting Missile, Burst Asunder, Throne-Keeper Bullfrog, Frostsworn Paladin, Acquiescing Rejection, Spalling Cleanse, Tariff Ring)

sideboardNotes.text: Cabin brings in Nullifying Lantern, which makes every card in Fallen Buu's graveyard a norm card and turns off Carpsong Coda. The casters also expect a second Song of Frost, since Cabin's list has only one Spalling Cleanse in the main deck and none in the side.

The casters expect Fallen Buu to adjust his distant enablers and Aether charges, because the deck needs a precise balance. They note that Fallen Buu already plays a Bauble of Scarcity in the material deck, and that Cabin has two non-water baubles there.

games.summary: Fallen Buu wins — Cheshire Cat on turn one cannot be removed, then Smoke Bombs make Carpsong Coda lethal

beats.text: Fallen Buu is on the play and plays Cheshire Cat on turn one with an Inert Sword. Cabin cannot remove the Cat, and its three damage each turn is the pressure he never answers. Cabin draws two with Unmake Duality, sacrificing the Looking Glass, and has Acquiescing Rejection ready.

Cabin builds fractals slowly: Fractal of Snow, Fractal of Intrusion (which looks at Fallen Buu's memory), Spalling Cleanse for recovery and a Throne-Keeper Bullfrog. He uses Tariff Ring and Shimmering Refraction to hold back Fallen Buu's allies, but he is out of actions and takes eight damage early.

Fallen Buu levels Diana, uses floating memory for Krustallan Archer and Languid Toadtroll, and holds Carpsong Coda. If he draws a second Coda, it is over. Cabin uses the Bullfrog and Tariff Ring to waste two damage. Fallen Buu then plays Smoke Bombs, which turns off the Bullfrog's intercept, and Carpsong Coda and the Cheshire Cat deal lethal.

games.summary: Cabin wins — Acquiescing Rejection stops Fallen Buu's distant play, then a sixth fractal and Burst Asunder

beats.text: Cabin is on the play and plays a traditional fractal build-out with Nullifying Lantern in the side. Acquiescing Rejection denies Fallen Buu a card and the distant he needs. Fallen Buu ends his turn with Backstep for distant, and Cabin gets a free build-out turn.

Fallen Buu pushes damage with Charge the Soul and Aquamirage Whisper, and plays Krustallan Archer and Frostsworn Paladin. Take Aim, a two-cost four-damage card, brings Cabin close to lethal: he takes 12 damage in one turn, and Cabin goes hands down with no defense.
Cabin plays Enfeebling Orb to tax Fallen Buu's hand, then plays a sixth fractal and exhausts two more with Shimmering Refraction. He pays four more for Burst Asunder, and it deals lethal damage.

games.summary: Fallen Buu wins — a very long game decided at the last point of damage; a Frostsworn Paladin finishes after Cabin's Burst Asunder falls one short

beats.text: Fallen Buu is on the play again and plays Cheshire Cat with Inert Sword on turn one. Cabin has Zhang Jiao, Way of Peace in hand to recover four, and he fractures the Inert Sword with Fracturize. A Frostsworn Paladin intercepts and kills the Cat with a retaliate, and the Ranger Strides plan is gone.

Fallen Buu keeps replacing his threats with Krustallan Archer, Frostsworn Paladin and Aquamirage Whisper, and Weaving Manastream gives free floating memory. Cabin answers with Acquiescing Rejection and Enfeebling Orb, and uses Shimmering Refraction and Flash Grenade to keep the Archer off the board. Cabin plays Nullifying Lantern and Tariff Ring and heals with Zhang Jiao.

Both players dig for the last points of damage with Captivating Opulence, Backup Charger, Crystalline Mirror, Prismspire Scepter and Smoke Bombs. Fallen Buu uses Ranger Strides to give Diana range four and Cabin fracturizes the Palvor Sword in response. Cabin resolves two Burst Asunder in one turn, but Fallen Buu answers with Refreshing Charge to recover three each time.

Cabin has eight Fantasia allies for Captivating Opulence and puts 17 damage on Fallen Buu. The casters think he fires too early: he does not target the Frostsworn Paladin, and the card he draws is a Fractal, not the lethal card. Fallen Buu's Frostsworn Paladin comes in for three and ends the game.

matches.round: Top 4 — Semifinal (untimed): Water Genbu against Fire Aetherwing Diana

players.name: Superior
players.deck: Water Guo Jia / Genbu (undefeated all event: Fractal of Rain, Tidestone Bovine, Frostsworn Paladin, Resonating Fugue, Strategem of Myriad Ice, Unbroken Mustang, Fracturize, Song of Frost, Safeguard Amulet, Tariff Ring)

players.name: DJNoVa
players.deck: Fire Aetherwing Diana (Cheshire Cat, Ranger Strides, Staggering Strike, Burning Aethercharge, Ignition Draw, Manaflare Barrage, Flash Grenade, Flickering Cinder, Singeing Leap, Quickdraw Piercer, Ashwound Shot)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters expect Superior to change his material deck: Beastbond Boots over Tabula of Salvage, and maybe Smoke Bombs. They say the Boots need animals on the board, and Superior did not flip Genbu in game 1.
DJNoVa has few sideboard options in this matchup. The casters name Stifling Trap, a skill that can target Genbu, as the card he brings in against the Genbu deck.
The casters think Superior was afraid of Stifling Trap in game 2 and expect little change. They note Superior has a Song of Frost and two Strategem of Myriad Ice available.

games.summary: DJNoVa wins — a lucky start and a Cheshire Cat from the top of his deck beat the Safeguard Amulet

beats.text: Superior is on the play with Fractal of Rain and Unbroken Mustang in hand. He levels up early and plays Frostsworn Paladin, but refuses to attack so that he takes no damage. DJNoVa passes his first turn, which is normal for a fire Diana deck.

DJNoVa uses a pre-recollection Aether charge to deal three damage to every unit but his champion, which kills the Paladin. Infernal Manastreak and the Diana regalia weapon add more damage. Superior uses Unbroken Mustang to destroy the regalia weapon, and the casters say this removes DJNoVa's best damage source.

Superior has no way to stop DJNoVa's damage this turn and a Safeguard Amulet does not save him. DJNoVa draws the Cheshire Cat from the top of his deck, which adds three damage, and Staggering Strike and a Ranger Strides line add two more for exact lethal.

games.summary: Superior wins — he keeps influence up, wipes the Aether charges with Fracturize and builds a huge graveyard for Strategem of Myriad Ice

beats.text: Superior has Refracting Missile, Seaside Ringleader and Strategem of Myriad Ice and plays a protective game. He holds his influence against the fire deck and uses Refracting Missile to put floating memory in the graveyard. DJNoVa plays Ranger Strides early and draws a card.

DJNoVa puts out Palvor Sword, Infernal Vessel (no recover for Superior) and a Trivier regalia weapon, and his first Aether charges nearly end the game. Superior mills Fracturize, which the casters say may cost him the game. Palvor Sword banishes the graveyard face down, and Superior's water cards are denied.

Superior gets Song of Frost and Resonating Fugue online, flips Genbu (a 9/3 body with Fugue) and holds two Strategems of Myriad Ice. DJNoVa keeps pressure on with Quickdraw Piercer and Singeing Leap, but Superior has the Safeguard Amulet and the answers to each hit. DJNoVa scoops after he sees a Strategem.

games.summary: Superior wins — Fracturize and Tidal Lock deny the early Aether charges; Genbu and Tidestone Bovine mill for a 15-damage threat

beats.text: DJNoVa is on the play and wants a fast start. Superior has two Resonating Fugues, two Gentle Respites and a couple of Fractals of Rain in hand, and plays Tidal Lock at once. The casters ask if DJNoVa can load enough Aether charges.

Superior fractures the Trivier regalia weapon and negates the early Aether charges. DJNoVa plays Ignition Draw and finds only one Aether charge, and he uses Flickering Cinder and Burning Aethercharge to put two damage on Guo Jia.

Superior levels up, flips Genbu and attacks with Tidestone Bovine to mill two cards for quest counters. He mills three more with Fractal of Rain, so a Genbu attack for 15 is lethal. DJNoVa answers with Flash Grenade and Manaflare Barrage, but he has no distant enabler and no Dissuading card to stop the swing. The turtle wins the game.

Result per Omnidex (2-1). Card names are as called by the casters and may contain minor ASR errors; the Trivier regalia weapon could not be matched to a catalog card.

matches.round: Grand Finals (untimed, best of 3) — Water Genbu against Wind Seiryuu, the first Genbu against Seiryuu final

players.name: Superior
players.deck: Water Guo Jia / Genbu (undefeated all event, Canada: Fractal of Polar Depths, Fractal of Rain, Tidestone Bovine, Conniving Plans, Seaside Ringleader, Fabled Sapphire Fatestone, Unbroken Mustang, Fracturize, Strategem of Myriad Ice, Tabula of Salvage)

players.name: Lifdrasyl
players.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (USA, TM32 SoCal turbo-draw build: Turbo Charge, Dungeon Guide, Baby Green Slime, Dream Fairy, Aesan Protector, Windmill Engineer, Stifling Trap, Regal Inquisition, Fabled Azurite Fatestone, Portentous Tanggu, Topsy Decree, Byakko's Command)

matches.result: Superior wins 2-1 — Ascent London champion, finishing the event unbeaten

sideboardNotes.text: The casters expect Superior to add Song of Frost, Excalibur and Frozen Dismissal. Frozen Dismissal helps him fight Lifdrasyl's Dungeon Guide. Superior keeps Tabula of Salvage and Beastbond Boots as options in the material deck.

Lifdrasyl plays no Nullifying Lantern. The casters say that this hurts him against a graveyard deck. His answers are Topsy Decree and a new Phantom Monarchs card that banishes cards from the graveyard.

games.summary: Lifdrasyl wins — a huge influence lead and a full answer for every Genbu step, then Byakko's Command on the Seiryuu for 10 twice

beats.text: Superior builds a graveyard with Fractal of Rain and Fabled Sapphire Fatestone. Three floating memory cards are in his graveyard already, so Strategem of Myriad Ice could hit for 9 to 12. Lifdrasyl stays on Spirit of Wind, plays Turbo Charge and Backup Charger, and takes care of the Tidestone Bovine quickly.

Lifdrasyl banishes five cards from Superior's graveyard with a new Phantom Monarchs card, and uses Baby Green Slime and Stifling Trap on the Censer of Restful Peace and the Unbroken Mustang. He has no Nullifying Lantern, but he accepts one floating memory for Superior to disable the fractals.

Lifdrasyl has about 13 influence and answers each Genbu step: Baby Green Slime, Incapacitate and Regal Inquisition protect his board. He plays Byakko's Command on the Seiryuu for a buff counter (five power) and wakes it up, which makes two swings for 10 damage. Superior has no cards in hand.

games.summary: Superior wins — both players count decks for 35 minutes, and a Fractal of Polar Depths mills Lifdrasyl out

beats.text: Superior goes first and plays carefully with Fractal of Polar Depths, Seaside Ringleader, Primordial Ritual and two Fracturizes for answers. He is behind: Lifdrasyl has a huge hand, with Dream Fairy, Baby Green Slime, Aesan Protector, Stifling Trap and Frozen Dismissal, and Superior can never flip Genbu safely.

Lifdrasyl plays Topsy Decree to banish Superior's graveyard cards, Orb of Sealing and Portentous Tanggu to draw, and Purifying Thurible. He takes a slow line and never needs to flip the Seiryuu. Superior draws a hand of Strategems that he cannot use, and the casters say it looks like Lifdrasyl is winning.

Superior fractures Lifdrasyl's items and mills himself with Conniving Plans, Tidestone Bovine and Fractal of Rain. He plans to mill his own deck out and use Tabula of Salvage, and both players count the cards in each deck. Lifdrasyl holds the Topsy Decree for the Polar Depths, but cannot keep the graveyard down.
Superior passes the turn, and in response to Lifdrasyl's Topsy Decree he pops Fractal of Polar Depths and mills Lifdrasyl out. The casters call it a mill victory that no action could have stopped.

games.summary: Superior wins — Tabula of Salvage puts two Polar Depths on top and the double activation mills Lifdrasyl out

beats.text: Lifdrasyl starts, but the casters say his slow, careful style takes away some of the advantage of going first. Superior finds a Polar Depths early. Tidestone Bovine attacks every turn to mill cards, Tariff Ring and Enfeebling Orb take away Lifdrasyl's interaction, and Lifdrasyl needs Ensnaring Fumes, Dream Fairy and Baby Green Slime to slow the graveyard.

Lifdrasyl removes Superior's Throne-Keeper Bullfrog with an Aesan Protector and a Frostsworn Paladin, and plays Turbo Charge into a Dungeon Guide level and a Seiryuu board. Superior chooses not to flip Genbu and attacks with the Bovine. The casters say that this is the safest, most relaxed way to play.

Superior has 19 cards in the graveyard and 22 in his deck. He mills with Conniving Plans, Seaside Ringleader and the Bovine until his deck is empty. Lifdrasyl holds back his Harness Lightning attack and passes the turn. The casters think he fears a Song of Frost.

Superior plays Tabula of Salvage and puts up to five cards from the graveyard on the bottom of his empty deck, which is also the top. He puts Fractal of Polar Depths on top, and draws it. A Seaside Ringleader gives an extra draw and a second Polar Depths. Both activate, and Lifdrasyl mills for twice the water cards in Superior's graveyard and has no response.

matches.round: Round 1 (Day 1) — World Champion Seiryuu Guo Jia against Wind Gun Diana

players.name: boeboe
players.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (the world champion's dragon deck: Shimmercloak Assassin, Brisk Windtrotter, Primal Whip tech against Tristan, Quicksilver Grail)

players.name: Steve
players.deck: Wind Gun Diana (ally and turbo build: Looking Glass, Unmake Duality, Aesan Protector, Shadow's Twin, Stifling Trap, Dream Fairy)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters expect Taylor to change his plan against an unexpected Diana deck. They expect Calming Breeze to come in (it turns off many ally attacks), and point out that his Primal Whip is already in the list to push Staggering Strike over Calming Breeze against Tristan.
Steve adds Dream Fairy to the main deck and expects to bring in Enfeebling Orb to delay the Seiryuu combo turn. The casters note that the Diana material deck is very tight.

games.summary: Steve wins — a wide ally board, then Shadow's Twin and Umbral Tithe

beats.text: Taylor levels Guo Jia and reveals the Quicksilver Grail as the material deck. Steve plays an Aesan Protector and bounces Windmill Engineers with it. The casters call Steve's deck a surprise, and Taylor does not yet know what he is up against.

Taylor plays Brisk Windtrotter, Stifling Trap hits his Trained Hawk, and Taylor responds with Displace. The Windtrotter enters again and gives the Hawk a buff counter, so the Hawk survives the two damage.

Steve uses Reclaim on a Windmill Engineer for a level and Unmake Duality for two cards. He then goes from Diana level one to level three with Dungeon Guide, and fires Seeker's Rifle and Shadow's Twin into Taylor.

Taylor flips Seiryuu in response to the load, but Steve has a Dream Fairy and Displace ready. Baby Green Slime suppresses the Shadow's Twin for a turn, but Steve returns it, uses Regal Inquisition to check Taylor's hand, and finishes with Punishing Cartridge and Umbral Tithe.

games.summary: boeboe wins — Taylor risks the dragon to clear the Dungeon Guide, then Arcane Blast

beats.text: Taylor starts with Shimmercloak Assassin and a Fairy Whispers to trigger the Fabled Azurite Fatestone. Steve builds a big hand, holds his Regal Inquisition, and plays Silvan Envelopment and Displace on a Windmill Engineer to level fast.

Baby Green Slime suppresses Steve's bullet and Stifling Trap answers a Dream Fairy line. Taylor gets to level three, flips Seiryuu, and attacks the Dungeon Guide instead of Steve's face. This forces Steve to find another way to level.
Taylor plays Tariff Ring to tax Steve's level-up, draws with Incandescent Reliquary, empowers Arcane Blast, and swings with the dragon. Steve does not have the answers and packs it up.

games.summary: boeboe wins — a mis-sequenced Regal Inquisition, then the 40-damage Seiryuu turn

beats.text: Steve plays first and has Unmake Duality on turn one and Enfeebling Orb in his hand. He uses Scout the Land and Baby Green Slime to dig and to suppress Taylor's Focusing Round. Taylor misses Beseech the Winds and Dungeon Guide and cannot turbo.

Steve plays Shadow's Twin before Regal Inquisition, so Taylor's Baby Green Slime suppresses the gun and the Taser Shot is lost for good. Steve holds the Inquisition for the wrong moment, and Taylor gets another turn to level.

Taylor levels with Reclaim, flips Seiryuu and uses Seiryuu's Command and Harness Lightning. A Veiling Breeze from Steve reduces the damage, but two Arcane Blast and empower attacks (nine damage per hit) end the game.
