matches.round: Round 2 (Day 1) — 100% suited ally deck against Wind Tristan

players.name: Arg0naut94
players.deck: Fire 100%-suited ally deck (Ace, King and Queen allies, Five of Spades, Two of Spades, Four of Hearts, Wonderland's Reign, Verita, Trump Set)

players.name: Dragowil
players.deck: Wind Tristan (defensive build: Lost Providence as the divine relic, Sadi, Mastermind Scheme, Shadow Strike, Crystallized Destiny)

matches.result: Dragowil wins (Omnidex lists 2-0; the broadcast shows game 1 ending in a game loss ruling against Dragowil)

sideboardNotes.text: Arg0naut94 goes more aggressive: a Rogue Ace of Hearts, Noir and a couple more Two of Hearts. The casters say Noir with two buff counters and stealth is very hard for Tristan to answer without Stifling Trap or Dream Fairy.
The casters do not know Dragowil's sideboard. They note that Staggering Strike and Stonechance are the common Tristan hate cards, and that Dragowil plays only one Topsy Decree.

games.summary: Game 1 goes to Arg0naut94 by ruling — Dragowil plays out a Tristan win, but a sideboard card is found in his main deck

beats.text: Arg0naut94 starts with Five of Spades (a 1/4 body that wins whether it is on the board or in the graveyard), Four of Hearts and Two of Hearts, and plays Wind Resonance Bauble. Dragowil gets only a Windmill Engineer and no early value.

Two of Spades comes in with fast activation and Trump Set stands ready to redirect an attack. Dragowil finds a defensive wind card and Ensnaring Fumes, but each removal resets the allies' card-ry abilities.

Dragowil reaches six preparation counters and Shadow Dancer, then uses Mastermind Scheme to double the counters to 12 for agility. Arg0naut94 is running out of ways to deal damage and the game ends in Dragowil's favor on the board.

A judge calls the table: a card that belongs in Dragowil's sideboard is in his main deck. The casters say that a deck mistake like this is normally a game loss. Dragowil wins the game on the board but receives the game loss, so game 1 is recorded for Arg0naut94.

games.summary: Dragowil wins — he survives a full suited board, then Verita kills an Ominous Shadow and Shadow Strike closes it

beats.text: Arg0naut94 builds a Noir, Two of Spades, Three of Hearts and Seven of Hearts board and plays Wonderland's Reign (it removes reserve cost from every card-ry ability). Five different reserve costs on the board make a suited flush for six damage.

Dragowil does not level. He goes hands down, draws with Innervate Agility, and uses Sadi to pick off an ally. Arg0naut94 holds Trump Set to redirect the attack and cancels the Sadi plan. Dragowil levels to two, reclaims Sadi, and goes to level three the next turn.

Arg0naut94 uses Noir to pick off Sadi, then activates Verita with ten reserve cost from the graveyard. Five of Spades hits the Ominous Shadow. The casters think this is the first time raw damage has removed one.

Dragowil uses Veiling Breeze and Crystallized Destiny to survive the big suited turn. His Shadow Strike is unblockable, so Arg0naut94 cannot stop it once Trump Set is spent, and the game ends in Dragowil's favor.

matches.round: Round 3 (Day 1) — Wind Tristan against Fire Lraine level 3

players.name: Horinti
players.deck: Wind Tristan (Winbless Lookout, Dungeon Guide, Shadow Reaver, Shadow Strike, Regal Inquisition, Ensnaring Fumes, Tariff Ring)

players.name: APotato
players.deck: Fire Lraine level 3 (Sword Saint's Vow, Inert Sword, Clarent Reimagined, Runeblade, Heavenly Guide, Cheshire Cat, Rending Flames)

matches.result: Horinti wins 2-0 (game 2 awarded by a deck list ruling)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters talk about Crystallized Destiny as the main anti-Tristan card, since most Shadow Strikes deal more than seven damage. They also like Regal Inquisition to strip Shadow Strikes and see Staggering Strike and Stonechance as the usual hate cards. The game 2 sideboard was never played, because of the ruling below.

games.summary: Horinti wins — a near-perfect Tristan start, then a late Runeblade comeback from APotato falls just short

beats.text: Horinti plays first and gets two Winbless Lookouts, a Reclaim and a Dungeon Guide level. He chooses agility over a preparation counter to get a card back at the end of the turn. APotato's early Three of Hearts and Library Witch are cleared and APotato loses a Dungeon Guide on the level-two turn.

APotato plays Cheshire Cat with an Inert Sword. Horinti uses Tariff Ring (APotato must put the cards down) and then Ensnaring Fumes, so the Cat is bounced and Lraine's Blademaster on-kill trigger is blanked. Horinti reaches level three with Shadow Reaver, two Ominous Shadows and a hand full of cards.

Horinti uses Regal Inquisition and sees two Rending Flames in APotato's hand. APotato answers with Resolute Stand, so Horinti's Shadow Strike deals eight and not lethal, and he discards the Rending Flames. Heavenly Guide comes down to gain influence for APotato.

APotato builds Sword of Shadows, Clarent and Runeblade with Hone by Fire for extra damage. Runeblade with the Crux Knight wakes his attacker over and over by sacrificing swords, and APotato pushes Horinti's life very low. Horinti still has Sadi, Shadow Claw and preparation counters, and wins the game just in time.
A judge call follows the game: APotato's deck list shows the Lraine Spirit Ruler champion and not the Crux Knight variant he played. The judges keep the game 1 result.

games.summary: Game 2 awarded to Horinti — a game loss for APotato's incorrect deck list

beats.text: The judges give APotato a game loss for the deck list error, so there is no game 2 or 3. The casters say that both deck lists are close enough that a wrong Lraine champion is an easy mistake, but the penalty stands.

matches.round: Round 4 (Day 1) — Fire Merlin against Water Guo Jia / Genbu

players.name: EnderZone
players.deck: Fire Merlin (King Slayer level 3: Sacred Engulfment, Incarnate Majesty, Ghost of Pendragon, Looking Glass, Inert Sword, Nimue's Cursed Torch, Reprogram)

players.name: Alisaris
players.deck: Water Guo Jia / Genbu (Fractal of Polar Depths, Tidestone Bovine, Seaside Ringleader, Throne-Keeper Bullfrog, Spalling Cleanse, Resonating Fugue)

matches.result: Draw, 1-1 (EnderZone wins game 1, Alisaris wins game 2, game 3 times out)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters expect Nimue's Cursed Torch and Reprogram as a way to remove Genbu, and look at Protect Her At All Costs and Fluffy Shopkeep as protection. They like Sacred Engulfment: a one-cost exalted fire card that banishes fire cards from the graveyard to empower four plus one for each.
Alisaris has few unusual sideboard cards. Topsy Decree is an odd choice for Genbu because it is hard to imbue, but it can lower the number of cards milled by Fractal of Polar Depths.
Alisaris brings in Frozen Dismissal, which he uses at once on EnderZone's Dungeon Guide to slow down the level-up.

games.summary: EnderZone wins — Sacred Engulfment puts out Incarnate Majesty, then Fireball

beats.text: EnderZone uses Three of Hearts and a Liminal Guide, levels Lraine and plays Inert Sword, and plays Distortion regalia through Looking Glass. Alisaris answers with Throne-Keeper Bullfrog, Frostsworn Paladin and a Tidestone Bovine to build floating memory.

Alisaris plays Fractal of Polar Depths and Tidal Lock (in response to a Ghost of Pendragon) to stay in the game. Seaside Ringleader and the Fabled Sapphire Fatestone move Guo Jia toward the flip, and Alisaris reaches 10 quest counters.

EnderZone plays Sacred Engulfment: with two fire cards banished he empowers six, goes to level three, and puts out Incarnate Majesty with a free Majestic Spirit. Alisaris flips Genbu and uses Resonating Fugue (a 9/3 Genbu), but does not take down the Spirit.
Alisaris takes 14 and cannot stop the next attacks. Spalling Cleanse recovers three, but EnderZone responds with a Fireball. He holds a second Fireball in hand, so this one is lethal.

games.summary: Alisaris wins — a huge buffed board behind Genbu; EnderZone scoops to start game 3

beats.text: EnderZone has Protect Her At All Costs, Fluffy Shopkeep and a Dungeon Guide in memory. Alisaris sends a Seaside Ringleader and Frostsworn Paladin early, and a Throne-Keeper Bullfrog stops most damage. EnderZone loses a Ghost of Pendragon to the Dungeon Guide level.

Another Sacred Engulfment banishes five fire cards (empower nine) for a free Incarnate Majesty. A Majestic Spirit comes back again and again with Resolute Stand, and Alisaris cannot target it because it has spell shroud.

Alisaris uses a Primordial Ritual, Seaside Ringleaders and Heaven's Favored to put buff counters on everything he plays: a 3/7 Bullfrog, a 3/9 turtle and a Tideholder Claymore. Refracting Missile and Tidestone Bovine clear the Spirit. He holds three Fractals of Polar Depths and a Strategem of Myriad Ice.

EnderZone holds up Topsy Decree to protect against Strategem of Myriad Ice and uses Sudden Steel, Song of Frost and Reprogram, but he is facing a board he cannot attack through. With six minutes left in the round, EnderZone scoops to start game 3 and play for a win.

games.summary: Draw — the round times out before either player can close

beats.text: Alisaris uses Frozen Dismissal on EnderZone's Dungeon Guide, so EnderZone cannot level fast. Seaside Ringleader and Tidestone Bovine give Alisaris pressure, and the Bovine mills a Liminal Guide.

The players are in extra turns. Alisaris needs Polar Depths, Strategem of Myriad Ice and Resonating Fugue for a finish, but EnderZone's Fireball on the Bovine breaks the line. Both players accept a draw.

matches.round: Round 5 (Day 1) — Water Guo Jia / Genbu against Fire Vanitas (horse and taxes), table one

players.name: Superior
players.deck: Water Guo Jia / Genbu (two Fractal of Rain imbued, Fractal of Polar Depths, Strategem of Myriad Ice, Seaside Ringleader, Resonating Fugue, Spalling Cleanse, Tidestone Bovine)

players.name: OkaygeBusiness
players.deck: Fire Vanitas (Domino Rex, horse-and-taxes: Dungeon Guide, Impact Hammer, Searing Rebuke, Extortion Scheme, Brisk Windtrotter, Lavasoul Tiger)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters look at Frozen Dismissal as a card against Vanitas's Dungeon Guide level-up. Superior also adds a second Topsy Decree and a Fractal of Polar Depths line.

OkaygeBusiness adds a second Extortion Scheme and has no Nullifying Lantern. The casters say Lantern or Nullifying Censer would have turned off the graveyard plan, and that he did not expect to face a graveyard deck. In the interview Superior says the matchup is hard for Vanitas because the deck lacks answers for Genbu's negates.

games.summary: Superior wins — OkaygeBusiness has a dream start but Superior's graveyard and Genbu flip take over

beats.text: Superior plays two imbued Fractals of Rain and a Looking Glass draw on turn one, and mills his own deck. OkaygeBusiness levels Vanitas fast with Dungeon Guide, Impact Hammer and a horse, and gets a strong early board.

OkaygeBusiness has Impact Hammer plus Searing Rebuke and the Dungeon Guide for a lethal threat, but he does not take it and uses Seering Rebuke for protection. The casters say it was a gamble: Superior does not have a second Topsy Decree, so he would have been dead.
Seaside Ringleader, Spalling Cleanse and Resonating Fugue give Superior card flow. The fractals give him quest counters, he flips Genbu, and his full graveyard lets him close out the game.

games.summary: Superior wins — Strategem of Myriad Ice with a graveyard full of floating memory

beats.text: OkaygeBusiness plays Lavasoul Tiger (a new addition to the deck) with Brisk Windtrotter buff counters on a Liminal Guide, and Extortion Scheme is ready to suppress an ally. Superior answers with a Throne-Keeper Bullfrog, Frostsworn Paladin and Primordial Ritual.

Superior builds to five quest counters and flips Genbu in response to an attack. He cracks Fractal of Polar Depths to soak up damage and keeps the Strategem in hand while OkaygeBusiness has no cards in hand.

Superior banishes floating memory from the graveyard and plays Strategem of Myriad Ice. Three damage for each banished card clears the board and kills OkaygeBusiness. The casters say a Nullifying Lantern would have saved him.

matches.round: Round 6 (Day 1) — Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia against Fire Slimes, both 4-1

players.name: Sano
players.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (turbo list with two Ensnaring Fumes main, two Veiling Breeze, Inert Agility, Baby Green Slime, Dream Fairy, Stifling Trap)

players.name: sungorio
players.deck: Fire Slimes (Sylvie, Slime Sovereign: Storm Slime, Ethereal Slime, Lustrous Slime, Limitless Slime, Slime King, Baby Red Slime, Covenant of Thorns, Gaia's Blessing)

matches.result: Draw, 1-1 (Sano wins game 1, sungorio wins game 2, game 3 times out)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters find nothing obvious for Sangorio in the sideboard. Spell Shroud Terra and Twilight Slime give his allies spell shroud, but Sono won game 1 on protection and influence and not on spells. Regal Inquisition could help, but is not a clear fit.
With 12 minutes left in the round, both players sideboard again. Sono opens with Thurible and Sangorio plays Covenant of Thorns, Slime King and Stonescale Band.

games.summary: Sano wins — a huge hand outlasts Sangorio's slimes

beats.text: Sangorio opens with Baby Silver Slime and a patient Slime Eruption on a reclaimed Windmill Engineer. Sono plays Looking Glass and Unmake Duality for a big hand. Sono has two Ensnaring Fumes main deck, which he plays so he does not lose mirror matches.

Sono uses Baby Green Slime on Sangorio's Quicksilver Grail trigger so the card under it is lost (Horn of Beastcalling). He keeps the influence advantage with Dungeon Guide and Stifling Trap, and Sangorio's Sylvie level three never gets going.
Sangorio runs out of influence and cannot play his Creative Shock or Cremation Ritual (both cost three). Sono has two Veiling Breezes and a big hand, and Sangorio packs it up.

games.summary: sungorio wins — Slime Kings, Covenant of Thorns and a Seiryuu that never gets going

beats.text: Sono does not level to Guo Jia. He keeps a big hand and uses Thurible during the recollection phase, then uses Baby Green Slime to put an Aesan Protector in play and draw cards. Sangorio sets up with Baby Red Slime and Ethereal Slime.

Sangorio plays Slime King (taunt, and it puts three banished slimes under it when it leaves play) and a second Slime King. Gaia's Blessing and Stonescale Band keep his hand full, and a Storm Slime in hand threatens a large fireball-style hit.

Sono flips Seiryuu and clears the Twilight Slime, then uses Dream Fairy and Displace to remove slimes. Sangorio puts Covenant of Thorns on the Seiryuu and plays Gaia's Songbird. The Seiryuu is removed, and Sono, without allies, cannot stop the slimes.

games.summary: Draw — the round times out with both players still in the game

beats.text: Sono opens with Thurible again and takes a Forest Cake and Scout the Land line. Sangorio goes to Sylvie level one and double Dungeon Guide from level two to three, with Storm Slime, Ethereal Slime and Cremation Ritual in hand.
Sangorio puts a big Ethereal Slime and Lustrous Slime into play and bullies Sono into spending cards. Sono holds two Veiling Breezes and Undeniable Truth for the Storm Slime trigger.

Time is called on Sangorio's turn, so Sono gets one more turn and the game ends with no result. Sono flips Seiryuu to respond to the Quicksilver Grail, but a Baby Green Slime and Veiling Breeze keep both players alive. The casters call it a dead-even match.

matches.round: Round 7 (Day 1) — Fire Diao Chan aggro against Fire Lraine (Clarent, Reimagined), both 4-2

players.name: DinkyDane
players.deck: Fire Diao Chan aggro (Firebloom Flourish, Searing Rebuke, Fractal of Sparks, Ashwick Cremator, Scathing Seminary, Crystallized Destiny, Everflame Staff)

players.name: rexaren
players.deck: Fire Lraine level 3 (Clarent, Reimagined: Crux Knight, Dungeon Guide, Varuckan Acolyte, Spirit Blade: Ascension, Rending Flames, Ghost of Pendragon, Fluffy Shopkeep, Resolute Stand)

sideboardNotes.text: DinkyDane brings in Crystallized Destiny, a card the casters did not expect, to survive a Rending Flames when he would otherwise lose. It is a cleric and tamer skill reaction that he pays for with Glimmer counters.
rexaren looks at a card that stops spell and skill activations from memory. The casters say it would punish the Glimmer counter plan, but note that Rexarion's sideboard is mostly damage prevention.

games.summary: rexaren wins — Clarent, Reimagined and a 14-damage Rending Flames

beats.text: DinkyDane plays first with Firebloom Flourish, Searing Rebuke and Fractal of Sparks. Each prevented damage becomes free damage to the opponent through Searing Rebuke and Fractal. Ashwick Cremator and the no-cards-in-hand trigger add more damage to both champions.

rexaren uses Varuckan Acolyte to remove the Censer of Restful Peace, plays Liminal Guide and Clarent, Reimagined, and drops a Dungeon Guide to reach Lraine level two. Clarent prevents two damage per durability counter, and DinkyDane forces the counters out one at a time.
rexaren finds Spirit Blade: Ascension and Rending Flames. With swords banished it is exactly 14 damage through Searing Rebuke, and DinkyDane has no Dao Chan answer in hand.

games.summary: DinkyDane wins — Crystallized Destiny from memory stops a huge Crux Knight attack

beats.text: DinkyDane starts with Firebloom Flourish again, with both the class bonus and the Diao Chan bonus on, and sets up Fractal of Sparks. Searing Rebuke and Fractal of Sparks hit rexaren for free damage.
rexaren has two Dungeon Guides and a Fluffy Shopkeep, and levels twice to a large life total. Smoke Bombs give DinkyDane's ally stealth, so the Shopkeep cannot intercept.

DinkyDane gets Crystallized Destiny into memory and activates it with a Glimmer counter during rexaren's turn. This prevents the big Crux Knight attack. Rexaren is hands down and has no defense left, and DinkyDane finishes with Vermilion Decree, Grand Crusader's Ring and free damage.

games.summary: DinkyDane wins — he forces out six Clarent durability counters, then Scathing Seminary for unpreventable damage

beats.text: rexaren goes first with Three of Hearts and Fluffy Shopkeep, banishes swords for Sword of Seeking, and plays Fanatical Devotee. DinkyDane's early Searing Rebuke and Fractal of Sparks keep pushing damage through Clarent.

rexaren uses Spirit Blade: Ascension to banish and return Clarent with three fresh counters. He plays Ravenous Pyre and a Dungeon Guide to stay at a comfortable life total, and DinkyDane has to push damage on both turns.

DinkyDane uses Searing Rebuke, Cinder Geyser (four damage), Scepter of Fascination and Crystallized Destiny. After six Clarent durability counters, Smoke Bombs remove the Shopkeep's intercept and Scathing Seminary adds unpreventable damage for the win.

matches.round: Round 8 (final round, Day 1) — Water Diana level 1 allies against Wind Tristan, two friends from Germany and Austria

players.name: Celednb
players.deck: Water Diana (level 1 allies: Krustallan Archer, Frostsworn Paladin, Aquamirage Whisper, Ranger Strides, Inert Sword, Power Sword, Languid Toad Troll, Bobble of Scarcity)

players.name: Asuna
players.deck: Wind Tristan (fully-foiled list: Incapacitate, Stifling Trap, Staggering Strike, Sadi, Shadow Claw, Flash Grenade, Enfeebling Orb)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters expect Asuna to bring in Staggering Strike and Unbroken Mustang (against a water deck), the Obnigation to recover health, and maybe Nocturne's Oblation. They note that Songs of Frost force both players to sacrifice an ally, which would punish a Tristan with only Ominous Shadow tokens.
Celad plays Enfeebling Orb, which the casters think is very strong against a Tristan with so much influence. They say it denies Asuna the chance to pay for his cards.

games.summary: Celednb wins — Krustallan Archer, Ranger Strides and Aquamirage Whisper for exact lethal

beats.text: Celad plays Incapacitate and Enfeebling Orb against a Tristan with a lot of influence, and glimpses two cards for floating memory. A Frostsworn Paladin with a buff counter and a free float starts early damage. Asuna is behind on tempo and damage counters (11).

Asuna uses Dungeon Guide and Stifling Trap from memory to stay in the game, and a Flash Grenade-style reaction to gain cards back at the four-damage threshold. He holds Sadi and does not play it until he sees an ally, which keeps Incapacitate alive.

Celad lines up Ranger Strides (ranged four, five with ranged one), Aquamirage Whisper (six) and Frostsworn Paladin (nine), with two Krustallan Archers and cards with floating memory. Asuna has two influence and two cards in hand, so he cannot respond, and it is exactly lethal.

games.summary: Celednb wins — Enfeebling Orb denies Asuna's plays; Power Sword and Staggering Strike finish

beats.text: Asuna uses Staggering Strike and the Obnigation from his sideboard. He fractures the Censer of Restful Peace to turn on floating memory and runs two Incapacitates, but Enfeebling Orb makes him pay more and an Incapacitate is banished because he cannot pay two more.

Celad forces out Asuna's preparation counters one at a time with Krustallan Archer and attacks. Flash Grenade and Reposition (distant) from Asuna delay the Archer, and Asuna uses Slice and Dice for nine damage with three counters. Celad survives with a damage-prevention reaction.

Asuna has no preparation counters and a low influence. Celad plays Power Sword (banishes a graveyard, two attack) and a Turbo Charge on a Power Cell, uses Tactical Retreat, and attacks with Staggering Strike for five. Asuna packs up.

matches.round: Round 1 (Day 1): Fire Merlin against Water Genbu

players.name: Egg
players.deck: Fire Merlin (Merlin, Kingslayer; Merlin, Memory Thief; Ghosts of Pendragon x2; Fireball; Spirit Blade: Ascension; Sword of Seeking; Drawn Blade; Demolition; Prismatic Edge; Resolute Stand x2; Liminal Guide; Fluffy Shopkeep; Cheshire Cat, Impish Grin)

players.name: Long
players.deck: Water Genbu (Fractal of Rain, Genbu, Tidestone Bovine, Frostsworn Paladin, Refracting Missile, Revitalizing Cleanse, Grand Crusader's Ring, Portentous Tanggu, Conniving Plans, Unbroken Mustang, Snow White, Weiss Queen, Fracturize; a Merlin-style Genbu deck)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters see options in Long's sideboard. They discuss Kongming-style tricks and note that Genbu acts more as a defender than an attacker for Long in this matchup.

games.summary: Egg wins — a Fireball and Sword of Seeking line leaves Long in danger, and he extends the fist

beats.text: Long goes up to level two to deny some floating memory. He does not open Fractal of Rain, so he does not mill as much as the casters expected, and he needs the Tidestone Bovine. The Fugue wincon is in his hand, and the Merlin Egg has already taken one of his other wincons.

Egg gets into a great position about to go to level three, and Long has to double-negate to get value. A compulsory Liminal Guide trigger that was milled off the Fatestone is questioned by the judges.

The casters say Egg is in the danger zone for Long: Fireball comes in for six and Sword of Seeking for three. The casters say this could already be game one if Long has nothing to say. Egg throws the Fireball and Long extends the fist.

games.summary: Long wins — slow, steady Genbu play, with Black Tortoise flickering Paladins and farming influence

beats.text: Long draws first blood with a Liminal Guide and Cremation Ritual, and uses Reprogram on Egg's Cheshire Cat so it cannot attack. The casters say Egg has a lot of options with a Resolute Stand, but cannot cast spells, only skills.

Long goes up to Guo Jia level three, fully discounted because Genbu, Black Tortoise is on board. The casters note that once Genbu hits level three it keeps flickering the Paladin, and a Prismatic Edge with a fire card can do three damage to a three-life Genbu.
Long farms influence and pushes forward cleanly, finally taking out Egg's Merlin. The casters say it was very clean gameplay.

games.summary: Egg wins — Pendragons and a Fireball line, and Long concedes with Genbu gone

beats.text: Long goes second and knows the deck has many allies: Liminal Guides, Fluffy Shopkeeps, a Cheshire Cat. He gets a Frostsworn Paladin and three quest counters. The casters count one Fractal in game three against two in game two, and that the Pelagic Fatestone has not been milled yet.

Egg uses Merlin, Memory Thief to steal memory, and Long ends up with an empty memory. Egg's hand is full of Crux: two Ascensions, a second Ghosts of Pendragon and a Fireball, and the casters say he is not yet going for the lethal line.

Egg puts Spirit Blade: Ascension on the board and plays the Pendragons. The casters count six from the Pendragons and 17 total, one short, but Egg still has cards in hand. Egg throws the Fireball and Long extends the fist, and Egg wins the match 2-1 against one of the best players in Taiwan.

matches.round: Round 2 (Day 1): Astra Arisana against Water Aetherwing Diana

players.name: Aqua
players.deck: Astra Arisana (Astral Zenith star calls, Polaris, Cosmic Bolt, Three Visits, Angelic Channeling, Angel Attendant, Calming Breeze, Gentle Respite, Fracturize, Weaving Manastream, a Sensor)

players.name: HARO
players.deck: Water Aetherwing Diana (Quickstep Treads, Inert Sword, Flash Grenade, Krustallan Archer, Undercurrent Vantage, Charge the Soul, Aether Dilettante, Fracturize, Tariff Ring, Dungeon Guide)

matches.result: Aqua wins 2-0 (going second in both games)

games.summary: Aqua wins — Polaris, a Sensor and three Cosmic Bolts out-glimpse the Aetherwing

beats.text: Aqua explains Astral Zenith: she gets a free star call each turn, where a glimpsed Astra card is activated for free. Three Visits in the opening hand is one of the best glimpses, and Aqua gets Polaris, which is good into aggro.

HARO plays the typical Diana game: a level one deck that gets the weapon out and charges in. He needs to crack the Sensor and cannot, and he has the Inert Sword for three damage. The casters say Polaris makes him less able to commit more allies.

Aqua goes to level three, loses an Angel Attendant and a Beseech, and uses Angelic Channeling to stack the top of the deck. She uses three Cosmic Bolts for a real win, and HARO lets it go. Aqua wins on the draw, which is a surprise against an aggro deck.

games.summary: Aqua wins — HARO has Fracturize but cannot answer Polaris, and Aqua wins again going second

beats.text: HARO throws Charge the Soul or Weaving Manastream as the discard and considers Undercurrent Vantage, depending on his hand. Aqua keeps a Besiege card and a Dungeon Guide. The Angel Attendant, imbued, is another strong card in the matchup.

Aqua banishes the last card in her graveyard to bring out Polaris and uses Calming Breeze to stifle much of the damage. A Fracturize and a Flash Grenade do not help HARO, because he cannot answer the Polaris. The casters say Aqua is losing the Polaris race and passes.
HARO's Aether Dilettante does not make it and the Diana cannot get through. Aqua takes the game and the match 2-0, going second both times. The casters say Arisana is a deck not to be slept on.

matches.round: Round 3 (Day 1): Fire Krux Lorraine against Water Umbra Alice

players.name: RubyXillia
players.deck: Fire Krux Lorraine (Lorraine, Spirit Ruler; Drawn Blade; Sword of Seeking; Prismatic Edge; Ghosts of Pendragon; Spirit Blade: Ascension; Fluffy Shopkeep; Dungeon Guide; Turbo Charge; Incapacitate; Resolute Stand; Regal Inquisition)

players.name: DragonJG
players.deck: Water Umbra Alice, Phantom Monarch (Dynastic Whirlpool mill-out plan, Umbra Sight, Fantasmagoria mastery, Pearl Prayer, Regal Inquisition, Song of Frost, Reflected Blight, Resolute Stand, Void's Cloak, Victor's Tiding, Fluffy Shopkeep)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters note that Void's Cloak, which stops Regal Inquisition, is in DragonJG's side. They also note that Song of Frost comes in as an answer to the three-damage reveals.

games.summary: DragonJG wins — three Dynastic Whirlpools mill RubyXillia out

beats.text: RubyXillia goes to Lorraine level one and brings out the Sword of Seeking. The casters explain the plan against Alice: farm influence and cards, then mill. DragonJG shows Pearl Prayer and Regal Inquisition, which tells RubyXillia this is not the Genbu deck he expects.

DragonJG's Alice starts with two Fantasmagoria counters and takes seven unpreventable damage with the Umbra Sight. RubyXillia brings out the Drawn Blade and reveals fire cards with Prismatic Edge, which deals three damage each turn, but the water cards do not show up.
DragonJG plays another Dynastic Whirlpool and mills up 50 cards. His Regal Inquisition handles RubyXillia's key card, and DragonJG takes game one with three Dynastic Whirlpools.

games.summary: RubyXillia wins — Prismatic Edge pressure and Ghosts of Pendragon force a concession before the whirlpool arrives

beats.text: RubyXillia puts the Drawn Blade out and plays Fluffy Shopkeep, so he can skip the Sword of Peace turn. The casters note Alice has only 22 total life, so a Resolute Stand matters and DragonJG must still take seven damage at Alice level two.

RubyXillia goes to level three with Lorraine, Spirit Ruler and uses the Ghosts of Pendragon to return the Prismatic Edge to the material deck, which draws more. DragonJG pays Pearl Prayer to go down to 10 damage counters again, and a Tariff Ring delays the game.
DragonJG sees that he does not have enough heal and recovery to win and concedes. The casters call it a pressure-based matchup where RubyXillia just needs to present the damage fast.

games.summary: DragonJG wins — he survives with Song of Frost and Resolute Stand and the Umbra Sight draws find the lethal

beats.text: RubyXillia cycles through his deck first, then finds a Dungeon Guide and puts Ruby up to level three. Lorraine, Spirit Ruler tries to find victory. A Turbo Charge starts the turn, and the Ghosts of Pendragon return a card to the material deck for more draws.

DragonJG plays Song of Frost so the three damage does not resolve. Two more Umbra Sights are available in his deck, and he draws five cards, one of them an Umbra Sight, with a Void's Cloak in play. RubyXillia has Spell Shroud against Regal Inquisition.
RubyXillia does not find the Reflected Blight and cannot find lethal. The casters say DragonJG wins around turn 10 with the power of the Dynastic Whirlpool, and he takes the match 2-1.

matches.round: Round 4 (Day 1): Fire Luxem Zander against Fire Ciel Oblation

players.name: Awi
players.deck: Fire Luxem Zander (Lightweaver's Assault, Luxem Sight, Striking Illuminance, Planted Explosive, Topsy Decree, Regal Inquisition, Dungeon Guide, Angelic Channeling)

players.name: Centratus
players.deck: Fire Ciel Oblation (Baleful Oblation, Angelic Channeling, Orb of Sealing, Dungeon Guide, Liminal Guide, Backup Charger)

games.summary: Awi wins — recovery survives Centratus’s double Oblation turn, and Centratus concedes

beats.text: Awi, from Brunei, faces Singapore’s Centratus. Both use Angelic Channeling to prepare advanced-element cards. Centratus’s non-imbued Topsy Decree makes Awi banish an Angelic Channeling from his graveyard.

Awi uses Topsy Decree to disrupt Centratus’s graveyard setup. The casters initially identify Regal Inquisition in Awi’s hand, then correct it to Lightweaver’s Assault. Centratus struggles to build enough influence for his double Oblation plan.

Awi pressures with Planted Explosive and Striking Illuminance. Centratus plays two Baleful Oblations around Awi’s Incapacitate and uses Feu Awakening. Awi survives with recovery from Luxem Sight revealed by Lightweaver’s Assault and his Serene release. Centratus concedes after exhausting his Oblations.

games.summary: Awi wins — Centratus starts fast but cannot find a second Oblation, and Lightweaver's Assaults finish

beats.text: Awi uses Angelic Channeling to set up Lightweaver’s Assault and Luxem Sight. Centratus reaches level three with Dungeon Guide and threatens Baleful Oblation and Feu Awakening.

Centratus deals 15 with Baleful Oblation, then uses Feu Awakening. Once it resolves, Awi uses Topsy Decree’s spellshroud against the two Mirage’s Grave triggers. Centratus keeps attacking, forcing Awi’s Serene release, but Awi reaches his Luxem cards and recovers.

Centratus reaches six omens and tries Feu Awakening again. Awi answers the resulting Mirage’s Grave triggers with Topsy Decree’s spellshroud and graveyard banishment. With Centratus out of cards, Awi finishes with Lightweaver’s Assault to win 2-0.

matches.sourceNote: Southeast Asia Nationals Day 1, Round 4. Full captions at 276:16–281:52 identify Awi (Brunei, Fire Luxem Zander) and Centratus (Singapore, Fire Ciel); captions also render their names as “AI” and “Sentus”. Omnidex event 56265 round 4 pairing 10, player countries and registered decks corroborate both identities and Awi’s 2-0 win.

matches.round: Round 5 (Day 1): Wind Razor Gale Arisana against an arcane Advent deck

players.name: marupiyo
players.deck: Wind Razor Gale Arisana (Razor Gale x3, Essence Crucible, a speed potion, Tempest Downfall, Veiling Breeze, Fairy Whispers, Dream Fairy, Nullifying Mirror, Mnemonic Charm, Careful Study, Fracturize, Tri-Castles of Lucenia in the side)

players.name: eoe
players.deck: Arcane Advent deck (Advent of the Stormcaller, Arcane Elemental, Fortuitous spirit, Cosmic Bolt-style arcane cards, Dream Fairy, Veiling Breeze, Fracturize; plays a lot of arcane cards and wants to reach a high level and dump them)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters see Tri-Castles of Lucenia in the side and note that eoe's deck has no Scatter Essences. They say it is really a game of whether he can kill fast enough, and that Fractal cards are not what the Advent deck wants against Razor Gale.

games.summary: marupiyo wins — a double Razor Gale and Essence Crucible combination ends the game with three minutes left

beats.text: The casters say Razor Gale Arisana is making a comeback after good showings at Nats and EU Nats, though many think the deck is falling off. marupiyo plays his first Razor Gale, a four-cost Fantasia that sticks, and then a second one, and eoe has no answer.

eoe looks for the Advents and Arcane Elementals. He gets to level eight and banishes two arcane cards to hit for 10, drawing two cards, but marupiyo keeps a Veiling Breeze. The casters say Arcane Elemental swings for seven and that Advent would take eoe to level 20 to 30 for a large Erratic.

marupiyo uses a speed potion for Agility three to draw three cards and play fast-speed cards, and fires a Tempest Downfall when the Essence Crucible comes out. With a block of two prevented, more Fairy Whispers and the Razor Gale triggers, marupiyo takes game one.

games.summary: marupiyo wins — eoe's Advent deck is too slow with low influence, and the Razor Gales punish every card

beats.text: marupiyo uses Mnemonic Charm to put cards down so he can level up next turn, and he draws an extra card. The casters note that a careful study that banishes an arcane card fuels his level ups, so it is a positive. The Razor Gale deck punishes opponents without defensive lines.

eoe has only seven influence after recollection, which is extremely low, and a Careful Study in hand that he cannot cast for free. He uses a Nullifying Mirror and tries to keep up, but the casters say he has no other game plan.
marupiyo has the Crucible and the potion, and the casters say that if he finds the Razor Gales eoe just dies. eoe's only out is to be faster, and he is not. marupiyo wins 2-0.

matches.round: Round 6 (Day 1): Fire Slimes against Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia

players.name: Zabauu
players.deck: Fire Slimes (Storm Slime, Baby Green Slime, Ghastly Slime, Slime Eruption, Beastbond Boots, Benediction Angel, Dungeon Guide, Backup Charger, Unyielding spell shroud tools; the casters call it the lesser, younger cousin of Seiryuu's allies plan)

players.name: Raypig
players.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (Su Azure Dragon, Seiryuu's Command, Byakko's Command, Dungeon Guide, Imperial Countermeasures, Excalibur, Zephyr, Crystallized Destiny, Fairy Whispers; Beseeched Fatestone)

games.summary: Zabauu wins — he patiently gathers slimes, keeps the Beastbond Boots for protection and swarms the Azure Dragon

beats.text: Raypig farms resources because he cannot stop the dragon. The casters say Seiryuu won Ascent Taipei last year before Radiant Origins. Raypig brings out the Su Azure Dragon with a Seiryuu's Command and Byakko's Command 32-damage combo, which Zabauu cannot stop except for the Beastbond Boots.

Zabauu keeps an arcane slime in hand on purpose. He uses Baby Green Slime to take out Raypig's effects, a Windshear Bringer, and the on-death of a Storm Slime. The casters note that the Azure Dragon has four buff counters and an 8/16 body, but the Boots protect Zabauu from the damage.

Zabauu plays Innervate Agility to return the Gatri, Heaven's Favor to Raypig's material deck and stares down ten allies. The casters call it a patient play: gather all the friends and go into the dragon. Slime Eruption is a skill, which the casters forgot. Zabauu takes game one.

games.summary: Zabauu wins — a Benediction Angel start and a double Storm Slime line for 22 damage

beats.text: Raypig hopes for a start as strong as last game, with the Besiege Fatestone, but it does not happen immediately. Zabauu has been denied a draw for the level two earlier, and this time he guarantees it. A Benediction Angel and a quick Ethereal Slime come down.

Zabauu uses a Dungeon Guide to get level three with the Storm Slime on board. He needs a specific number of cards to flip the Storm Slime, and the casters note he needed three Storm Slimes to close the previous game but could not find them.

A Storm Slime deals six and itself attacks for three, so nine damage and a double Storm Slime line deals 22. Zabauu wins 2-0, and the casters say this slime deck will take the rest of the nationals by storm.

matches.round: Round 7 (Day 1): Water allies against Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia

players.name: Joel
players.deck: Water allies (Nia, Mistveiled Scout; Snow White, Weiss Queen; Corhazi Trapper; Dream Fairy; Dungeon Guide; Stifling Trap; Crowd Guard Slash, a card never seen on stream before; Fluffy Shopkeep; Inert Sword)

players.name: NeptuneI
players.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (Beseeched Fatestone, Resolute Stand, Veiling Breeze, Nullifying Mirror, Frostbind, Seiryuu's Command, Byakko's Command, Aquafer Senkall, Parasel; a Neptuno original build with a panda)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters say there is not much in NeptuneI's sideboard to change the matchup. They note he may have thought Joel was on water Diana instead of water allies, which could have affected his judgment until it was confirmed.

games.summary: Joel wins — he ignores the panda, plays around Resolute Stand and a Crowd Guard Slash turns the game

beats.text: NeptuneI uses the Beseeched Fatestone to go up to level one in a steep way, flips the panda because he materialized two things this turn, and plays Parasel to draw into memory. A Resolute Stand goes on the panda.

Joel ignores the panda, which the casters say is probably correct for an aggro deck, and Nia names a card to reveal. He plays Dream Fairy and Corhazi Trapper and keeps a Stifling Trap in play. The casters see he has a Crowd Guard Slash in hand, a three-power attack that gains plus three when the opponent has a taunt.
NeptuneI thinks about a Nullifying Mirror and Veiling Breeze but there is not much he can do. Crowd Guard Slash goes crazy against the panda and the casters say he is lost. Joel takes game one.

games.summary: Joel wins — NeptuneI gets the Seiryuu out too slowly, and Crowd Guard Slash wins a second time

beats.text: NeptuneI is far away from getting the Seiryuu onto the board and does not go for quest counters. Five more quest counters would let him flip the dragon, but he is then in Frostbind range with five cards in hand.

Joel plays Nia, who reveals NeptuneI's cards, and keeps a Snow White that costs seven or eight cards. The casters call the Dream Fairy a simple two-three with true sight; an ally player wants as many two-threes as possible. A Dungeon Guide is top-decked.

NeptuneI goes for the Veiling Breeze and the Nullifying Mirror is tapped in response. Crowd Guard Slash takes game two, and the casters tell chat to buy it. Joel wins 2-0, and the casters note that just one card of influence matters in a game this close.

matches.round: Round 8 (Day 1): Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia against Fire Arthur aggro

players.name: Abbey
players.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (Dream Fairy, Seiryuu's Command, Byakko's Command, Smoke Bombs, Lost Providence, Dungeon Guide, Beseeched Fatestone, Stifling Trap, Incapacitate; Blanche in the side)

players.name: Microcanthus
players.deck: Fire Arthur aggro (Poisoned Dagger, Memorite Blade, Impact Hammer, Demolition, Kindle, Molten Echo, March Hare, Tweedle Dum, Aesan Protector, Blazing Throw, Mad Hatter-style rabbit tricks; assassin cards that are mostly spells)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters discuss Abbey's side: Incapacitate is good because it stops Veiling Breeze and Resolute Stand, but it is hard to know what to remove for it. They say Blanche is hard to play in the matchup and the timing matters.

games.summary: Abbey wins — Dream Fairy bounces Microcanthus's allies and the Seiryuu's Command arrives with no Veiling Breeze to stop it

beats.text: Abbey opens with a Dream Fairy on turn one, which the casters call the best opening against a fire aggro deck. Microcanthus is blown back into memory, and his Demolition hits the Dream Fairy only with a Tweedle Dum answer. He has two allies that are Dream Fairied.

Microcanthus is hands down with no allies to clear the board, and most of his cards are spells that the Seiryuu's spell protection stops. He attacks with the Memorite Blade and needs another seven damage, but he is behind on influence and cannot commit.

Abbey has a Seiryuu's Command for the recollection phase and flips the Seiryuu with the Lost Providence and Ranger-style influence. The casters say the idea is to end the game as soon as possible. Abbey takes game one.

games.summary: Abbey wins — Smoke Bombs, Byakko's Command and a patient Seiryuu beat the March Hare loop

beats.text: Dream Fairy is in the opening hand once again. Microcanthus keeps spamming the Poisoned Dagger and Kindle combo to chip away. The casters say the difference this game is that Abbey realizes he is behind and plays patiently, while Microcanthus cannot go further down on influence.

Microcanthus kindles to activate the weapon and brings back the March Hare with its effect, using Molten Echo for extra damage and putting Abbey up to eight damage. The casters say some people just have an affinity for a certain deck.

Abbey draws Blazing Throw and uses Smoke Bombs, draws a card, and goes for a Byakko's Command with the dragon. Microcanthus cannot keep up and the casters say a wall in front of an ally deck is hard to deal with. Abbey wins 2-0 while Microcanthus needs to win his last round for Day 2.

matches.round: Round 9 (final Swiss round of Day 1) — win-and-in for both players: Astra Aetherwing Diana against Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia

players.name: megalobana
players.deck: Astra Aetherwing Diana (Aquamirage Whisper, Backup Charger, Quickstep Treads, Krustallan Archer, Dungeon Guide, Fracturize, Weaving Manastream, Byakko's Command; a build that looks like water Diana but goes up to level three and dumps floating memory)

players.name: NeptuneI
players.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (Beseeched Fatestone, Displace, Dungeon Guide, Relic Query, Seiryuu's Command, Byakko's Command, Gatri, Heaven's Favored; Neptuno was 6-1 before the round)

matches.result: NeptuneI wins 2-1 per Omnidex (the VOD shows game 1 and the start of game 2)

games.summary: NeptuneI wins — a Displace on the Dungeon Guide takes him to Guo Jia level three while megalobana's Diana takes half his life but cannot close

beats.text: The casters call the match a win-and-in game for both players. megalobana plays the Astra Diana list and pushes in four damage with an Archer, taking Neptuno almost to half his life at Guo Jia level one. A Fracturize could have hit the end phase instead.

NeptuneI holds a Displace in hand and does not need the quest counters yet. The casters point out that megalobana neglected the trigger that is already on the stack, so he cannot prevent the draw from Relic Query, a beginning-of-recollection trigger. He uses Backup Charger and does not force a level up.

NeptuneI plays Displace on the Dungeon Guide while the Archer's swing is on the stack, so he goes up to Guo Jia level three, Heaven's Favored. The casters call it terrifying and note that he usually does not attack taunts or intercepts until later in the game. NeptuneI wins game one.

matches.round: Round 11 (Day 2, Round 2) — Water allies against Water Genbu

players.name: Xabichan
players.deck: Water allies (Nia, Mistveiled Scout; Lily, Marine Castellan; Frostsworn Paladin; Snow White, Weiss Queen; Seaside Ringleader; Titan Mk II; Snow Fairy; Portentous Tanggu; Smoke Bombs; Song of Frost; Staggering Strike in the side)

players.name: KUOJIA
players.deck: Water Genbu mill (Fractal of Rain, Refracting Missile, Fracturize, Cerulean Decree, Liminal Guide, Unbroken Mustang, Revitalizing Cleanse, Primordial Ritual; a taunt bullfrog protects Genbu)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters see Xabichan add Staggering Strike and more snow cards against the Genbu deck. They note that Staggering Strike costs more when the terrain is active.
The casters point to four Revitalizing Cleanse between the main deck and side, and say KUOJIA's list is tanky. They question why he has so few answers to the allies when the Genbu plan is slow.

games.summary: KUOJIA wins — Genbu flips into a 17-attack swing while Xabichan is tapped out

beats.text: Xabichan starts with Nia, Mistveiled Scout, which names a card and reveals KUOJIA's memory. KUOJIA answers with Fractal of Rain and Fracturize to turn off the Nia, and the bullfrog taunt and the floating memory slow the allies.

Xabichan plays Lily, a Frostsworn Paladin and two Seaside Ringleaders, and brings a Snow White and a Song of Frost into play. KUOJIA uses Cerulean Decree and Refracting Missile to remove the allies, and the casters say the deck has no cheap removal of its own.
Xabichan taps out with no Song of Frost available. KUOJIA flips Genbu and swings with a 17-attack turtle for exact lethal, and the casters say Polar Depths was there as a backup if he needed it.

games.summary: Xabichan wins — the allies race Genbu before KUOJIA finds his bullfrog

beats.text: Xabichan chooses to go first after the loss and opens with a turn-one Lily. KUOJIA has many negates, Unbroken Mustang to remove the regalia, and a hand that does little against the allies. The casters note that Xabichan also has Primordial Ritual to sacrifice the Frostsworn Paladin and mill two cards.

Snow Fairy taps the Frostsworn Paladin so it cannot stand up, and Xabichan has a free floating memory from KUOJIA's own mill. KUOJIA has only one copy of the big frog in the deck and does not draw it.
Xabichan attacks for the game before KUOJIA can mill enough counters to flip Genbu. The match goes to a third game.

games.summary: KUOJIA wins — in overtime Xabichan declines the all-in swing and Genbu flips first

beats.text: Xabichan opens with Nia at level one and taxes KUOJIA's memory. KUOJIA mills past his floating memory and Liminal Guide several times in a row, which the casters call unlucky comedy. Portentous Tanggu gives Xabichan a quest counter and more cards.

KUOJIA keeps his hand small and plays carefully: Fractal of Rain, Refracting Missile on Jing and Titan Mk II, and Cerulean Decree. Staggering Strike costs five because the terrain is active, and the casters note it is a misplay for Xabichan to forget that.

The game goes to overtime and will end on Xabichan's turn. The casters count that three plus three plus four with Cerulean Decree would have been exact lethal, but Xabichan is not sure of it. KUOJIA flips Genbu before the combat phase and wins the game and the match.

matches.round: Round 12 (Day 2, Round 3, stream table) — Wind Shadowstrike Tristan against fragmented Fire Merlin

players.name: Quarax
players.deck: Wind Shadowstrike Tristan (Windmill Engineer, Fairy Whispers, Dungeon Guide, Heavenly Guide, Slice and Dice, Mastermind Scheme, Sadi, Shadow's Claw, Windwalker Boots, Innervate Agility, Incapacitate, Resolute Stand)

players.name: Chuwubs
players.deck: Fire Merlin, fragmented (Spirit Blade: Ascension x3, Fireball, Rile the Abyss, Creative Shock, Cremation Ritual, Fluffy Shopkeep, Ghosts of Pendragon, Inert Sword, Crystallized Destiny)

matches.result: Chuwubs wins 2-0 — Quarax's first defeat of the tournament, per the casters

sideboardNotes.text: The casters discuss Quarax's side: Regal Inquisition and an extra Incapacitate to answer an Incapacitate, and they expect the Incapacitate also helps when he plays second. They also name a card that is one of the most sideboarded in the tournament and is good against level three decks.

games.summary: Chuwubs wins — three Spirit Blade: Ascension denials leave Quarax with too few cards, and he concedes

beats.text: Chuwubs keeps Fluffy Shopkeep and an Inert Sword to deal with the Black Market Broker, and the casters note he saves his Creative Shock for the right moment. Quarax answers with Dungeon Guide and takes the broker back with a reclaim to stay net neutral.

Quarax takes a Winbless Lookout for a preparation counter and a controlled level one. Chuwubs hits him for five total damage and keeps Ghosts of Pendragon ready, and Quarax has the Incapacitate and Slice and Dice in his hand.

Chuwubs plays Spirit Blade: Ascension again and again, each one hitting a Dream Fairy and banishing a random card from Quarax's memory. A second Ascension keeps Quarax from reaching level two with no Dungeon Guide in hand, and the casters say Quarax knows when he is cooked. He moves straight to game two.

games.summary: Chuwubs wins — Fireball finishes after a long fight over Crystallized Destiny and Veiling Breeze

beats.text: Quarax opens with Fairy Whispers into Windmill Engineer, reclaims it and levels to one right away. Chuwubs deals one damage with Fluffy Shopkeep and plays Cremation Ritual, and the casters see him plan to hard level to three next turn without a Dungeon Guide in hand.

Chuwubs shows a rainbow Spirit Blade: Ascension again. Quarax reaches four preparation counters and materializes Shadow's Claw with two shadows, and Sadi kills the Fluffy Shopkeep. The casters see Chuwubs holding a lot of fast-speed cards, including Fireball, and Quarax holds Veiling Breeze for his fire cards.

Chuwubs uses Creative Shock to draw the card that denies Crystallized Destiny, which would have protected Quarax. Quarax keeps Resolute Stand so his shadows cannot swing, and Chuwubs plays Incapacitate into the key Quarax spell.

Chuwubs shows his whole hand, kills the Fluffy and then throws the last card, Fireball, at Quarax. The casters say Chuwubs could have killed Quarax three turns earlier with the same Fireball. The casters note that only two Swiss rounds remain, so Quarax must hope to make the top eight despite this loss.

matches.round: Round 13 (Day 2, Round 4, stream table) — Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia against Fire Suzaku Guo Jia

players.name: Apaul
players.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (Beseeched Fatestone, Dungeon Guide, Sunblessed Gazelle, Seiryuu's Command, Byakko's Command, Innervate Agility, Resolute Stand, Spellward Scepter, Nullifying Mirror, Regal Inquisition)

players.name: Quon0823
players.deck: Fire Suzaku Guo Jia (Suzaku's Command, Heated Vengeance, Blazing Throw, Restorative Flame, Fiery Interference, Vermilion Decree, Creative Shock, Rile the Abyss, Purifying Thurible, Tariff Ring)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters expect Apaul to put his Beseeched Fatestones back in if he goes first, and note he has Regal Inquisition and a Nullifying Mirror for the Veiling Breeze plan. Fiery Interference is the sideboard card Quon0823 uses against the Innervate Agility.

games.summary: Quon0823 wins — Apaul goes first and still cannot close, and Quon0823 finds the last damage

beats.text: Apaul goes first and materializes the fate stone and Dungeon Guide in his first turns, flips the stone to bring out a panda and goes to Guo Jia level three early. The casters point out that Apaul went first, found both the Beseeched Fatestone and the Dungeon Guide, and still could not win.

Quon0823 keeps Suzaku's Command and Heated Vengeance in hand, and he wants to flip the Suzaku in response. The panda has two defense, so a spell clears it easily, and Quon0823 uses Restorative Flame as insurance against an all-in Seiryuu's Command.
The Suzaku flips and the last burn damage goes through. The casters say Apaul went first, had the Fatestone on board, and still could not close the game, while Quon0823 found the last bit of damage.

games.summary: Apaul wins — a Sunblessed Gazelle wall and the Seiryuu's Command combo beat a Quon0823 hand full of stranded Blazing Throws

beats.text: Quon0823 uses Rile the Abyss and Creative Shock to dig and discards to the Purifying Thurible. His Blazing Throws sit in hand without a weapon, and a Heated Vengeance for five becomes live after the Fatestone does one damage to his champion.

Apaul plays Sunblessed Gazelle with a +7 influence boost, an eight-life taunt, and adds a second taunt. The casters say the Suzaku cannot get past the wall, and only a big Suzaku's Command for eight can break the Gazelle.

Apaul has Seiryuu's Command and Byakko's Command, which together can kill from two in a row. The casters say Quon0823 missed a sequencing chance: Fiery Interference before the Innervate Agility resolved would have stopped the heal and changed the game.

games.summary: Apaul wins — the Suzaku never arrives and the Seiryuu's Commands go through

beats.text: Apaul puts the fatestones back in, levels up quickly, and flips his panda. The casters see Quon0823 with three cards in hand and assume a burn spell, but nothing comes. Apaul plays a little fast and loose, and Quon0823 cannot punish it.

Apaul flips the Seiryuu in response to an instant attack and plays Tariff Ring. The Seiryuu's Command and Byakko's Command deal eight, and the Gazelle adds to the board. Quon0823 waits for the Suzaku but it does not come, and the casters compare it to an order that never arrives.
Apaul closes the game with the Seiryuu's Command damage, and the casters say Quon0823's Suzaku was too slow. Apaul wins the match 2-1.

matches.round: Round 14 (final Swiss round, Day 2, stream table) — the winner takes the last Top 8 place: Fire Krux Lorraine against Fire Oblation Ciel

players.name: Enki
players.deck: Fire Krux Lorraine, fragmented (Rile the Abyss, Creative Shock, Undying Dreams, Rending Flames, Flame Sweep, Clarent, Reimagined, Ghosts of Pendragon, Resolute Stand, Crystallized Destiny, Regal Inquisition, Cremation Ritual; two Krux sights)

players.name: Long
players.deck: Fire Oblation Ciel (Baleful Oblation, Advent of the Stormcaller, Orb of Sealing, Liminal Guide, Sword of Shadows, Inert Sword, Fluffy Shopkeep, Dungeon Guide, Cremation Ritual, Undying Dreams; the Mirage's Grave plan that returns swords)

matches.result: Long wins 2-1 and takes the last Top 8 place

sideboardNotes.text: The casters expect Long to bring in Regal Inquisition and discuss the new Regalia that draws more cards at the cost of damage to himself. They note that Orb of Sealing is how he shuts down a Regal Inquisition.
The casters note that the winner usually chooses to go first in this meta, and that this had a large impact on Enki's game 2.

games.summary: Long wins — Baleful Oblation with Advent of the Stormcaller clears the board and finishes Enki

beats.text: Enki opens with Rile the Abyss and Creative Shock, and the stream shows both players in the Looking Glass. Long plays two Dungeon Guides, discards a second Stalwart Shieldmate and builds floating memory with the Hasty Messenger.

Enki gets value from Reduce to Ash and Undying Dreams, and a swing hits Long for three. Long still needs to set up his Oblation pieces, including the Orb of Sealing, and is under pressure from Enki's one-, three- and four-cost allies.

Long plays a Spirit Blade spell that puts cheap swords from his banishment and material deck into play, then swings with the swords and the Liminal Guide to tap Enki out. Baleful Oblation deals damage equal to the swords and the Advent of the Stormcaller makes it lethal, and Rending Flames comes too late.

games.summary: Enki wins — Rending Flames deals 22 and Regal Inquisition strips Long's answers

beats.text: Enki goes first and draws a stream of Rile the Abyss, Creative Shock and Liminal Guide. He reaches level three while Long's Resolute Stand and Incapacitate are the only way to stay alive.

Enki plays Flame Sweep and Clarent, Reimagined, and the casters count Rending Flames at 22 damage with five banished swords. Long uses a Crystallized Destiny and Resolute Stand, but Enki's Regal Inquisition removes the answers, and the casters say Long has no second Resolute Stand.
Long needs to materialize the Orb of Sealing to stop the Regal Inquisition, but he cannot and Enki wins with the flames and the Flame Sweep. The match goes to game 3.

games.summary: Long wins — Cremation Ritual into a double Baleful Oblation finds the final damage through Enki's Rending Flames

beats.text: Long chooses to go first. He plays Fluffy Shopkeep to protect the early game and keeps a Liminal Guide for the right moment. Enki uses Creative Shock to look for answers and holds Crystallized Destiny to protect himself from a Rending Flames.

Both players play safe because of the Incapacitate risk. Enki plays Regal Inquisition and sees Long's hand, and Long keeps his Resolute Stand. The casters say Long has no way to draw the Incapacitate.

Long plays Cremation Ritual with ten cards in hand and finds a double Baleful Oblation. Enki cracks his Clarent and Crystallized Destiny to prevent four damage, but Baleful Oblation is not preventable. The casters say Enki's Rending Flames left his sword on two durability, which made the Oblation do two less damage than it could. Long finds the win through two lost Oblations.

matches.round: Top 8 — Quarterfinal (featured match, untimed): Wind Wake Up against Fire Krux Lorraine

players.name: Yamikin
players.deck: Wind Wake Up allies (Mad Hatter, Concealed Marksman, Cheshire Cat, Second Wind, Evasive Maneuvers, Fairy Whispers, Backup Charger, Stifling Trap, Incapacitate, Resolute Stand; unique allies such as Purse and Lupe that gain value from distant cards)

players.name: Zero0000000000
players.deck: Fire Krux Lorraine (Rending Flames, Flame Sweep, Clarent, Reimagined, Ghosts of Pendragon, Fluffy Shopkeep, Sword of Shadows, Inert Sword, Resolute Stand, Incapacitate)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters talk through both sideboards. Yamikin has a regalia removal card that can hit cost-one regalia, and a null spell plan: Second Wind is itself a spell. They expect Cheshire Cat to be a good ally once Yamikin materializes the Inert Sword.
Zero0000000000 keeps the Krux cards that fill his banishment and watches for Besiege cards in Yamikin's hand.

games.summary: Yamikin wins — Wake Up allies and distant cards build a big hit through a Resolute Stand

beats.text: Yamikin opens slowly, finds a Resolute Stand early and levels with Tristan for a cost discount. Zero0000000000 clears the Dungeon Guide and the cards in the graveyard and has the faster start. The casters think Yamikin will have to work hard, because he has done no damage for many turns.

Zero0000000000 swings his Lorraine to kill an ally, and a Flame Sweep and Clarent, Reimagined keep Yamikin's board small. The casters say the door is closing for Yamikin, but his Stifling Trap and a Fluffy Shopkeep on Zero0000000000's side slow the race. Yamikin has put seven of 15 damage counters on Zero0000000000.

Yamikin uses Evasive Maneuvers to make Purse and Lupe distant and plays Mad Hatter, Second Wind and Ranger Strides. Zero0000000000 goes face and puts Yamikin on 13, but one hit-point is all Yamikin needs. The distant allies deal eight damage three times, and Yamikin wins game one.

games.summary: Yamikin wins — a slow game where he collects the pieces and unloads through the Resolute Stand

beats.text: Yamikin keeps Reduce to Ash in hand, and the casters say that was smart. He plays Fairy Whispers to look for a wind card and finds the Mad Hatter, a Concealed Marksman and a Cheshire Cat. Zero0000000000 has Rile the Abyss and Backup Charger and throws Krux cards into the banishment.

Zero0000000000 has two Resolute Stands and uses them to protect his life total. Yamikin goes to Tristan level one for an Incapacitate buff and plays Stifling Trap, and Zero0000000000 uses Spirit Blade: Ascension on the Ghosts of Pendragon swing.

Zero0000000000 is tapped out. Yamikin needs 28 damage, and he reaches it with the Cheshire Cat and Lupe, two plus eight from the double Ranger Strides, even through the Resolute Stand. The casters say Yamikin amassed so much damage that he could finish through the Resolute Stand, and Yamikin moves into the semifinals.

matches.round: Top 4 — Semifinal (featured match, untimed): Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia against Fire Oblation Ciel

players.name: Apaul
players.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (Taiwan; Seiryuu's Command, Byakko's Command, Arcane Blast, Harness Lightning, Fairy Whispers, Stifling Trap, Winds of Destiny, Purifying Thurible, Incandescent Reliquary, Grand Crusader's Ring, Incapacitate)

players.name: Long
players.deck: Fire Oblation Ciel, Omen Bringer (Baleful Oblation, double Dungeon Guide, Rile the Abyss, Reduce to Ash, Crystallized Destiny, Incapacitate, Liminal Guide; started the day at 621 points and had won every match until this one)

matches.result: Apaul wins 2-0 and reaches the final

sideboardNotes.text: Long brings in a second Dungeon Guide after game 1 to help him reach level three quickly. The casters note that the semifinal rounds are untimed, so both players can think about the best cards for the matchup, and say another spell would help him stop the damage.

games.summary: Apaul wins — Purifying Thurible and Liminal Guide slow Long, then the dragon and Arcane Blast combo finish through his Crystallized Destiny

beats.text: Apaul uses Winds of Destiny for many materializations and a Purifying Thurible, which draws into memory and removes Long's whole graveyard. Long cannot materialize his Backup Charger early, and Apaul keeps a Harness Lightning for an extra empower on the Seiryuu's attack.

Long plays Rile the Abyss and Reduce to Ash for floating memory and tries to reach level three, but Apaul keeps the pressure with the panda and the dragon. Long's Guardian is at level one with 20 maximum life, and the casters say level two has 25. The casters call that the key break point.

Apaul sets up the Seiryuu's Command and Byakko's Command combo with Arcane Blast. Long's Incapacitate is itself Incapacitated, and the Arcane Blast and the dragon deal the rest through his Crystallized Destiny. The casters say the Incapacitate war was the big difference.

games.summary: Apaul wins — the dragon hits for nine twice and Arcane Blast finishes

beats.text: Long holds two Dungeon Guides and Reduce to Ash and wants to reach level three before Apaul's Seiryuu. Apaul loses a Fairy Whispers from the top of his deck but keeps Stifling Trap, and denies Long's Rile the Abyss with it again.

Long sacrifices a Dungeon Guide on enter and plans a double Baleful Oblation. The casters say he is forced to spend the Oblation to try to win the game. Apaul reaches nine quest counters and can flip the dragon.

Apaul uses Seiryuu's Command and Byakko's Command so the dragon swings twice, for nine and nine, and Arcane Blast adds five, five and eleven. He wins the semifinal. The casters say the game was won by the dragon hitting for nine and nine, not just the blast, and that Apaul accelerated very quickly with the Wake Up-style start.

matches.round: Bronze Match (third place, untimed): Fire Oblation Ciel against Wind Wake Up

players.name: Long
players.deck: Fire Oblation Ciel (Baleful Oblation, Advent of the Stormcaller, Dungeon Guide, Rile the Abyss, Creative Shock, Reduce to Ash, Undying Dreams, Cremation Ritual, Consumption Ring, Crystallized Destiny, Incapacitate)

players.name: Yamikin
players.deck: Wind Wake Up allies (Purse, Lupe, Mad Hatter, Concealed Marksman, Cheshire Cat, Ranger Strides, Evasive Maneuvers, Second Wind, Draught of Stamina, Stifling Trap, Incapacitate, Resolute Stand; a patient, high-influence build)

matches.result: Long wins 2-1 (the VOD shows one game in full)

games.summary: Long wins — Baleful Oblation and Consumption Ring hold off the allies, and Yamikin misses the Ranger Strides he needs

beats.text: Yamikin starts slowly with a Sensor-style board, Purse and Lupe, and the casters wonder if Long is lost on how to approach the matchup. Long plays Rile the Abyss and drops two floating memory, and Backup Charger gives him a power cell. The casters say the ally deck is built to survive with high influence and be very patient.

Long uses Cremation Ritual to dig for more cards, and Yamikin tries to protect the Cheshire Cat with Evasive Maneuvers. The casters say Long can throw the Baleful Oblation as soon as Yamikin goes below five cards in hand. Long plays the Consumption Ring and the Oblation does 15.

Long hits level three with 30 life, which the casters call too much for the Wake Up deck to deal with, and Yamikin draws a hand with Draught of Stamina but not the Ranger Strides. Long keeps his Crystallized Destiny, which makes it hard for OTK combos to get through.

Yamikin commits to the Mad Hatter combo and has a one in seven chance of hitting Ranger Strides, but he misses. Long survives with Evasive Maneuvers' help and Incapacitate bait, and Yamikin finishes fourth. The casters say the game was close to the end.

matches.round: Grand Finals (best of 3, untimed): Fire Suzaku against Wind Seiryuu

players.name: ProAnnn
players.deck: Fire Suzaku Guo Jia (first seed of the tournament; Suzaku's Command, Heated Vengeance, Vermilion Decree, Demolition, Searing Truth, Impact Hammer, Creative Shock, Rile the Abyss, Dungeon Guide, Resolute Stand, Restorative Flame, Fiery Interference, Fabled Ruby Fatestone, Peppered Chef)

players.name: Apaul
players.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (Taiwan; Seiryuu's Command, Arcane Blast, Sunblessed Gazelle, Baby Green Slime, Stifling Trap, Winds of Destiny, Grand Crusader's Ring, Portentous Tanggu, Fairy Whispers, Innervate Agility, Fabled Azurite Fatestone)

matches.result: Apaul wins 2-1 and is the Ascent Taipei champion

sideboardNotes.text: Apaul chooses to go first in game two. The casters note that he has only one extra Resolute Stand and that most of his sideboard is for level three decks.
ProAnnn goes first in game three and the casters say he must play around Baby Green Slime in every turn. His Fiery Interference is already used.

games.summary: ProAnnn wins — Demolition and a stream of burn spells bring Apaul down while he has no hand

beats.text: ProAnnn materializes his Spirit of Fire, but has no Beseech the Winds in hand and uses Fairy Whispers to look for it. The casters note he has seven quest counters while Apaul has ten, and a Peppered Chef is in his hand.
Apaul pays dearly for a Resolute Stand early. He sits on a hand of zero cards at 22 life. ProAnnn plays Demolition for three, levels to Guo Jia two and keeps Restorative Flame ready.

ProAnnn throws another burn spell and Suzaku's Command, and Apaul's Gazelle taunt cannot stop the burn. The casters say Apaul could take 16 to 20 damage in a single turn out of nowhere. ProAnnn takes game one.

games.summary: Apaul wins — he goes first, flips the Seiryuu with ten quest counters, and Resolute Stand pays out

beats.text: Apaul goes first and uses Glimpse and Winds of Destiny to dig through the deck. ProAnnn cannot use his Liminal Guide for a net-neutral level up. The casters say the Seiryuu needs only nine more quest counters and is easy to bring to ten.

ProAnnn answers with Rile the Abyss in Apaul's end step and top-decks a Creative Shock off a double Rile the Abyss. He has Heated Vengeance and a Tree of Hearts, and Apaul must show respect to the burn.

Apaul goes up to nine and then ten quest counters with the Dungeon Guide, and levels to Guo Jia level three. A Baby Green Slime targets the Fabled Ruby Fatestone, because it is not a spell, and Apaul's Seiryuu comes in. ProAnnn does not have the Resolute Stand and loses the game.

games.summary: Apaul wins — a top-decked Innervate Agility and Seiryuu's Command beat ProAnnn's burn, and ProAnnn forgets a Gazelle trigger

beats.text: ProAnnn goes first with no Creative Shock and no Rile the Abyss, so he has no net-neutral level up. He uses Searing Truth for two quest counters and keeps a Fabled Ruby Fatestone, but has no Peppered Chef to flip the Suzaku early.

Apaul uses Baby Green Slime to stop the Impact Hammer and a Fabled Ruby Fatestone, and the quest counters stay but the stone is suppressed. ProAnnn uses a Vermilion Decree for three damage, and Apaul answers with Winds of Destiny and Fairy Whispers.

Apaul pops Portentous Tanggu and finds Innervate Agility. Innervate Agility recovers five and lets him level, and he takes ProAnnn to 22 with a seven plus four plus eleven line. ProAnnn needs a Suzaku's Command but does not find it, and the casters say Apaul would take the game with the Seiryuu's Command.

Apaul forgets that Gazelle is tapped and makes a misplay, but ProAnnn still cannot burn him out. Apaul wins the match 2-1 and is the Ascent Taipei champion; the casters say they love a misplay that still wins.

matches.round: Round 1: Wind Fortuitous Rye (arcane elemental) against Fire Oblation CL

players.name: Hyouka
players.deck: Wind Fortuitous Rye, arcane build (Arcane Elemental; Arcane Blast x2; Advent of the Stormcaller; Disorienting Winds; Tome of Sacred Lightning; Pneumonic Charms; Careful Study; Lost Providence; Three Visits; Fluffy Shopkeep; Dungeon Guide x4; Veiling Breeze and Weaken Resistance tech)

players.name: DuckHats
players.deck: Fire Oblation CL (Baleful Oblation, Cremation Ritual, Liminal Guide, Undeniable Truth, Topsy Decree, a Mansion/Maximum armoire package; Orb of Sealing from the side)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters point out the open decklist format: DuckHats knows that Hyouka has access to Orb of Sealing. They discuss using it on the Cremation Ritual and creative-shock style early plays instead of Baleful Oblation, to slow the explosive Rye start down.

games.summary: Hyouka wins — a long Pneumonic Charm and Arcane Blast level-up sequence beats the Oblation clock

beats.text: DuckHats opens on Fire CL with Liminal Guide and Cremation Ritual, setting up a Baleful Oblation and holding a Feu Awakening. The casters call Feu Awakening the key card for DuckHats to find before Hyouka reaches level three.

Hyouka holds all four Dungeon Guides and goes straight to level three, using Undeniable Truth on a Liminal Guide to draw. He is influence-maxing with two Pneumonic Charms and Tome of Sacred Lightning, which makes each charm able to cast an Arcane Blast for free once he reaches level nine.

Careful Study gives a huge pile of enlightened counters, and a second Arcane Blast plus the Arcane Elemental are ready. The casters note CL's 30 life is a bigger buffer than most champions have, but Hyouka finds the swing before DuckHats can use his own lethal turn. Hyouka takes game one.

games.summary: DuckHats wins — Orb of Sealing and Topsy Decree stall Hyouka, and the Oblation clock closes

beats.text: DuckHats lines up Topsy Decree and an Oblation, and uses the Mansion/armoire turns to keep Hyouka off the arcane cards. Hyouka brings in the Orb of Sealing from the side as an answer to the fire build.

Hyouka digs for Arcane Sight and Erratic Bolt, and holds a Spell Shield Arcane. The casters say DuckHats wants exactly this, because it lets him play directly through the shield, and Hyouka tries to use Tome of Sacred Lightning to bank more arcane cards but only finds an Advent of the Stormcaller.
The casters call the 28 damage Hyouka needs a non-viable line, so he plays safer with Careful Study, but DuckHats closes the game. DuckHats wins game two and takes the match to a third game.

games.summary: Hyouka wins — going first, he stacks the top of his deck and finishes with Arcane Blast and Arcane Elemental

beats.text: Hyouka gets to go first, which the casters call night and day in level three matchups. DuckHats brings down the Grande Sonnerie with the reserve costs for a lethal attack on its own, and Hyouka answers with Fluffy Shopkeep and Three Visits.

Hyouka has too many arcane cards for his own hand, banishes the useless ones and digs with Careful Study. The casters note Fluffy Shopkeep on intercept is a good call. Lost Providence stacks the top of the deck.

Hyouka sends 15 damage at the face. With two Disorienting Winds, a second Arcane Blast and an Advent of the Stormcaller, he chains Arcane Blast into Arcane Elemental and Advent. Disorienting Winds returns the Arcane Elemental for another seven damage, DuckHats concedes and Hyouka wins the match.

matches.sourceNote: Cleaned broadcast transcript, The Gauntlet 2026 VOD, Round 1 feature match. Casters call the players "Hyoka" and "Duck Hats" (Omnidex usernames Hyouka and DuckHats). Result per Omnidex (Hyouka 2-1). Card names are as called by the casters and may contain minor ASR errors; decks and mid-game plays were summarized from a sampled read of the captions and are partly uncertain.

matches.round: Round 2: Water Fractals Diao Chan against Fire Slimes Sylvia

players.name: Xaleonidas
players.deck: Water Fractals Diao Chan (Fractal of Rain, Fractal of Snow, Fractal of Insight, Fractal of Refreshment, Captivating Opulence, Glimmering Refusal, Refracting Missile, Fracturize, Burst Asunder, Frostsworn Paladin, Bullfrog, Backup Charger)

players.name: HolySamurai
players.deck: Fire Slimes Sylvia (Baby Red Slime, Baby Gray Slime, Limitless Slime, Storm Slime, Slime King, Slime Eruption, Escape the Wreckage, Horn of Beastcalling, Dungeon Guide, Backup Charger, Turbo Charge; raccoon package of Portly Raccoon, Bandit and Protector; Twilight Slime from the side)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters note that Xaleonidas is not built to beat slimes. His only help is a lantern that answers Slime King, and Topsy Decree does not do much against many small allies.
HolySamurai brings in Twilight Slime and boots-style protection. The casters call Twilight Slime a huge piece in this matchup, because Fractals kills its targets and the slime shrugs that off.

games.summary: HolySamurai wins — constant raccoon and slime pressure lets him close without ever resolving a beast

beats.text: Xaleonidas starts with Spirit of Water and a Fractal of Snow, but throws only one Fractal, which the casters say is low for going second. He draws a second Fractal off the first Fractal of Refreshment and holds a Refracting Missile.
Xaleonidas snipes the Baby Gray Slime with Refracting Missile, which stops HolySamurai from returning it and negates the Escape the Wreckage. The casters call it a huge momentum shift.

HolySamurai has a Bandit and a Protector Raccoon in the opening hand, which the casters say constricts Fractals. He baits two Glimmering Refusals and gets in with Gaia's blessing and a Slime Eruption in hand. The casters say HolySamurai has lethal on board and beats his chest when game one is his.

games.summary: Xaleonidas wins — Enfeebling Orb and a burst of Fractals break HolySamurai's Blanch timing

beats.text: HolySamurai starts with Creative Shock and discards a Hymn of Gaia's Grace. Xaleonidas hits through the board three more times and takes HolySamurai to six damage of fifteen.

Xaleonidas plays Captivating Opulence to stifle HolySamurai, who must pay extra for each play. The casters point to the Stonescale Band, the Horn of Beastcalling and the Covenant of Thorns in HolySamurai's hand. HolySamurai tries to get the Slime King down, which needs three different elements of slimes.

HolySamurai will not pay ten into a Glimmering Refusal and instead slows down with Blanch in hand. The Frostsworn Paladin attacks into the Blanch and banishes it. Xaleonidas lines up an 18-damage burst, one over the needed amount. HolySamurai sends the Blanch too early, the Enfeebling Orb forces it to be popped, and Xaleonidas takes game two.

games.summary: Xaleonidas wins — a race against the clock ends in a Burst Asunder with six fractals out

beats.text: Both decks must end the game fast with little time on the clock. HolySamurai goes bandit into bandit and plays a double Dungeon Guide start. Xaleonidas plays a double fractal start with Fractal of Snow and Fractal of Insight, and throws a Burst Asunder away to the discard.

HolySamurai plays Limitless Slime and a Baby Red Slime for a six-damage turn, over half of Xaleonidas's life in one turn. The casters say it is the only play that makes sense, because he needs Slime Eruption to deal damage.
Xaleonidas has five fractals out, then six. He puts down the Enfeebling Orb and pays for a Burst Asunder. HolySamurai cannot stop it, and Xaleonidas wins the match 2-1.
