matches.round: Round 3: Water Genbu against Fire Oblation CL

players.name: Royan
players.deck: Water Genbu from Taiwan (Genbu, Black Tortoise; Tidestone Bovine; Frostsworn Paladin; Fractal of Rain x2; Revitalizing Cleanse; Tidal Lock; Engulf; Excalibur; Fracturize; Enfeebling Orb; Blanch, Sheltering Saint in the side)

players.name: JacePatrick
players.deck: Fire Oblation CL (Baleful Oblation, Folded Shadow, Feu Awakening, Advent of the Stormcaller, Creative Shock, Liminal Guide x4, Golden Checkmate, Resolute Stand, Manxome Armoire, Turbo Charge, Backup Charger)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters see very lean sideboards on both sides. JacePatrick has few options, perhaps an Abnegation-style answer if the kill turns line up. Royan has the heavier hitters, and the casters point to Blanch, Sheltering Saint.

games.summary: Royan wins — Tidal Lock into Engulf leaves JacePatrick with no interaction, then Genbu arrives

beats.text: JacePatrick uses Creative Shock, but Royan's Engulf stops Advent of the Stormcaller from going to the graveyard, so he adds it to the omens from hand. Royan is happy to see floating memory in the graveyard for later plays.

Royan draws extra from the Tidestone Bovine and takes his time because Genbu is hard to bring out unless he is set up. JacePatrick holds a scary hand with a 19-damage Baleful Oblation lethal line but no Feu Awakening yet, and the casters note that Royan has shown a Revitalizing Cleanse that answers it.

Royan casts Tidal Lock into Engulf, so JacePatrick is out of interaction. Genbu, Black Tortoise hits the battlefield and Royan takes game one. The casters say JacePatrick's early and mid game was rough even though he held late-game bombs.

games.summary: Royan wins — JacePatrick sends his whole hand to the graveyard with Feu Awakening, but Royan finds the line through Folded Shadow

beats.text: JacePatrick has drawn the Turbo Charge this time, and plays a Liminal Guide as the first play. Without a Creative Shock, he adds a Golden Checkmate to the banish with an omen counter. The casters say he has four guides in memory, which helps fight the water negate decks.

Royan keeps pressure on with annoying minions and the Tidestone Bovine, going up to six quest counters and six cards in hand for the Revitalizing Cleanse. JacePatrick's Folded Shadows puts Royan under spell shroud and stealth, and the casters say Royan cannot easily push through.

JacePatrick throws Feu Awakening and sends his entire hand to the graveyard in a hail-mary line. Royan still has the Revitalizing Cleanse that could escape lethal, takes the chance JacePatrick will walk in, and finds the path to win. Royan moves to 3-0 against the boogeyman of the event, Oblation CL.

matches.round: Round 4: Fire Oblation CL against Water Jin mill

players.name: TheRainGoddess
players.deck: Fire Oblation CL (Baleful Oblation, Feu Awakening, Cremation Ritual, Creative Shock, Liminal Guide, Dungeon Guide x3, Turbo Charge, Backup Charger, Lost Providence, Manxome Armoire, Angel Attendant, Angelic Channeling, Topsy Decree; Abnegation, Blanch and a null spell in the side)

players.name: Dal157
players.deck: Water Jin mill (Dynastic Whirlpool, Pearled Prayer, Umbra Sight, Transfusive Aura, Regal Inquisition, Angelic Channeling, Benediction Angel, Spirit of Serene Water, Chime of Endless Dreams, Delusional Vapors, Fracturize; a Chalice for recovery)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters see Abnegation and Blanch in TheRainGoddess's side, which protect against Relentless Outburst and enrage swings. They call a null spell the all-star in the matchup because it stops Dynastic Whirlpool and Regal Inquisition.
Dal157 brings in Spirit of Serene Water, Chime of Endless Dreams and Delusional Vapors for more recovery and extra mill, because recovery is the best counterplay to Baleful Oblation.

games.summary: Dal157 wins — TheRainGoddess never finds Baleful Oblation and the Dynastic Whirlpool mills the deck out

beats.text: TheRainGoddess keeps the opening hand but has to be careful: against mill, each extra card drawn pulls the deck closer to empty. She removes a lantern and an Orb of Sealing from the material deck to draw an additional card.

Dal157 starts slowly and goes up to Jin level one, and the casters point out that levels one and two just lead to level three in these Jin decks. A triple Angelic Channeling puts advanced element cards in his lineage, and he uses Fracturize on TheRainGoddess's chalice.

TheRainGoddess has only 14 cards left, still no Baleful Oblation, and has drawn the cards Dal157 needed. A bubble of abundance and a 15-card mill finish it, and she scoops. Dal157 stabilizes and mills out TheRainGoddess to take game one, a game that was rough in the early stages for him.

games.summary: TheRainGoddess wins — a huge Turbo Charge start and a clean Oblation sequence, then Dal157 goes to sleep

beats.text: TheRainGoddess hits a 53 off Rector's Tiding with Backup Charger and Turbo Charge, going up to level one with Creative Shock and a discarded Liminal Guide. The casters call it the start you want in game two and note Cremation Ritual is next. Topsy Decree handles an Angelic Channeling.

Dal157 has the Spirit of Serene Water ready to heal six at any time and uses Umbra Sight to sculpt his hand. He goes down to 17 and back up to 32, and Transfusive Aura makes a recovery cheaper, but the casters say the longer game helps TheRainGoddess.

Dal157 goes down to 15 because of Transfusive Aura, but it is still not enough. TheRainGoddess finds no Berserker's Plate for him, plays Feu Awakening with Oblations and sends Dal157 to sleep. The casters call it a masterclass Oblation game and count 30 minutes for game one and 20 for game two.

games.summary: No winner — the round ends one card short of a TheRainGoddess lethal

beats.text: Dal157 goes first with about seven minutes left and keeps Spirit of Serene Water. His opening hand has Liminal Guide, Angelic Channeling and Angel Attendant but no Cremation Ritual. The casters say a double loss would be painful for both players, and the two are friendly with each other.

TheRainGoddess uses Fracturize on Dal157's Power Cell to deny his floating memory, Dal157 tries three games in a row to go to level one with floating memory and fails again. TheRainGoddess uses Creative Shock, Backup Charger and a Dungeon Guide to find Oblations, and she uses Cremation Ritual.

Dal157 uses Pearled Prayer to recover seven (down to 45 damage) and Manflesh, and goes to Jin level three with Undying Resolve. He uses Dynastic Whirlpool to mill 15, and the Serene Spirit takes him from 19 to 13, which TheRainGoddess has to push 28 damage through. She is one damage short; the next card would have been Feu Awakening, but time is called and the match is a draw.

matches.round: Round 5: Fire Oblation CL against Fire Suzaku Guo A

players.name: Guruthos
players.deck: Fire Oblation CL, team Main Deck list (Baleful Oblation, Feu Awakening, Crystallized Destiny, Chalice of Blood, Golden Checkmate, Manxome Armoire, Mirage's Grave, Nocturne's Oblivion, Dungeon Guide, Angelic Channeling, Topsy Decree, Resolute Stand, Orb of Sealing; Abnegation, Blanch and Flamewreath Call in the side)

players.name: Jayare
players.deck: Fire Suzaku Guo A, team Creative Shock (Suzaku's Command, Restorative Flames, Peppered Chef, Planted Explosive, Auspicious Manifestation, Crystallized Destiny x2, Vermilion Degrees, Fiery Interference, Chalice of Blood; many one-of burn spells; a null spell and Restorative Flames from the side)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters expect Jayare to bring in a null spell to slow CL down, and possibly another Restorative Flames because CL's damage is unpreventable. They also name Blanch and Flamewreath Call as other possible sideboard cards.

games.summary: Guruthos wins — he survives a double Crystallized Destiny and a Grande Sonnerie swing finishes with an Oblation

beats.text: Jayare opens with a Dungeon Guide level-up that the casters call really bad, playing Liminal Guide-style value and Planted Explosive for a four-damage trap. Guruthos plays Angelic Channeling at end of turn and Mirage's Grave off a Dungeon Guide, going to 30 life with 21 left for Jayare to deal.

Jayare must play slowly because he needs Crystallized Destiny in hand to survive CL's big Oblation turn. Guruthos uses Nocturne's Oblivion on the Orb of Sealing and sends Baleful Oblation at the materialization.

Guruthos loses the Turbo Charge to memory, which he is happy about, and draws a Feu Awakening off the Grande Sonnerie. The Grande Sonnerie swings for five unpreventable damage and Jayare has no Restorative Flames with an empty fire graveyard. Jayare never finds Blazing Throw or Heated Vengeance, and Guruthos takes game one.

games.summary: Jayare wins — Suzaku's Command and Peppered Chef get through Oblation negation

beats.text: Jayare plays first with Suzaku Guo A. Guruthos has Resolute Stand and Topsy Decree down early and a Liminal Guide, and the casters say the Blanch is strong for him here. Jayare keeps up fire cards in the graveyard for the Peppered Chef.

Guruthos wants the Chalice of Blood and Manxome Armoire and uses a free Resolute Stand to get through. He pays for the Golden Checkmate, which is dangerous because Jayare can throw away the Checkmate. Jayare gets two quest counters with Fiery Interference while only two fire cards are in hand, so he cannot imbue it.

Guruthos plays Baleful Oblation to clear the board, but Jayare activates the Suzaku's Command before swinging with the Peppered Chef. Guruthos's Orb of Sealing flips the omen, so the Oblation does zero damage. The lethal Suzaku attack wins game two for Jayare.

games.summary: Guruthos wins — he goes first, banishes two to level up and uses Abnegation to stop the burn

beats.text: Guruthos goes first. The casters say going first is a huge advantage for CL into fire aggro, and that fractals and fire aggro are CL's worst matchups. He has only four cards in influence and must banish two to level up, losing an Angelic Channeling to Jayare's quest counters.

Jayare starts with the first Crystallized Destiny, then Manxome Armoire resolves and takes the Checkmate back to hand. The casters talk about the Chalice of Blood as the reason Guruthos may live through Jayare's damage.

Guruthos holds Abnegation, so Jayare's Fiery Interference line cannot use the heal. Guruthos plays Baleful Oblation at the end of turn with the Abnegation backup, and Jayare has no Restorative Flames and an empty fire graveyard. Jayare scoops and Guruthos wins the match 2-1, going to 4-1.

matches.round: Round 6: Wind Krux Lorraine against Fire Oblation CL (a rematch of their Worlds 2024 Round 1 match)

players.name: GlenyBoi
players.deck: Wind Krux Lorraine (Lorraine, Blademaster; Spirit Blade: Ascension x2; Prismatic Edge; Drawn Blade; Sword of Seeking; Aella; Ghosts of Pendragon; Fairy Whispers; Fluffy Shopkeep; Dungeon Guide; Imperious Galebind; Illusion Longbowman; Lost Providence; Angelic Channeling; Orb of Sealing and Chamberlain Toad in the side)

players.name: Limelight
players.deck: Fire Oblation CL (Baleful Oblation, Feu Awakening, Manxome Armoire, Cremation Ritual, Creative Shock, Liminal Guide, Dungeon Guide, Carter, Resolute Stand, Umbra Sight; a null spell and Spurell in the side; the casters say his list has its own tech compared with other Oblation decks)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters point to the Orb of Sealing in GlenyBoi's side. They think he may add Chamberlain Toad so that Spirit Blade: Ascension becomes card neutral, and they note that Illusion Longbowman would have helped in game one.
The casters expect Limelight to bring in a null spell and the Spurell, which he puts down and later has ripped away. They note he plays his own take on the Oblation list.

games.summary: GlenyBoi wins — Ascension rips Limelight's memory apart and Prismatic Edge pushes the last damage

beats.text: The casters frame the match as a rematch of Worlds 2024 Round 1, when Limelight's Fire Umbra Diana beat Glenny's Merlin on the way to the lock. They favor the Oblation player in the matchup, but since the Clarent nerf to one prevention, much of the Oblation advantage is gone.

GlenyBoi sets up the dungeon guides on top of the deck and goes to level three. He uses Aella and Spirit Blade: Ascension to bring Prismatic Edge in and out of play, and plays Fairy Whispers to know what is on top. Fluffy Shopkeep and Calming Breeze do little against Limelight's plan.

Limelight finds Cremation Ritual and Liminal Guide, and keeps Resolute Stand and an Enel-style spell in hand to answer the pressure. The Baleful Oblation is banished off a Spirit Blade: Ascension on the Prismatic Edge. GlenyBoi swings with Prismatic Edge for three, then another Ascension, and takes game one, to the casters' praise for the deck mastery.

games.summary: GlenyBoi wins — Imperious Galebind and a double Ascension rip clear the last Oblation

beats.text: GlenyBoi draws into the Dungeon Guide he stacked on top, uses a Scout the Land to see two Ascensions, and starts with Sword of Seeking and Lorraine level one. He rips the Spurell out of the sideboard and into the banish before it can do anything, then rips Undeniable Truth out of Limelight's hand.

Limelight tries to level with Dungeon Guide and holds up the null spell. The casters say he has no Resolute Stand this time and has to look for another way to survive, but sacrificing his ally only draws Carter. Baleful Oblation clears the board, but GlenyBoi's Krux sight returns the Ascension to hand.

GlenyBoi uses Imperious Galebind on the Aella and Ghosts of Pendragon, and double Ascension rips Limelight's memory. Limelight casts Feu Awakening and sends the damage at Aella, but GlenyBoi has all he needs, and the casters celebrate his revenge from Worlds 2024.

matches.round: Round 7: Water Jin mill against Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (two players with one loss or fewer)

players.name: Aqua
players.deck: Water Jin mill, Fortuitous Spirit build (Spirit of Fortuitous Water, Dynastic Whirlpool, Regal Inquisition, Relentless Outburst, Enrage, Quicksilver Grail, Shangi, Backup Charger, Dungeon Guide, Angelic Channeling, Bauble of Abundance, Manflesh, Crimson Presence)

players.name: Apaul
players.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia, Ascent Taipei 2025 winner's list (Su, Azure Dragon; Seiryuu's Command; Byakko's Command; Optical Control; Angelic Channeling; Daunting Panda; Stifling Trap; Pixie Zone Heaven; Auspicious Manifestation; Innervate Agility; Scout the Land; Regal Inquisition and Blanch in the side; Mirrorbound Covenant and Eternal Magistrate as tech)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters say Blanch could help Apaul against Aqua's Relentless Outburst line, and Regal Inquisition could also come in. They note the previous game was very close, with Aqua one card short.
Aqua keeps a Crimson Presence-style defensive card against arcane damage in his list. The casters say Aqua is not down and out because game one was closer than it looked.

games.summary: Apaul wins — a turn-two panda and big Seiryuu's Command turns push Aqua to the edge, and Aqua runs out of out cards

beats.text: Apaul opens with a five-quest-counter Guo Jia start on turn two, using Scout the Land and recollect to draw into the panda. The casters introduce Daunting Panda and Angelic Channeling as the key cards that accelerate quest counters.

Seiryuu's Command triggers three modes on each attack and Apaul chooses empower. The Su Azure Dragon grows by one for every five damage counters on it, reaching 12 power. Aqua is at Jin level two with 24 damage and uses Enchanted Fete to recover memory.

Aqua lines up Relentless Outburst into Shangi plus a swing to finish the game, and the casters say he was literally one thing away. Apaul commands a huge amount of damage and Aqua is forced to win in one turn or lose. Apaul takes game one.

games.summary: Apaul wins — Optical Control locks out half of Aqua's deck and Aqua just misses the Quicksilver Grail line

beats.text: Aqua plays Spirit of Fortuitous Water to glimpse seven, and goes for a Backup Charger to level up as a control deck. Apaul uses a Besiege Faint Stone, Auspicious Manifestation discarded for a quest counter, and Angelic Channeling for another three quest counters.

Apaul brings out the dragon and a stifling trap, which had wrecked Aqua in the previous game. Optical Control shuts off a type of card, and the casters note it called action cards, so Aqua cannot use spells unless he pays four. Aqua takes up to 37 damage and must recover at least 10 to survive his end step.

Aqua thinks hard about a Quicksilver Grail into Shangi into Enrage sequence that would take the match to game three, and pops the Bauble of Abundance to draw. He finds Hemorrhaging Rend and Relentless Outburst, but there is not enough damage. Apaul takes round seven 2-0 with the dragon.

matches.round: Round 8: Fire Oblation CL against Water allies CL

players.name: Emp
players.deck: Fire Oblation CL (Baleful Oblation, Feu Awakening, Mirage's Grave, Manxome Armoire, Advent of the Stormcaller, Turbo Charge, Backup Charger, Umbra Sight, Weighted Accord, Resolute Stand, Dungeon Guide); North American Nationals and Ascent Auckland 2025 winner

players.name: Yamikin
players.deck: Water allies CL from Oceania Nationals (Bandit, Portly Raccoon, Protector Raccoon, Cheshire Cat, Snow White, Death Essence Amulet, Song of Frost, Frostbind; no Freezing Hail)

games.summary: Emp wins — he survives Yamikin's raccoon pressure and closes with Baleful Oblation and Manxome Armoire

beats.text: Yamikin opens with a fast ally start: Bandit, Portly Raccoons and an early Cheshire Cat. The casters say it plays like an aggressive water deck or a tamer deck and not like a CL deck, and the raccoons start pressure on Emp. Yamikin has five damage on board and a full grip.

Emp does a clean Backup Charger turn and goes to CL level two with a Turbo Charge for two extra cards. Umbra Sight and Mirage's Grave hit the board for Emp, and he puts an Advent of the Stormcaller into the omens from hand to take out the Bandit.

Yamikin passes with four cards active but cannot survive the Baleful Oblation. Manxome Armoire comes out through the materialization and the casters call the damage huge. The Death Essence Amulet, which makes the opponent discard when an ally dies, is not enough, and Emp takes game one with an amazing finish.

games.summary: Emp wins — Yamikin is one step short, and Umbra Sight pays for Weighted Accord to cast the final Oblation

beats.text: Yamikin goes first and plays a Backup Charger, which the casters call a trap. Emp finds a Resolute Stand with Rector's Tiding and adds cards to the omens from hand. He has lots of influence but no Dungeon Guide to level up faster.

Yamikin goes up to CL level one with Snow White, and the casters note he has no Freezing Hail to keep Emp's level two CL rested. He pushes in as much damage as he can, with a Power Cell and an automaton, to bring Emp down.

Emp goes to level three, and without an Umbra Sight he could not cast Baleful Oblation because of Weighted Accord, but he has one. Yamikin goes down to 19 damage counters with one card in hand, Baleful Oblation does 15 and Feu Awakening seals it. Emp wins 2-0, and the casters call Oblation the talk of the Gauntlet.

matches.round: Round 9 (last Swiss round): Astra Arisana against Fire Luxem Zander

players.name: likeBAILEY
players.deck: Astra Arisana, Starfall build, TM32 (Polaris; Cosmic Bolt x2; Angelic Channeling; Three Visits; Floral Arrangement; Gentle Respite; Comet Fall; Calming Breeze; Incapacitate; Wisdom's Reprise; Imbued Topsy Decree; Cosmic Astroscope; Blanch, Weighted Accord and Stifling Fumes in the side)

players.name: Leowong
players.deck: Fire Luxem Zander, Serene Spirit build (Zander, Blinding Steel; Gleaming Cut x3; Lightweaver's Assault x3; Striking Illuminance; Prism Spire; Insignia of the Corhazi; Dungeon Guide; Creative Shock; Turbo Charge; Angelic Channeling; Lost Providence; Pretentious Tongue; Regal Inquisition, Crystallized Destiny, Safeguard Amulet and Blanch in the side)

matches.result: Leowong wins 2-1 (result per Omnidex; the VOD stops during game 2)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters list Weighted Accord in Bailey's side, but note it is weak against Luxem, who often leaves its advanced cards in memory. Stifling Fumes is not expected to come in either. On the Luxem side they name Regal Inquisition, Crystallized Destiny, Safeguard Amulet and Blanch as ways to shore up the matchup.

games.summary: Leowong wins — a triple Gleaming Cut, triple Lightweaver's Assault turn-four kill

beats.text: Bailey gets a Floral Arrangement and herb generation going and sets up Cosmic Bolts. He pitches Gentle Respite for floating memory, but Leowong has a Turbo Charge, a Creative Shock and another Angelic Channeling, and the casters say Leowong is ahead on influence.

Leowong gets Zander, Blinding Steel to level three on the stack with a Dungeon Guide banishing two, and sets up the Insignia of the Corhazi to draw extra cards. Bailey goes to Arisana level three on Dungeon Guide, a new level three the casters have not seen before.

Leowong reveals seven and holds three Lightweaver's Assaults and a Striking Illuminance with two prep counters. Triple Gleaming Cut draws four more cards, and the Striking Illuminance counts every reveal, including the reveals from the Lightweavers. The casters call it one of the highest-roll games they have ever seen: a turn-four kill, and Leowong takes game one.

matches.round: Round 1: Water Umbra Alice mill against Wind Crux Lorraine

players.name: ProAnnn
players.deck: Water Umbra Alice, Phantom Monarch mill (Dynastic Whirlpool, Regal Inquisition, Reflected Blight, Pearled Prayer, Abnegation)

players.name: DuckHats
players.deck: Wind Crux Lorraine, Spirit Ruler (Ghosts of Pendragon, Spirit Blade: Ascension, Aella, Cleansing Reunion, Purifying Thurible)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters discuss Bandersnatch as a taunt-and-recovery option, along with Slip Away and Nullifying Mirror. These are boarding suggestions; the broadcast does not establish which copies ProAnnn brings in.

games.summary: DuckHats wins — Cleansing Reunion disrupts the mill plan and Aella suppresses Ducal Seal

beats.text: DuckHats opens Lorraine, Blademaster with the Dungeon Guide and swings the Sword of Seeking into the Angel Attendant. ProAnnn answers with a Cerulean Decree, and the casters note how many recovery cards the Alice deck packs: Abnegation, Pearled Prayer and more.

DuckHats uses a second Dungeon Guide to reach Lorraine, Spirit Ruler, then materializes Enfeebling Orb. ProAnnn uses Maledictum Vitae for recovery and Regal Inquisition to discard Ghosts of Pendragon; DuckHats retrieves a Ghost with Crux Sight. ProAnnn materializes Ducal Seal to tax the incoming attacks.

DuckHats’s Cleansing Reunion denies ProAnnn’s Reflected Blight retrieval of Dynastic Whirlpool. Imperious Galebind lets Aella return at end of turn to suppress ProAnnn’s Ducal Seal. Facing the next attack turn, ProAnnn concedes.

games.summary: ProAnnn wins — two Dynastic Whirlpools mill DuckHats out after he whiffs on the Dungeon Guide

beats.text: ProAnnn’s Regal Inquisition strips DuckHats’s hand, but the replacement draws still miss Dungeon Guide. ProAnnn later uses Phantasmagoria to recycle his graveyard and mills an Engulf.

ProAnnn finds an Engulf and a Dynastic Whirlpool; the casters count the deck at about 27 cards, so two whirlpools are enough. A Bauble of Abundance gives ProAnnn extra draws, and without the Enfeebling Orb in play DuckHats cannot deny any activations.

DuckHats eventually finds Dungeon Guide, then levels to Lorraine, Spirit Ruler through materialization. ProAnnn materializes Bauble of Abundance and finishes with two Dynastic Whirlpools, tying the match.

games.summary: DuckHats wins — Cleansing Reunion disrupts Reflected Blight and ProAnnn concedes

beats.text: DuckHats holds Purifying Thurible to threaten ProAnnn’s Fracturize setup, then uses it before leveling with Dungeon Guide. Lorraine, Blademaster clears Angel Attendant and draws a card.

ProAnnn plays Extricating Touch. DuckHats responds with Escape the Wreckage, putting Dungeon Guide into memory. ProAnnn removes Spirit Blade: Ascension instead; DuckHats then materializes Lorraine, Spirit Ruler.

After ProAnnn reaches Alice level two, DuckHats uses Cleansing Reunion to remove the target of Reflected Blight. The failed retrieval also leaves Alice without that curse in her lineage. With Resolute Stand but no recovery available, ProAnnn concedes.

matches.sourceNote: Worlds 2026 Swiss Stage VOD, Round 1: captions reviewed from 54:32–103:00 against the Swiss lists and local card text. DuckHats wins 2–1, consistent with Omnidex. Boarding suggestions remain distinct from observed plays. Swiss deck attachments use the explicitly labeled Swiss lists archived by Silvie.gg, rather than the event API’s current Top 8 lists.

matches.round: Round 2: Fire Oblation Ciel against Water Fractals Diao Chan

players.name: Raylam
players.deck: Fire Oblation Ciel, Mirage's Grave (Baleful Oblation, Feu Awakening, Hasty Messenger, Three of Hearts, Incapacitate)

players.name: TeamTrueCaban
players.deck: Water Fractals Diao Chan, Enchantress (Refracting Missile, Shimmering Refraction, Burst Asunder, Glimmering Refusal, Acquiescing Rejection)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters go through TeamTrueCaban's side. Crimson Protective Trinket does not stop fire. Nullifying Mirror and Overlapping Visages are not useful in this matchup. Song of Frost could be the one card to bring in against Devastating Blow variants, but he feels strong about his Oblation matchup.
Raylam plays Rictus Tiding in game two; his registered Swiss list places it in the sideboard. The captions do not establish how many copies he brings in or which cards he removes.

games.summary: Raylam wins — ally pressure and Feu Awakening overwhelm Caban’s defense

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban Fracturizes his Powercell, then uses its floating-memory card for Frostsworn Paladin. Raylam sacrifices the threatened Hasty Messenger to Undeniable Truth. Three of Hearts and another Messenger later clear the Paladin.

Raylam reaches Ciel, Omenbringer and draws from Liminal Guide, then uses Dungeon Guide to reach Mirage’s Grave. Caban builds fractals but remains at level zero after materializing Enfeebling Orb; the casters calculate that his available damage and influence fall short.

Raylam attacks with his allies. Caban uses Enfeebling Orb and targets Hasty Messenger with Shimmering Refraction, but Raylam shows Feu Awakening and Caban concedes. The casters discuss leveling to Diao Chan as a possible alternative in hindsight, not an established misplay.

games.summary: TeamTrueCaban wins — Raylam survives Burst Asunder, but later falls to Refracting Missile

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban opens with an imbued Fractal of Rain and a hand with Refracting Missile, Zhang Jiao and a Glimmering Refusal, everything a Fractals player wants except more fractals. He takes far less pressure than in game one.

Caban develops his fractals and deals damage with Refracting Missile. Raylam reaches Ciel, Omenbringer but cannot find Dungeon Guide. Caban holds Glimmering Refusal for Raylam’s defensive Topsy Decree.

Caban answers Topsy Decree with two Glimmering Refusals. Raylam uses Feu Awakening at level two, discarding his hand and memory so Topsy resolves and grants spellshroud against Burst Asunder. Caban retains his fractals. On a later turn, Shimmering Refraction adds damage; Enfeebling Orb empties Raylam’s hand before Refracting Missile finishes the game.

games.summary: Raylam wins — a third Baleful Oblation breaks through after two are negated

beats.text: Raylam plays a wide aggressive ally strategy, which the casters say is not what Oblation CL usually does but works to pressure Fractals. Fluffy Shopkeep banishes a key card, and Raylam discards a Floating Memory he does not need.

Caban spends Refracting Missile to remove Hasty Messenger. Fractal of Intrusion later discards Raylam’s Incapacitate from memory. Caban then uses Glimmering Refusal on Fluffy Shopkeep to deny Raylam its draw.

Caban negates Raylam’s first two Baleful Oblations. On the following turn, Raylam materializes Manxome Armoire and uses Lost Providence before recollection. A third Oblation resolves after Acquiescing Rejection; the ensuing omen damage and Armoire activation finish the game.

matches.sourceNote: Worlds 2026 Swiss Stage VOD, Round 2. Captions at 138:31–183:14 establish the game order and Raylam’s 2–1 win; targeted interview passages at 191:38–193:55 were also checked. players.deck: Wind Crux Lorraine

sideboardNotes.text: The casters propose Blessed Clergy to limit activations, Dream Fairy to answer Aella, and Tempest Downfall for damage or ally removal. They do not confirm exact boarding changes. Tempest Downfall is later visible in game three.
The casters discuss Annul Spell, Calming Breeze and more attack cards as Lifdrasyl’s options. Annul Spell is visible in game two; exact swaps are not shown.

games.summary: Lifdrasyl wins — repeated Prismatic Edge triggers exhaust Asuna’s hand

beats.text: Asuna establishes two imbued Eternal Magistrates. Lifdrasyl suppresses one with Verdigris Decree, removing its imbue, then attacks the other after leveling to Lorraine, Blademaster. Asuna reclaims it, opening the way for Lifdrasyl to reach level three.

Asuna eventually finds Razorgale Calling with Fairy Whispers and builds toward multiple Razorgales. Lifdrasyl’s Aella repeatedly suppresses Essence Crucible, removing its accumulated counters, while Asuna uses Veiling Breeze to keep combat damage out.

Imperious Galebind reuses Aella, Ghosts of Pendragon and Prismatic Edge, helping Lifdrasyl find his fire card and cut Asuna’s influence. On Asuna’s next turn, Enfeebling Orb forces more cards down. Displace reuses Aella for another Prismatic Edge trigger showing all three elements; Asuna concedes.

games.summary: Asuna wins — three Razorgale triggers with Essence Crucible end the game faster than a Razorgale hit the field in game one

beats.text: Lifdrasyl builds influence with Fluffy Shopkeep and Escape the Wreckage. Asuna levels early, establishes Razorgale Calling and brings out Essence Crucible. The casters later question whether Lifdrasyl lacks Dungeon Guide or is playing around Stifling Trap.

Asuna finds all three Razorgales, while the casters identify a single Verdigris Decree as Lifdrasyl’s answer. Speed Potion helps Asuna recover cards, and Three Visits plus a reclaim set up the remaining damage.

Asuna plays the second and third Razorgales, adding their damage triggers. Essence Crucible boosts the closing damage; the casters explain that Annul Spell cannot stop the Razorgale triggers even if it negates the spell. Asuna ties the match.

games.summary: No winner — time runs out with both players in a tense position, and the round ends as a double loss

beats.text: Lifdrasyl has Verdigris Decree in his opening hand and develops Windmill Engineer. Asuna’s imbued Eternal Magistrate attacks the Engineer, which Lifdrasyl reclaims. Lifdrasyl then levels to Lorraine, Wandering Warrior and brings out Sword of Seeking.

Lifdrasyl plays Dream Fairy targeting Eternal Magistrate. Asuna saves it with Escape the Wreckage and then plays Stifling Gyre instead of replaying Magistrate. The later commentary confirms Gyre names Ghosts of Pendragon. Asuna also uses Incapacitate to stop Ascension after its Sword cost is paid.

In overtime, both players keep Veiling Breeze available. Lifdrasyl materializes Sword of Seeking and shows Spirit Blade: Retribution, but lacks enough influence to activate it. Neither player wins the game; the broadcast confirms a 1–1 draw, worth no match points in this Worlds format.

matches.sourceNote: Worlds Swiss captions reviewed through all three games (224:52–302:27). The caster discussion at 291:50–292:11 confirms Asuna’s game-three Stifling Gyre names Ghosts of Pendragon. Retribution is shown and counted at the end, not activated. The official 1–1 match draw is preserved; the broadcast describes it as a double loss for standings purposes. sideboardNotes.text: The casters discuss Mystic Purifier, Obscured Offering, and Verdigris Decree as options for TheRainGoddess. These are suggestions, not confirmed boarding quantities.

Beastbond Boots and Expel the Departed are identified in Superior’s game-two deck; Expel is milled, not played. Blanche, Sheltering Saint is later seen in hand. The broadcast does not establish boarding quantities or cuts.

games.summary: Superior wins — Enfeebling Orb clears the way for Genbu and Resonating Fugue, backed by Frostbind

beats.text: TheRainGoddess uses Censer of Restful Peace to shut off Superior’s graveyard abilities, with Nullifying Lantern also available in the material deck. The casters note Superior has only two Unbroken Mustangs and may need Fracturize to answer the Censer.

TheRainGoddess starts with Floral Arrangement and Scout the Land, which finds Turbo Charge, and draws extra to fill her memory. She holds Ensnaring Fumes, which the casters call the absolute Genbu killer, but cannot play it with only five cards in hand.

TheRainGoddess’s Verdigris Decree destroys Superior’s Fractal of Rain. Superior uses Primordial Ritual and continues building his graveyard, then uses Enfeebling Orb to leave TheRainGoddess unable to pay for Ensnaring Fumes. Genbu and Resonating Fugue threaten 18 damage; Superior’s Frostbind stops Veiling Breeze to close the game.

games.summary: Superior wins by game loss — the broadcast reports an illegal Cyclical Breeze retrieval under Nullifying Lantern, upheld on appeal

beats.text: Superior shows Beastbond Boots and mills Expel the Departed. He holds Fracturize and removes TheRainGoddess’s Censer of Restful Peace. Later, Throne-Keeper Bullfrog enters with two buff counters alongside Tidestone Bovine and the growing ally board.

TheRainGoddess materializes Backup Charger, then later uses Turbo Charge on the Powercell. Superior keeps applying ally pressure while holding further options; TheRainGoddess still needs Arisanna and Essence Crucible to bring the potion engine online.

TheRainGoddess uses Cyclical Breeze to retrieve Fairy Whispers while Nullifying Lantern makes graveyard cards norm element. The casters report that the table judge issues a game loss because the state cannot be rewound, then confirm that the ruling stands on appeal. Superior wins 2–0.

matches.sourceNote: Worlds 2026 Swiss Stage VOD, Round 4. Targeted caption checks confirm TheRainGoddess’s Censer/Lantern/Verdigris ownership, Superior’s Genbu finish and game-two boarding observations. players.name: Guruthos
players.deck: Fire Oblation Ciel, Mirage's Grave (Baleful Oblation, Feu Awakening, Manxome Armoire, Grande Sonnerie, Orb of Sealing; Flamewreath Call in the sideboard)

players.name: Jett
players.deck: Wind Crux Lorraine, Spirit Ruler (Ghosts of Pendragon, Spirit Blade: Ascension, Prismatic Edge, Aella; Eternal Magistrate and Crystallized Destiny in the sideboard)

sideboardNotes.text: Jett brings in the Eternal Magistrate. The casters call it a thorn in Guruthos's side for games two and three, because it also stops Lost Providence from being activated in the main phase and gives Lorraine time to reach level three.

Before game three, the casters correct their initial Flamewreath Call boarding claim after noticing Guruthos is holding his sideboard. They report Flamewreath Call, Nocturne’s Oblivion, and Heavenly Guide being left out or removed. They discuss Call as a possible answer to Eternal Magistrate; no copy counts are established.

games.summary: Guruthos wins — an initial Oblation punishes Orb of Sealing, then two more beat Veiling Breeze

beats.text: Guruthos uses Creative Shock and Angelic Channeling to prepare fifteen-cost cards and Baleful Oblations. Jett establishes Orb of Sealing, then uses Dungeon Guide and Displace to reach Lorraine, Spirit Ruler before Guruthos reaches level three.

Guruthos orders his level-up triggers so Liminal Guide draws Baleful Oblation, leaving another Oblation and a fifteen-cost card near the top. Lost Providence enters play, while Jett’s Orb of Sealing threatens the fifteen-cost omen.

Guruthos plays the first Baleful Oblation in response to Jett’s Orb of Sealing. On Jett’s next turn, Ghosts of Pendragon rebuild the ally board and draw cards; one returns Enfeebling Orb to the material deck, leaving it unavailable to disrupt Guruthos’s next turn.

Guruthos materializes Manxome Armoire, draws Advent of the Stormcaller with Umbra Sight, and adds it as an omen at end of turn. He plays Baleful Oblation. Jett digs with Crux Sight and Fairy Whispers, then attempts Veiling Breeze. Guruthos responds with another Oblation and uses Armoire to restore a fifteen-cost omen, winning before Breeze resolves.

games.summary: Jett wins — Eternal Magistrate delays Guruthos, and Imperious Galebind stops the Grande Sonnerie finish

beats.text: Jett uses Purifying Thurible to deny Guruthos’s floating memory, then Dungeon Guide and Displace to reach Lorraine, Spirit Ruler. Eternal Magistrate shuts off Guruthos’s Guide plays and Lost Providence activation outside materialization. Jett then materializes Orb of Sealing.

Jett plays Aella during recollection and attacks with his allies. Guruthos uses Chalice of Blood, Umbra Sight, and Abnegation to stay alive. Jett responds to Abnegation with two Spirit Blade: Ascensions: Prismatic Edge draws cards and removes two from Guruthos’s memory, but deals no fire damage. Abnegation then recovers ten.

Resolute Stand buys Guruthos another turn. He retains Baleful Oblation and materializes Grande Sonnerie, then finds another fifteen-cost card. Jett’s Imperious Galebind denies the weapon damage needed to finish. Guruthos concedes without executing the proposed Oblation–Feu Awakening line.

games.summary: Jett wins — Aella and Prismatic Edge deny Ciel level three, then Lorraine lands the final weapon attack

beats.text: Guruthos goes first and uses Creative Shock to discard Golden Checkmate before leveling, choosing speed over a Backup Charger turn. Gentle Respite gives him another draw and floating memory.

Jett plays Eternal Magistrate to block Guruthos’s Guide acceleration, then uses Dungeon Guide and Displace to reach Lorraine, Spirit Ruler himself. Ghosts of Pendragon builds his board. Spirit Blade: Ascension brings in Prismatic Edge, which reveals wind, water, and Guruthos’s fire card for the full effect, including three damage.

Guruthos has Baleful Oblation and Feu Awakening, and uses Resolute Stand’s alternate cost to preserve cards for leveling. Jett’s Aella suppresses Prismatic Edge; its end-step return removes memory and denies Ciel level three. Guruthos materializes Chalice of Blood instead. On Jett’s next turn, ally attacks trigger the Chalice draw, but Guruthos finds Gentle Respite rather than another Resolute Stand. Lorraine’s Prismatic Edge attack finishes the game.

matches.sourceNote: Worlds 2026 Swiss Stage VOD, Round 5; Jett wins 2–1 per Omnidex. Game-one finish checked at 406:02–417:43; games two and three checked at 419:04–456:34. Game two ends in concession after Imperious Galebind stops the proposed weapon finish. In game three Guruthos has Oblation, but Jett prevents Ciel level three before the final weapon attack. Boarding commentary includes an explicit correction about Flamewreath Call. Swiss attachments use Silvie.gg’s explicitly labeled Swiss lists. The game-one opening was also reviewed at 395:19–406:02; the casters speculate about trigger handling while a judge is present, but do not establish a missed-trigger penalty.

The casters discuss Nullifying Mirror and Jianyu, Fate's Premonition as Noel’s options. Nullifying Mirror is subsequently shown in game two; exact swaps are not reported.

games.summary: Noel wins — Burst Asunder ends the game while Asuna is still on Gwendalin

beats.text: Noel reserves Fractal of Intrusion to cast Refracting Missile before Intrusion’s on-enter resolves, then uses the floating memory to discard Asuna’s Speed Potion. Asuna has already found an opening Razorgale Calling with Scout the Land.

Asuna materializes Viridian Protective Trinket and later plays Eternal Magistrate, imbuing it with two Three Visits. Noel builds fractals, deals four with Refracting Missile and materializes Nullifying Lantern.

Noel sends Burst Asunder while Asuna remains on Gwendolyn, Spirit of Wind. Asuna has no answer and loses game one. The two Three Visits are in memory; the casters’ discussion of whether keeping one would have saved him is inconclusive.

games.summary: Asuna wins — three Razorgales and Essence Crucible force Noel’s concession

beats.text: Asuna opens with Fluffy Shopkeep. Noel’s Acquiescing Rejection stops Reclaim when Asuna declines the draw. Noel later changes Fractal of Intrusion’s discard choice from Razorgale Calling to Stifling Trap; Asuna levels to Arisanna and establishes three Razorgales.
Noel materializes Nullifying Mirror and develops Fractal of Snow. Asuna brings out Essence Crucible, keeps Distilled Water through the level cost and finds Speed Potion for the closing turn.

Noel contests Speed Potion with Acquiescing Rejection and Glimmering Refusal. The casters explain that brewing still gives Essence Crucible its counter despite the negation. Noel concedes with further Razorgale damage available.

games.summary: Asuna wins — Obscured Offering protects Crucible, then three wind spells finish

beats.text: Noel opens with two Fractals of Snow and keeps Fracturize for Essence Crucible instead of using it to build another fractal. Asuna uses Reclaim while Noel is committed to Backup Charger, then levels to Arisanna and plays the discounted Razorgale Calling.

Asuna sets up Viridian Protective Trinket, Tend the Land and two Speed Potions. Noel responds to the second brew with Fracturize targeting Essence Crucible. Obscured Offering gives Crucible spellshroud, preserving its counters; the proposed defensive Zephyr is not the play used.
The Speed Potions recover cards through agility. In the end phase, Asuna plays Veiling Breeze, Calming Breeze and Three Visits for three Razorgale damage each, winning the match 2–1.

matches.sourceNote: Worlds Swiss captions reviewed from the match opening through its conclusion (480:37–522:09). The “game three” call at 493:33 is corrected to game two at 495:57. beats.text: Jayare’s Three of Hearts attacks Raylam’s Hasty Messenger. Raylam plays Escape the Wreckage to save it, then replays Hasty and discards Ionized Asceticism to set up a fifteen-cost omen.

beats.text: Jayare opens with Three of Hearts, and Raylam has the Hasty Messenger and Escape the Wreckage start again. Raylam discards a Liminal Guide, and the casters say a double Three of Hearts would have turned it for him.
The casters call out the cards in Jayare's grip: Impact Hammer, Heated Vengeance and Blazing Throw, with all the pieces for a lethal turn two into four.

Jayare plays Heated Vengeance into a big swing at Raylam's face, hits with the Impact Hammer, and throws it with Blazing Throw. Raylam has no answer. The casters call it an insane turn-two Turbo line and say the two games took only 15 minutes. Raylam goes on to win game three, which the VOD does not show.

DuckHats plays imbued Eternal Magistrate in game two. It restricts GlenyBoi’s material deck outside GlenyBoi’s materialize phase, leaving DuckHats free to use his own Dungeon Guides. The broadcast also discusses Annul Spell and Calming Breeze as options.

games.summary: GlenyBoi wins — repeated Prismatic Edge triggers and Ghosts draws force a concession

beats.text: Both players build influence with Fluffy Shopkeep and Backup Charger. DuckHats reaches Lorraine, Blademaster with Dungeon Guide. When GlenyBoi later uses Displace to level, DuckHats responds with his own Displace before the opposing Prismatic Edge engine can strip his memory.
GlenyBoi develops Ghosts of Pendragon and Spirit Blade: Ascension, keeping DuckHats low on influence through Prismatic Edge. A fire card in memory enables damage as well as the wind effect.

games.summary: GlenyBoi wins — Annul Spell opens the level-up, then Aella and Ascension take over

beats.text: DuckHats reveals Eternal Magistrate while imbuing an Engineer, then plays Magistrate to constrain GlenyBoi. DuckHats breaks a hard-materialized Drawn Blade in combat and reaches level three ahead of GlenyBoi.

GlenyBoi’s Rally the Peasants misses. He later uses Annul Spell against DuckHats’s Imperious Galebind, gets the Lorraine draw and finds Dungeon Guide. That lets him reach Spirit Ruler, then play Ghosts of Pendragon and find Ascension.

GlenyBoi draws more Ghosts, Aella and Ascension. Aella suppresses Prismatic Edge, and Crux Sight returns Ascension for another Edge trigger. DuckHats loses more memory cards and concedes without finding the Crux cards to recover.

matches.sourceNote: Worlds Swiss captions reviewed at 560:00–592:55. Both games end in DuckHats’s concession. games.summary: TeamTrueCaban wins — he goes first with five fractals and Zhang Jiao, and Sano concedes

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban goes first with an imbued Fractal of Rain and builds toward Zhang Jiao, Way of Peace. He bottoms an extra Acquiescing Rejection and Burst Asunder while setting up the draw.

The casters note that Sano's list has no Clarent, so he has less defense against Burst Asunder. Sano has no Stifling Trap to stop the Zhang Jiao draws. TeamTrueCaban has eight cards in hand and four fractals, effectively 12 influence, with Glimmering Refusals backing up the kill turn.

The casters call it a default win for TeamTrueCaban, who only had to play the cards, and Sano concedes early to keep time for game two. The casters say TM32 are happy to concede early with Wind Krux to avoid a double loss.

games.summary: TeamTrueCaban wins — Nullifying Mirror limits Sano’s answers to the final Burst Asunder

beats.text: TeamTrueCaban uses Acquiescing Rejection on Fluffy Shopkeep. Sano allows the two-card draw, so Shopkeep resolves. TeamTrueCaban later uses Fractal of Intrusion to discard Ghosts of Pendragon, then kills Shopkeep with Refracting Missile.

matches.round: Round 1 (Day 1) — 2025 World Champion in a round-one pairing

players.name: Dit
players.deck: Water Genbu Guo Jia (Fractal of Polar Depths mill-out)

players.name: boeboe
players.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (Fatestone / Angelic Channeling main deck)

matches.result: Dit wins 2-1 (game 3 awarded after a game loss to boeboe)

sideboardNotes.text: boeboe sideboards in Nullifying Lantern (turns every graveyard card to no element, so Fractal of Polar Depths mills nothing and Deluge goes offline), Psychopomp's Gale (banishes the whole graveyard) and extra Dream Fairies. The casters also expect fast-speed Fantasia removal to stay out because Dit played an unprotected Polar Depths.
The casters predict Dit brings in the third Unbroken Mustang, Song of Frost and the last Engulf, to answer the Lantern and the dragon combo. These are caster predictions, not a confirmed list.

games.summary: Dit wins by Polar Depths mill-out

beats.text: Dit opens with an early Fractal of Polar Depths and Fabled Sapphire Fatestone, milling Seaside Ringleader and Fractal of Rain on turn one. It is rare to see main-deck Fantasia removal, so the unprotected Polar Depths goes unpunished.

boeboe has a clunky opener (three Dungeon Guides and little other Wind). They play Angelic Channeling before levelling, imbue a Windmill Engineer to show a Reclaim, and bank Fatestone of Heaven cards under Channeling for later.

boeboe levels Guo Jia quickly using Dungeon Guide banishes for quest counters, flips Seiryuu first (ten counters versus Genbu's nine), and sends an Arcane Blast to their banishment off the attack. A short judge ruling checks how Angelic Channeling's top/bottom trigger resolves.
Dit plays a defensive Frostsworn Paladin game rather than going for an unsafe lethal swing, and Primordial Ritual answers the attacking Paladin in response to the dragon's attack trigger.

boeboe plays Optical Control naming action cards, so Dit's Fugue costs four more. Auspicious Manifestation banishes Seiryuu so it returns awake at end of turn and can taunt. The line buys time but cannot beat the mill-out plan.

Dit plays three Fractal of Polar Depths in a row, stacking them to mill boeboe's library (target self, self, then opponent). boeboe concedes. Naming Fantasia instead of action cards would have been the only way to catch it.

games.summary: boeboe wins with a sideboarded lock and Arcane Blast

beats.text: boeboe opens with an imbued Benediction Angel and Dream Fairies. The fairies stop Dit from playing Bullfrog or Frostsworn Paladin for most of the game.
Nullifying Lantern hits the board. All cards in graveyards become no element, so Dit's Polar Depths mill and Deluge turn off. Dit holds Unbroken Mustang to remove it.
Dit plays both Unbroken Mustangs. boeboe answers with Stifling Trap, so the Lantern survives. Dit has no Primordial Ritual to sacrifice the Mustang and fizzle the trap.

boeboe adds Censer of Restful Peace and then Purifying Thurible. Dit's Fracturize answers the Sensor but not the Lantern, because of layering. boeboe keeps Aella, Zephyr's Hand ready to save the Lantern, and holds Psychopomp's Gale.
Dit stays alive with Song of Frost, Enfeebling Orb, Spalling Cleanse and Beastbond Boots, flips Genbu, and tries to dodge the dragon. The round timer runs low as boeboe stays patient.

Dit negates the first dragon attack trigger with Song of Frost. boeboe uses Byakko's Command to wake the dragon so it attacks again, and then fires the stored Arcane Blast for 11 damage that Dit cannot stop.

games.summary: Dit wins — game loss to boeboe for an illegal deck

beats.text: With about three minutes left, both players agree to try game three. In the rush, boeboe shuffles the generated Arcane Blast into their deck. They call the judge themselves, but the judges rule an illegal deck and give a game loss. Dit wins the match 2-1.

matches.round: Round 2 (Day 1) — Suited debuts against Astra Arisanna

players.name: TlsoVotl
players.deck: Fire Suited (Proxy Vault Duchess's Thorns, Fiery Interference)

players.name: Aqua
players.deck: Wind Astra Arisanna (Polaris, Cosmic Bolt glimpse)

sideboardNotes.text: TlsoVotl is expected to bring in Infernal Vessel and Safeguard Amulet (the casters doubt Nullifying Mirror makes it, as Aqua does not imbue). In the post-match interview, TlsoVotl also names Pseudo Trickery and Mortal Ambition as side tech against champion-cleave decks such as Lorraine.
Aqua is expected to bring in extra Imperial Countermeasure and Regenerate for more healing. Aqua is on the play for game 2 because they chose after losing game 1.

games.summary: TlsoVotl wins on card advantage and a clutch Fiery Interference

beats.text: TlsoVotl wins the roll and opens with Four of Spades. Suited cards replace themselves via Cardistry, so TlsoVotl keeps eight or more cards in influence and rebuilds the board quickly after Aqua's sweeps.

Aqua levels to Arisanna 2 and sets up the Polaris plan. Herbs sacrificed by pairs draw cards and add counters to Polaris. Calming Breeze (negates up to three damage) holds off early attacks, and Polaris and Meteor Strike clear the ally board twice.
TlsoVotl lands Six of Hearts and Arthur, Young Heir for a big swing that puts Aqua's spirit low. Aqua answers with Cosmic Bolt on Arthur and Three Visits to heal.
TlsoVotl holds Fiery Interference. In response to Aqua's Serene Spirit heal, it prevents the recovery and the final attacks go through. Aqua cannot stabilize before level three.

games.summary: Aqua wins with defensive cards and Cosmic Bolts

beats.text: Aqua starts with two Calming Breezes, two Gentle Beseeches and Gentle Respite. TlsoVotl's hand has few cheap allies and uses Backup Charger to fix it.

TlsoVotl commits Three of Hearts, Rouge and Eight of Hearts (sacrificing allies to reduce its cost). Aqua sweeps with Polaris and then Meteor Strike (via Cosmic Astroscope and Star Calling), and holds Safeguard Amulet.
Imperial Countermeasure and the Astra Sight glimpse keep Aqua alive. Two Cosmic Bolts take TlsoVotl's spirit down and Aqua closes out the game.

games.summary: TlsoVotl wins in overtime with Verita and Arthur

beats.text: TlsoVotl goes first and opens Four of Hearts into Arthur, Young Heir on turn two. Aqua has no Arisanna on turn one, so Polaris is two turns away.

Aqua uses Angelic Channeling to put Meteor Strike on top. After a Dungeon Guide level up, Aqua wipes the board with Meteor Strike via Cosmic Astroscope, and Polaris with Calming Breeze and Stifling Gyre blunt the follow-up.

TlsoVotl rebuilds with Verita (free by banishing suited allies from the graveyard) and The Duchess. Aqua stays alive with two Imperial Countermeasures but is down to 20 life, and the match enters overtime.

TlsoVotl sequences Arthur's swing first, then attacks with Verita and the others. Aqua has only a Cosmic Bolt to answer the board and is one glimpse short of stabilizing. TlsoVotl takes the match 2-1.

matches.round: Round 3 (Day 1) — Water Exia Jin mirror

players.name: Noel
players.deck: Water Exia Jin (Chess Club build: Huaji of Abyssal Fall, Sunce, Looking Glass)

players.name: Tress
players.deck: Water Exia Jin (Regal mill-out build: four Regals, Dynastic Whirlpool side)

sideboardNotes.text: Tress brings in three Dynastic Whirlpool (mill 15) after Noel's deck milled with no anti-mill tech in game 1. The casters also expect Verdant Protective Trinket.
Noel brings in a fourth Regal for the mill race, more Engulfs and Crimson Rupture (Regalia removal). The casters note Noel plays no Dynastic Whirlpool, Tabula or Chime of Eternity.

games.summary: Tress wins — survives Noel’s final attack to complete the mill-out

beats.text: Both players start the long Jin mirror with Spirit of Serene Water. Noel uses Gentle Respite and Back-up Charger well and uses Dungeon Guide to hit Jin level three first.
Noel plays Regal Inquisition to strip Tress's hand, leaving only Angel cards. Tress answers with Angelic Channeling, Fractal of Waves and Quicksilver Grail to rebuild.
Seething Intercession finds Return to the Archive, then Enrage, Engulf and a Regal. Banished cards cannot be discarded by a Regal, so these three hits give Tress a protected advantage.
Tress sets up Shade-Mist Priestess (recover one on every damage) and keeps a Regal in banishment. With four Regals, Tress changes the plan to a mill-out, and Noel has no anti-mill tech.
Noel transforms Huaji into Huaji of Abyssal Fall and adds Sunce for big unpreventable-damage attacks. Relentless Outburst deals the damage, but Shademist Priestess recovers the triggers.
Noel has already drawn out of cards. Noel goes all in at the end, but Tress shows a heal and Mend Flesh and survives.

games.summary: Noel wins — Tress runs out of healing, tying the match 1–1

beats.text: Both players play more carefully: Noel holds Backup Charger for a level up, and Tress plays Topsy Decree to deny Noel's float. The two sides trade Angelic Channeling and Fractal Fracturize tricks to set up top-of-deck cards.
Tress uses Dynastic Whirlpool to mill the cards Noel put on top with Channeling: three Regals and two Engulfs go to the graveyard. This removes Noel's protection and the main way to mill Tress.

Noel switches to a damage plan. Shuangji, Berserker Plate, Fracturize and an Enrage push huge swings, and Tress answers with Crimson Rupture on the Shuangji plus Pearled Prayer, Regenerate and Serene Spirit.
Tress digs for a heal using Tome of Abyssal Heaven but cannot find a second one. Noel wins game two with damage, tying the match 1–1 as time expires. The casters praise Noel for playing to outs.

matches.round: Round 4 (Day 1) — Fractals Diao Chan against Genbu

players.name: TeamTrueCaban
players.deck: Water Fractals Diao Chan (influence-denial build: four Fractal of Intrusion, Acquiescing Rejection, Topsy Decree)

players.name: Superior
players.deck: Water Genbu Guo Jia

matches.result: Draw — 1-1 in games, game 3 drawn at time

sideboardNotes.text: The casters predict Caban brings in Crystalline Mirror (to remove Safeguard Amulet), Expel the Departed against Polar Depths, Song of Frost and perhaps Delusional Vapors. These are caster predictions, not a confirmed list.
Superior brings in Expel the Departed, which Caban expected, and adds Regal Inquisition, Engulf and Beastbond Boots. Superior also chooses to play first.

games.summary: Caban wins — influence denial and a Burst Asunder that Superior cannot stop

beats.text: Caban plays a Fractals list that mostly runs Fractal of Intrusion, Acquiescing Rejection and four Topsy Decrees, so Superior's float and memory are banished each turn. The goal is to keep Superior's influence too low to flip Genbu.

Superior starts with imbued Fractal of Rain, then Safeguard Amulet, Tidestone Bovine and Fractal of Polar Depths. But the mills are poor and the key Polar Depths and Stratagem cards fall into the graveyard.

Caban Fracturizes cards to add fractals, uses Refracting Missile to pull out Safeguard Amulet, and negates every important play with Glimmering Refusal and Acquiescing Rejection. Superior's Diamond Ribbon gives influence but cannot get a play through.
With six or more fractals, Burst Asunder deals 14 or more. Superior responds with Cerulean Decree, but Caban pays and Burst Asunder resolves for lethal.

games.summary: Superior wins — Caban's Burst Asunder is Engulfed and Superior steals the race

beats.text: Superior plays Fractal of Polar Depths on turn one, unprotected, and Expel the Departed from the side to stop Caban's Zhang Jiao turn. Caban's Sapphire Fatestone mill and Return to the Archive give Caban a good start.
Caban tries an imbued Topsy Decree on Superior's Frostsworn Paladin trigger, but Superior has an imbued Cerulean Decree and a Title Lock. Superior comes out ahead with a 3/4 Paladin.
Superior double-activates Fugue to threaten lethal, but Caban holds two Glimmering Refusals. Superior then rebuilds influence with Seaside Ringleader and Diamond Ribbon and levels Guo Jia.
Caban has Burst Asunder and six fractals (14 damage) but no third Glimmering Refusal, so Superior uses Engulf on the Burst. Caban tests the waters and learns he is out of refusals.

Superior keeps the board with Shademist Priestess and Frostsworn Paladin. A fast Refracting Missile for eight damage nearly wins for Caban, but Superior activates Genbu to survive and wins the game on Fast Cure.

games.summary: Draw — time expires

beats.text: With only nine minutes left, both players have to race. Superior's Shademist Priestess recovers damage, and Caban Fracturizes the Safeguard Amulet and builds fractals.

Caban builds a lethal line in the last turns (Refracting Missile, Glimmering Refusal, extra fractals). Superior holds Engulf and Cerulean Decree. Caban plays two extra fractals to beat an Engulf plus recovery, but Superior has Engulf and Cerulean Decree instead. The game ends in a draw.

matches.round: Round 4 (Day 1) — Both players 3-0; level-three Diao Chan (Full Bloom) against Aetherwing Diana

players.name: Shuteemdown
players.deck: Water Tera Diao Chan (level 3 Wither plan, Full Bloom, Shademist Priestess)

players.name: Zetdivx
players.deck: Water Aetherwing Diana (Take Aim, Aquamirage Whisper, Nimble Longbowman)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters suggest Viridian Protective Trinket, Engulf and Song of Frost for Shuteemdown. Trinket and Engulf appear in game two.
The casters suggest Expel the Departed and Aetheric Reforging for Zetdivx. Expel is played in game two; the number boarded in is unconfirmed.

games.summary: Zetdivx wins — Frozen Dismissal forces Shuteemdown hands-down, then Take Aim for 11

beats.text: Shuteemdown has two Acquiescing Rejections early. Zetdivx lets them resolve (giving four cards) because he needs to become distant with Undercurrent Vantage, then plays Prudent Nock and Aquamirage Whisper for the first swing.
Zetdivx removes Shademist Priestess with Charge the Soul and uses Aetheric Reforging to banish the float, slowing Diao Chan's level up. Art of War and Fractal of Polar Depths fill out the board.

Shuteemdown reaches Diao Chan level three with Dungeon Guide. Zetdivx answers with Frozen Dismissal and Mana Resonance. Shuteemdown pays four, but everything gets Wither counters and the Wither tax strips the rest of the hand.
With no Song of Frost, Zetdivx's Take Aim (11 damage, from distant Diana plus the Mirage Whisper) closes out the game.

games.summary: Zetdivx wins — plays around Engulf, then Krustallan Archer and Nimble Longbowman close it

beats.text: Shuteemdown materializes Viridian Protective Trinket and Engulfs Undercurrent Vantage so Zetdivx cannot become distant. Zetdivx had kept enough other distant enablers to push through.
Aether Calibration finds Weaving Manastream, and Krustallan Archer plus Diana's glimpse keep the damage flowing. Zetdivx passes up an immediate dive because Diana players tax the opponent first.
Shuteemdown materializes Crystalline Mirror and tries Fractal of Waves and Even-tide Lure, but Expel the Departed from Zetdivx's side answers the Fantasia.
Zetdivx fractures Ranger Strides in response to hand-down plays, then plays Nimble Longbowman (distant) and Krustallan Archer for lethal.

players.deck: Razorgale Arisanna (Essence Crucible, Aesan Protector, Bandit, Gaze Leader)

games.summary: Jett wins with stacked Razorgale damage

beats.text: LongN has a smooth start: imbued Fractal of Rain, a level up to Guo Jia, Tidestone Bovine and Seaside Ringleader, plus mills that fill the graveyard for Fractal of Polar Depths.

Jett builds a large hand with Windmill Engineer and a Bandit, Gaze Leader that eats floating memory. Razorgale Calling and Essence Crucible deal repeated damage. LongN's Dream Fairy and Censer of Restful Peace slow Jett down, but cannot stop the grind.

Jett plays Essence Crucible and stacks Razorgale triggers so that LongN cannot respond with one answer. Aesan Protector holds back LongN's attack. The Genbu player cannot flip the Fatestone in time, and Jett wins game 1.

games.summary: Jett wins — game loss given to LongN after a judge call

beats.text: Both players play a long, grinding game. LongN sets up Fractal of Polar Depths and Conniving Plans, and Jett responds with Purifying Thurible, Essence Crucible and Razorgale Calling pressure.
A judge reviews an error by the Genbu player. The judge decision is a game loss for LongN, which gives Jett the game and the match. Jett ends Day 1 round 5 at 5-0.

matches.round: Round 6 (Day 1) — Aetherwing Diana mirror: beatdown build against Astra build

players.name: Celednb
players.deck: Water Aetherwing Diana (beatdown: Krustallan Archer, Take Aim, Cheshire Cat, Palvor Sword)

players.name: Quakems
players.deck: Water Astra Aetherwing Diana (Cosmic Focus glimpse combo, Angelic Channeling)

sideboardNotes.text: Celednb brings in Topsy Decree and Unbroken Mustang to remove the Aquamirage Whisper before it gains value. The casters also see Palvor Sword and Snow White as options.

Quakems brings in Dissuading Aether (gives an attack -3, so Diana's hit trigger stays off), Engulf and possibly Shademist Priestess. Quakems says later that Lake of Grieving Chill is a fifth Fracturize for Censer of Restful Peace.

games.summary: Quakems wins — Celednb concedes to the Astra setup

beats.text: Quakems opens with Backstep, then Aquamirage Whisper and Diana level one. Tactical Retreat ends combat to deny Celednb the hit trigger, and Quakems keeps three or more float in the graveyard for a free level three.

At level three, Quakems glimpses huge amounts of the deck and sets up Cosmic Focus and Cometary Vantage for the next turn. A Teardrop Diadem threatens a draw-three, with Celednb on the back foot and without Cheshire Cat or Mad Hatter.
Celednb concedes to Quakems’s Astra setup.

games.summary: Celednb wins — Krustallan Archer pressure and a Frostbind on Dungeon Guide

beats.text: Celednb's list now has Topsy Decree and Unbroken Mustang to take out the Whisper. Aether Calibration and Charge the Soul set up a Weaving Manastream, and Krustallan Archer eats the float for repeated hits.
Quakems uses Dissuading Aether to give the attack -3, but Celednb adds Take Aim to push the damage anyway. Quakems channels Cosmic Focus, Cometary Vantage and Constellation's Blessing to the top.
Quakems tries Dungeon Guide to hit level three for a seven-damage glimpse-eight swing. Celednb has Frostbind and negates Dungeon Guide. Quakems cannot keep up with the damage and scoops.

games.summary: Quakems wins — survives Celednb’s attack, then finishes with Cosmic Focus

beats.text: Quakems goes first and passes. Celednb uses Palvor Sword to banish the graveyard, which denies Quakems the free Teardrop Diadem turn, but Quakems is at 25 life with only five damage counters.
Quakems sets up Stellar Cosmos and two Cosmic Focuses (stacked two cards apart). Flash Grenade, Refreshing Charge and Diana's negate-unless-two ability absorb Celednb's Archer attacks.
Celednb goes all in with Ranger Strides, three Krustallan Archers and a Charge the Soul. The math is one damage short, and Quakems survives at two life.
Quakems glimpses into Cometary Vantage and swings with Cosmic Focus for lethal. Celednb has no Frostbind this time.

matches.round: Round 7 (Day 1) — Off-meta combo matchup: Umbra Tristan against Arcane Rai

players.name: Anjuhro
players.deck: Wind Umbra Tristan (Stifling Trap, Hexbound Blade, Shadow's Claw, Heavenly Guide)

players.name: Hyouka
players.deck: Wind Arcane Rai (Careful Study, Tome of Sacred Lightning, Ionized Asceticism)

games.summary: Hyouka wins — a chained draw turn at level three

beats.text: Both players start slowly. Hyouka imbues Windmill Engineer and sets up an Arcane Elemental plan. Anjuhro answers Dungeon Guide twice with Stifling Trap and uses Beseech of the Winds and Purifying Thurible to deny the Reclaim value.
Hyouka reaches Rai level two and then level three. Lost Providence, Tome of Sacred Lightning and chained Careful Study / Scry the Skies draws rebuild a huge hand from a five-card start.
Arcane Elemental and Disorienting Winds return the elemental to hand to attack again. Anjuhro cannot keep up, and Hyouka wins game 1 without losing influence.

games.summary: Hyouka wins — Ionized Asceticism and Arcane Blasts through the only Abnegation

beats.text: Anjuhro sideboards in answers and goes wide: Tariff Ring, Shadow's Claw, Shadow Dancer and Dungeon Guides to level up. The casters call out that Anjuhro knows Hyouka's hand from the earlier game.

Hyouka uses Surveil the Winds, Scry the Skies and Tome of Sacred Lightning to stack the top of the deck. Aella (Zephyr's Hand) and Tariff Ring from Anjuhro threaten to disrupt, and Anjuhro holds Abnegation for protection.

Hyouka plays Ionized Asceticism (draw seven, banish everything, lose levels) and Advent-style banish effects. Each Arcane card banished adds Arcane Blast damage, and Shattering Discharge finishes. Anjuhro's lone Abnegation is already used, so the lethal swing resolves.

matches.round: Round 8 (Day 1) — both players 6-1 and already through to Day 2

players.name: Zorr
players.deck: Water Genbu Guo Jia (Fractal of Polar Depths mill, Strategem, Unbroken Mustang)

players.name: Hessu
players.deck: Fire Silvie slimes (Storm Slime, Ethereal Slime, Creative Shock, Nullifying Lantern main)

sideboardNotes.text: The casters predict Zorr brings in the last Unbroken Mustang, Orb of Sealing (to turn banished slimes face down so Storm Slime hits less), Beastbond Boots and Excalibur.

Hessu's side includes Viridian Protective Trinket and Intensified Pyre. Hessu says in the interview that he plays Nullifying Lantern and Viridian Protective Trinket because they are strong in general, not only against Genbu.

games.summary: Hessu wins — Ethereal Slimes beat Genbu before it can flip

beats.text: Hessu opens with Gentle Respite, levels Silvie and uses Blissful Calling to find Baby Gray Slime. Baby Red Slime kills Zorr's Tidestone Bovine with Silvie's level-one buff counter.

Zorr gets a fast start with Fractal Polar Depths, Bovine and several floating memory cards, with six quest counters early. After the Bovines die, Zorr stays near Genbu's flip but is repeatedly short of counters.

Hessu goes to level two, plays Ethereal Slime and Lustrous Slime (play two for each), and clears Frostsworn Paladin. Zorr's Primordial Ritual leaves him unable to hold Title Lock, and slimes flood the board.

Hessu's main-deck Nullifying Lantern blanks the Polar Depths and Strategem combo. Zorr removes it with Unbroken Mustang and flips Genbu at level three, but does not activate Genbu on the first attack, and Hessu uses Slime Eruption (a skill, not a spell) to kill it.
With Genbu dead, Hessu swings with Baby Red and Ethereal Slime for lethal.

games.summary: Hessu wins with double Storm Slime

beats.text: Hessu opens with Blissful Calling again. Zorr's Orb of Sealing is a side card meant to limit banished slimes, and the casters track all four Storm Slimes (two in Hessu's hand).
Zorr fights for the board with Seaside Ringleader and Primordial Ritual, and plays Frostsworn Paladin. But Hessu's Ghastly Slime, Baby Silver Slime and Ethereal Slime keep the board wide.

Hessu plays Nullifying Lantern and Viridian Protective Trinket against Zorr's graveyard plan, a regalia lock. Zorr uses Unbroken Mustang on the Lantern and Safeguard Amulet, but a Spalling Cleanse is not enough.
Hessu sacrifices Horn of Beastcalling to play Storm Slime for free, and then a second Storm Slime. With five or more slimes banished, both hit for lethal through Genbu's spell protection.

matches.round: Round 9 (final round, Day 1) — win-and-in for Day 2

players.name: likeBAILEY
players.deck: Razorgale Arisanna (Essence Crucible, Protector Raccoon / Bandit Gaze Leader package)

players.name: Vernosius
players.deck: Water Luxem Zander (Zander Deft Executioner, Lightweaver's Assault, Striking Illuminance)

sideboardNotes.text: Bailey's sideboard has 12 unique main-deck cards and no material-deck cards. The casters expect more Scatter Essence, Purifying Thurible, Topsy Decree, Stifling Gyre and Verdigris Decree against the level-three deck.
Vernosius is expected to add the fourth Engulf and Blanch (holds Razorgale down). He has no real answer to the raccoons other than Engulf or hoping Bailey does not draw one.

games.summary: Bailey wins — turn-one Protector Raccoon, then Essence Crucible

beats.text: Bailey plays Protector Raccoon on turn one, banishing Vernosius's Gentle Respite from the graveyard. Raccoon, Bandit and a reclaim eat floating memory repeatedly and the Luxem deck cannot build influence on its way to level three.

Vernosius is forced to Fracturize his own and Bailey's Power Cell for float, banish cards at random for Zander, and has to level with few cards. Fractal of Waves and Verdigris Decree are all he can find.

Bailey levels to Arisanna, plays two Razorgales, then Essence Crucible. A Speed Potion brewed after the second Razorgale deals big damage with each trigger, and Bailey wins with the potion plus Windmill Engineer.

games.summary: Vernosius wins — Striking Illuminance with Incap lethal while Bailey stays on Spirit

beats.text: Vernosius goes first and plays Gentle Respite without punishment. Bailey has no raccoon on turn one, only a Razorgale start and Backup Charger.

Bandit scavenges and eats the graveyard again, but Vernosius uses a pair of Exploit Vulnerability to return Zander's card. He hits level three with Dungeon Guide and then Lost Providence, with Zander Blinding Steel in play.

Vernosius plays Striking Illuminance with Lightweaver's Assault, and Incap on Bailey's Skirting Step. Bailey is still on Spirit of Wind and takes lethal. The casters say Bailey waited too long to level.

games.summary: Bailey wins — Essence Crucible with Agility Three after Vernosius's Shroud in Mist is illegal

beats.text: Bailey opens with Bandit and Purifying Thurible, then builds a wide board with Protector Raccoon, a second raccoon and Viridian Protective Trinket. The raccoons make Vernosius's Gentle Respite and channelling bad.

Vernosius lands Dungeon Guide with no Stifling Trap. Double Gleaming Cut and Channelling combos restore his influence. He plays Blanch, but Bailey's raccoon board threatens it. Shroud in Mist cannot be paid because of the Trinket's extra cost, and a judge fixes the illegal play.

Bailey reaches Arisanna, plays Razorgale Calling at a reduced price and then Essence Crucible. A Speed Potion, Fairy Whispers and Agility Three give the three wind activations needed, and Bailey wins the match for a 6-3 start to Day 2.

matches.round: Round 10 (Day 2, Round 1) — Genbu master against Razorgale Arisanna

players.name: Superior
players.deck: Water Genbu Guo Jia (London-winning list, Diamond Ribbon package, Shademist Priestess)

players.name: Asuna
players.deck: Razorgale Arisanna (Essence Crucible, Stifling Gyre, Obscured Offering, Censer of Restful Peace)

sideboardNotes.text: Asuna brings in two Ensnaring Fumes, Scatter Essence and Blessed Clergy, and the casters also suggest Dream Fairy. Asuna's main deck already has two Obscured Offering and two Innervate Agility.

Superior brings in Beastbond Boots, Expel the Departed, an Engulf and the second Excalibur, Cleansing Light, as the only answer to Essence Crucible. These are caster predictions, partly confirmed by the cards that appear in play.

games.summary: Superior wins on Guo Jia level one — a 31-damage Genbu attack

beats.text: Asuna plays a turn-one Razorgale Calling and Essence Crucible, then Stifling Gyre naming Frostsworn Paladin and an early Censer of Restful Peace.
Superior has two Fractal of Polar Depths in hand. Fractal of Rain and Tidestone Bovine fill the graveyard, and Safeguard Amulet buys a turn while Guo Jia stays at level one.

Superior flips Genbu on turn three with six quest counters from the Bovine and Fabled Sapphire Fatestone. Resonating Fugue swaps life and power so Genbu is huge (with nine or more water cards, then 31 damage). Asuna has no Veiling Breeze in hand after the Gyre and Razorgale plays, and loses.

games.summary: Asuna wins — Essence Crucible under Quicksilver Grail, then a Tempest Downfall for 11

beats.text: Superior has Expel the Departed and Engulf from the sideboard. Unbroken Mustang kills the Censer of Restful Peace, and Superior mills Seaside Ringleader and a second Excalibur, so the answers to Essence Crucible leave his deck.

Asuna puts Essence Crucible under Quicksilver Grail, which allows a quick surprise Crucible. Purifying Thurible clears Superior's graveyard to deny the Ringleader mill, and Scatter Essence handles Fractal of Rain.
Both players are patient. Superior waits with Engulf, Expel the Departed and Fracturize but never gets to flip Genbu for lethal.
Asuna brews a Speed Potion with Essence Crucible, protected by two Obscured Offerings. Agility Three returns cards from memory, and Three Visits plus Tempest Downfall deal 11 damage to Guo Jia.

games.summary: Superior wins — Infeebling Orb strips Asuna's hand, then a double Fugue

beats.text: Asuna opens with Razorgale Calling again and uses Zephyr to kill Superior's Censer of Restful Peace answer. Superior has Unbroken Mustang and Primordial Ritual in hand.
Asuna again sets up Essence Crucible with Quicksilver Grail. Superior plays Enfeebling Orb to tax Asuna's hand to four cards, which turns off Ensnaring Fumes.

Superior levels to Guo Jia level two, flips Genbu (16 life) and plays Resonating Fugue. Asuna cannot find the extra card for Innervate Agility, and Superior Engulfs the Innervate. Genbu's swing is lethal.

Casters call the Razorgale player "Asa" (omnidex username Asuna). Card names are as called by the casters and may contain minor ASR errors.

matches.round: Round 11 (Day 2, Round 2) — Fire Suzaku against Wind Crux Lorraine, both 8-2 and chasing Top 8

players.name: Tacoboss
players.deck: Fire Suzaku Guo Jia (Avatar of Suzaku, Peppered Chef, no Liminal Guide)

players.name: TeppeSlorn
players.deck: Wind Crux Lorraine (Aella, Zephyr, Poisonous Breezecap, Clarent)

sideboardNotes.text: TeppeSlorn has two Calming Breezes and Tempestuous Seraphim (a fast ally that deals four damage to an attacking ally) in the sideboard. The casters say the list was not built for a Suzaku deck.

Tacoboss looks at Sparklite (unpreventable damage, a way through Clarent), Gilded Pyre, Intensified Pyre, Restorative Flame and Shatter the Brittle. Sparklite is expected to come in. The Avatar of Suzaku is first seen in game 3.

games.summary: Tacoboss wins — fast Suzaku flip and a 12-damage Suzaku's Command

beats.text: Tacoboss levels Guo Jia into Fabled Ruby Fatestone. Intensified Pyre, Vermilion Decree (two targets, two quest counters) and Impact Hammer build quest counters fast. TeppeSlorn pops Clarent to stop the Fatestone and Impact Hammer damage.

TeppeSlorn plays only value cards: Poisonous Breezecap, Jiang Xiao, Stifling Gyre, Purifying Thurible, which eats the graveyard but the Phoenix does not need the graveyard on its first flip. TeppeSlorn has no Calming Breeze and only two Veiling Breezes in the main.
Blazing Throw adds the last quest counters, Suzaku flips, and Suzaku's Command adds eight unpreventable damage for a 12-damage swing that ends the game.

games.summary: TeppeSlorn wins — Clarent and Numinous Monks stall Suzaku, then Pale Sword sweeps the graveyard

beats.text: TeppeSlorn plays Stifling Gyre on Peppered Chef, and the Thurible turns up early. Clarent is used carefully this time, not wasted on small hits.

At 17 of 20 damage counters, TeppeSlorn finds Dungeon Guide and hits level three, then a Palvor Sword to remove the fire graveyard. Two Numinous Monks and Angelic Channeling to the bottom of the deck set up life and defense.
Clarent absorbs the Suzaku trigger (both champions take two less), so Tacoboss cannot gain quest counters. At 16 life he cannot swing the Impact Hammer for the extra two, and concedes.

games.summary: Tacoboss wins — full Peppered Chef combo for 24

beats.text: Tacoboss wins the roll and plays Avatar of Suzaku. At 4-3 it swings each turn, and paying two to sacrifice it adds quest counters and can put Fabled Ruby Fatestone back from the material deck or banishment. Fluffy Shopkeep prevents four damage.

TeppeSlorn levels with Dungeon Guide and swings into the Avatar, which Tacoboss sacrifices for two quest counters. TeppeSlorn spends a turn on Clarent rather than Thurible, and Enfeebling Orb and Tangu only slow the combo.

At six quest counters, a fate-stone ping and Demolition give the seventh. Tacoboss flips Vermillion Phoenix (4 damage), plays Suzaku's Command first (another four, unblockable) so the sixth fire card is in the graveyard, then Peppered Chef for 16. That is 24 damage.
