matches.round: Round 12 (Day 2, Round 3) — Seiryuu against Genbu, Superior chasing a Top 8 seat

players.name: TLux
players.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (Fatestone of Heaven, Uther, Angelic Channeling, Aella)

players.name: Superior
players.deck: Water Genbu Guo Jia (Diamond Ribbon package, Resonating Fugue)

sideboardNotes.text: TLux brings in Nullifying Lantern, four Expel the Departed, two Psychopomp's Gale, Unbroken Mustang, Song of Frost and perhaps Regal Inquisition. The casters call nearly the whole sideboard relevant.
Superior's side has Beastbond Boots, Orb of Sealing and the second Excalibur. Nothing major is confirmed as swapped.

games.summary: Superior wins — TLux misses a Fatestone trigger and cannot recover

beats.text: TLux wins the roll and plays an ally beatdown start: Forest Cake, Windmill Engineer, Aesan Protector and Purifying Thurible to deny Gentle Respite. Superior answers with Frostsworn Paladin and Fractal of Rain.
TLux plays Censer of Restful Peace and Angelic Channeling (Aella, Uther and Seiryuu's Command to the top), with a flip of the dragon possible next turn.

Superior plays Unbroken Mustang and then Primordial Ritual to sacrifice it, which targets TLux and mills Aella and Uther off the top before they can be drawn. TLux also misses a trigger and has to recover three, which is a big swing.
Superior levels to Guo Jia 2, flips Genbu and plays Resonating Fugue, then Frostsworn Paladin and an attack for lethal, with Engulf held up. TLux concedes.

games.summary: Superior wins — Genbu swings for 27 through a Psychopomp's Gale

beats.text: TLux plays Nullifying Lantern, Expel the Departed on Fractal of Rain, and a Dream Fairy. TLux keeps the dragon unflipped and builds influence with Incandescent Reliquary, using the Fatestone of Heaven to clear Frostsworn Paladin.

Superior removes the Lantern with Unbroken Mustang, plays Tidestone Bovine, Throne-keeper Bullfrog and Diamond Ribbon, and mills his own graveyard to 14 water cards. TLux's two Enfeebling Orbs keep the pressure on Superior's hand.

Superior goes to level three and flips Genbu. TLux plays Psychopomp's Gale, but Superior Engulfs it. Pop the Enfeebling Orb forces Superior to put two more cards down, and Veiling Breeze only prevents four. Genbu swings for 27 and Superior is 8-0-4.

matches.round: Round 13 (final Swiss round, Day 2) — Seiryuu against Genbu, a Top 8 race

players.name: ChemCollapse
players.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (turbo list: Angelic Channeling, Royal Oathguard, Imperial Countermeasure, Tricastles of Lucenia)

players.name: mDuo13
players.deck: Water Genbu Guo Jia (Song of Frost, Fractal of Polar Depths, Quicksilver Grail)

sideboardNotes.text: ChemCollapse has a large anti-Genbu side: Tricastles of Lucenia, two Sasha, Purifying Acolyte (banishes every graveyard when it fosters), Scatter Essence, Noble Dissolution, Blanch, Topsy Decree, Tempestuous Seraphim and Sunblessed Gazelle. The casters argue for nearly all of them, and Sasha and Tariff Ring are seen in game 2.
mDuo13 looks at Regal Inquisition, a fourth Song of Frost and Submerged Fatestone (a Genbu mirror card, not relevant here). Tariff Ring is seen in play.

games.summary: ChemCollapse wins — Regal Inquisition clears Song of Frost, then Seiryuu's Command

beats.text: ChemCollapse goes first and turbos: Forest Cake, then Angelic Channeling banishing three advanced-element cards for three quest counters. Guo Jia reaches level three on the third turn.

mDuo13 holds Throne-keeper Bullfrog as a taunter, plays Fractal of Polar Depths and uses Cerulean Decree to tax ChemCollapse's Dungeon Guide level up. A Tricastles of Lucenia mill would have been the back-breaking card, but the Sapphire Fatestone flip finds a Bullfrog.

ChemCollapse waits a turn before flipping the dragon, and uses Aella to suppress his own Bullfrog target. Regal Inquisition makes mDuo13 show a hand with two Song of Frost. ChemCollapse discards both, mDuo13 draws two and misses the third, and Seiryuu's Command for lethal resolves.

games.summary: ChemCollapse wins — Sasha shuts off the graveyard and Uther removes Genbu

beats.text: mDuo13 starts with Tidestone Bovines and Fractal of Rain, and gets Genbu to 9 quest counters. Purifying Thurible banishes his float and ChemCollapse's Tariff Ring shuts down the Fugue plan, which is one card short anyway.
ChemCollapse follows with Censer of Restful Peace, then Uther, Illustrious King, which deletes mDuo13's Fabled Sapphire Fatestone (Guo Jia is only level one). Uther kills the Bovine in combat.
ChemCollapse fosters Sasha, Purifying Acolyte, so no graveyard exists for the rest of the game. Smoke Bombs and Aella protect Sasha and Uther, and mDuo13 concedes.

matches.round: Round 13 (final Swiss round, Day 2) — Aetherwing Diana against Fire Luxem Zander, both 8-3-1

players.name: Fallinbuu14
players.deck: Water Aetherwing Diana (Cheshire Cat, Mad Hatter, Inert Sword, Palvor Sword, double Frostsworn Paladin)

players.name: Yadon
players.deck: Fire Luxem Zander (Serene Spirit, Angelic Channeling, Planted Explosive, Insignia of the Corhazi)

sideboardNotes.text: Yadon has Smoke Out main and in the side (to deal with Cheshire Cat), Planted Explosive ×2 and Crystallized Destiny. He says in the interview that he plays one Smoke Out main for turns where he has no preparation counter.
The casters expect Fallinbuu14 to bring in more Snow White, Weiss Queen and perhaps a third Rude, to stop Yadon levelling.

games.summary: Fallinbuu14 wins — Krustallan Archer and Ranger Strides for 12 through the Serene Spirit

beats.text: Fallinbuu14 has no distant enabler in the opener and plays Aetheric Calibration, Inert Sword and Cheshire Cat (a 3/3 with stealth and spell shroud) instead. Yadon uses Incapacitate on Reposition and Planted Explosive on the Cat.

Yadon opens with Angelic Channeling to protect Luxem Sight, Uncover the Plot and Lightweaver's Assault, levels Zander twice with Dungeon Guide, and stabilizes with Blinding Steel reveals and Tariff Ring.

Fallinbuu14 plays two Frostsworn Paladins, Quickstep Treads and Weaving Manastream. Yadon's Frostbind-able Planted Explosive are answered by a Frostbind. A final Incapacitate stops one distant enabler but Krustallan Archer plus Ranger Strides and a Cheshire Cat swing for 12 through the Serene Spirit.

games.summary: Yadon wins — double Lightweaver's Assault for lethal

beats.text: Fallinbuu14 finds only distant enablers and no Aether Charge, so the damage stays low. Yadon holds Topsy Decree, imbued, to strip the graveyard and levels to Zander level three with zero damage counters.

Yadon reveals Lightweaver's Assault, Sadi, Gleaming Cut and Luxem Sight through Blinding Steel and Corhazi Insignia, and uses Palvor Sword on Fallinbuu14's graveyard and Planted Explosive for Frostsworn Paladin. Fallinbuu14's Fracturize of the Insignia and Flash Grenade only delay.

Yadon reveals two Lightweaver's Assaults. Even through Flash Grenade (prevent three), each hits for four. With Exploit Vulnerability and the second Assault, the game ends. The Incapacitate held back covers the last reposition.

games.summary: Yadon wins — a final Lightweaver's Assault, with Fallinbuu14 two damage short

beats.text: Fallinbuu14 misses with Aetheric Calibration again and has Frostbind and two Backsteps instead of charges. Yadon removes Frostsworn Paladin and Cheshire Cat with Planted Explosive and a main-phase Topsy Decree.

Yadon uses Angelic Channeling again (Luxem Sight, Gleaming Cut, Excalibur) and takes Zander level three, though he forgets Lost Providence. Fallinbuu14 pushes 11 damage with Take Aim, Ranger Strides and a 12-card glimpse. Yadon's Chalice of Blood, Serene Spirit and Tariff Ring survive.

Fallinbuu14 gets within three, then two, damage of lethal on consecutive turns. Yadon uses Exploit Vulnerability and Mercenary's Blade on the Paladin, and finishes with Sadi and Lightweaver's Assault revealing seven cards.

matches.round: Top 8 — Quarterfinal (Diana beatdown against Exia Jin)

players.name: Zetdivx
players.deck: Water Aetherwing Diana (Cheshire Cat, Inert Sword, Nimble Longbowman, 17 distant enablers)

players.name: stevo7653
players.deck: Water Exia Jin (Regal Inquisition, Dynastic Whirlpool mill-out)

sideboardNotes.text: Zetdivx considers Song of Frost, Annihilation and Crimson Rupture-style cards but sees little that clearly needs to come in. The casters say that Zetdivx wants damage and allies, not more draw.

games.summary: Zetdivx wins — Diana pressure races Stevo before Jin level three

beats.text: Zetdivx opens with Backstep to become distant, gets Aquamirage Whisper on level up, and uses Refreshing Charge and Aetheric Calibration to glimpse. Stevo, on Fortuitous Water, has a full hand of Regal Inquisition, Frostbind and Fracturize but starts slowly.
Frostsworn Paladin and Krustallan Archer add damage each turn, and Stevo does not get to level three. Stevo's Jin is at 20 total life and cannot heal out of Zetdivx's damage.
Zetdivx closes out game one with a final Archer attack, while Stevo has no interaction left. The casters note that 14 damage was lethal on that turn.

games.summary: Zetdivx wins again — a two-turn kill before Stevo can reach level three

beats.text: Stevo starts with Gentle Respite and holds Dungeon Guide, Regal Inquisition and Dynastic Whirlpool. Spirit of Fortuitous Water gives him a slower spirit than serene water, and he plans to Fracturize Zetdivx's board.
Zetdivx plays Inert Sword, Cheshire Cat, Reposition and Quickstep Treads on turn two. Tactical Retreat saves the Cat and ends Stevo's one big attack, while Fracturize hits the Treads.

Stevo is on 21 life with a Serene Spirit heal but never gets to use his lineage release at the right time. Zetdivx swings for three, then lethal, and Jin dies at 24 total life. Zetdivx secures a Gauntlet invite and moves to the semifinals.

matches.round: Top 8 — Quarterfinal (untimed; the winner locks a Worlds slot)

players.name: Jett
players.deck: Razorgale Arisanna (Essence Crucible, raccoon package, Aesan Protector, Ensnaring Fumes, Orbital Ceiling)

players.name: ChemCollapse
players.deck: Wind Seiryuu Guo Jia (turbo list: Tricastles of Lucenia, Uther, Aella, Royal Oathguard, Regal Inquisition)

sideboardNotes.text: Jett brings in Turbo Charge (more norm cards, to pay for Tricastles of Lucenia), possibly Blessed Clergy, Topsy Decree and Mystic Purifier. Jett says in the interview that he rarely sides in Blessed Clergy.
ChemCollapse brings in the third Tricastles of Lucenia, Blanch and possibly Topsy Decree or Scatter Essence and Sasha, Purifying Acolyte, which could remove all Razorgales for good.

games.summary: ChemCollapse wins — Tricastles of Lucenia locks Razorgale, then Seiryuu's Command

beats.text: ChemCollapse uses Beseech the Winds to reach Guo Jia level one on turn one and builds quest counters with Scout the Land and Tangu. Jett responds with Fluffy Shopkeep, Backup Charger, and Windmill Engineer's Reclaim and trades.

After Dungeon Guide takes Guo Jia to level three, ChemCollapse plays Tricastles of Lucenia, preventing non-advanced element card activations. Once per turn, any player may banish a norm or advanced element card from hand to make Tricastles lose all abilities until end of turn.

ChemCollapse follows with Uther (removing a Razorgale), Aella and a Royal Oathguard. Jett plays three Dream Fairies, a Zephyr and Purifying Thurible but drops below six cards, which turns off Ensnaring Fumes. Aella suppresses Jett's Essence Crucible.
ChemCollapse flips Seiryuu, plays Seiryuu's Command (triple on-enter) to generate an Arcane Blast and empower it by eight. The Blast costs nothing and finishes Jett.

games.summary: Jett wins — Aesan Protector chip damage, then Zephyr and Veiling Breeze on the last Razorgale trigger

beats.text: Jett brings in Turbo Charge, plays Windmill Engineer and Aesan Protector early, and wants a board that can kill Tricastles of Lucenia in two turns. Fairy Whispers finds Razorgale Calling.

ChemCollapse levels with Beseech and Dungeon Guide and draws with Incandescent Reliquary, but a Tricastle banished by Throne-keeper mill and a Purifying Thurible deny him the lock. ChemCollapse plays Regal Inquisition on Jett, discarding Ensnaring Fumes, but Jett draws another copy. The replacement keeps Seiryuu locked down.

Jett plays two Razorgales and Essence Crucible with Distilled Water potions. Imperial Countermeasure absorbs the first trigger. Jett Zephyrs his own Aesan Protector and then uses Veiling Breeze as the final Razorgale trigger for lethal. The Aesan Protector is the MVP of the game.

games.summary: Jett wins the deciding game (not shown in full)

beats.text: ChemCollapse goes first for the first time in the match, uses Beseech the Winds on turn one and Portentous Tanggu, and holds Blanch and Dungeon Guide. Jett opens with Windmill Engineer, Aesan Protector and Fluffy Shopkeep, to keep at least four damage of allies on board against another Tricastle.

Jett finds Razorgale Calling, Aesan Protector and Ensnaring Fumes with Fairy Whispers and keeps six cards in hand so the dragon stays locked. The broadcast cuts to the semifinal and confirms Jett closed out the game 2-1 within the next couple of turns.

matches.round: Top 4 — Semifinal (Apex Players Guild against TM32; the winner reaches the Grand Finals)

players.name: Zetdivx
players.deck: Water Aetherwing Diana (Apex build: two Aetherwings, Cheshire Cat, Ranger Strides, Take Aim ×2, Aetheric Reforging)

players.name: Jett
players.deck: Razorgale Arisanna (raccoon package: four Bandit, two Protector Raccoon; Essence Crucible, Aesan Protector)

sideboardNotes.text: Jett brings in Obscured Offering (to protect Essence Crucible from a Fracturize), Topsy Decree, Turbo Charge, Blessed Clergy and Fluffy Shopkeep.
Zetdivx brings in a second Aetheric Reforging, Nullifying Mirror (to turn off Veiling Breeze), Expel the Departed, Nullifying Lantern as an option, Shademist Priestess.

games.summary: Zetdivx wins — a patient build-up, then a 19-damage one-shot

beats.text: Zetdivx goes first as the top seed and plays Censer of Restful Peace, which Jett's Fracturize removes. Zetdivx levels Diana, plays Aetheric Calibration to find Aetheric Reforging, and loads the Aquamirage Whisper.

Jett uses Protector Raccoon, Purifying Thurible and Veiling Breeze to blank the Whisper's first hit trigger. Jett has zero damage taken for much of the game and builds a hand of eight cards, while Zetdivx gets no float value.

Jett lands two Razorgales and Essence Crucible, but Zetdivx's Fracturize removes the Crucible (Jett has no Obscured Offering). Jett's hand has clunky norm cards, and Cyclical Breeze to get Veiling Breeze back is answered by Aetheric Reforging.

Zetdivx tests a Flash Grenade, gets no response, and then plays Krustallan Archer with Ranger Strides, two Take Aims and five Aether Charges in the Whisper. Quickstep Treads makes Jett's responses cost two more. That is a 19-damage swing and the attack finishes Jett.

games.summary: Jett wins — board control with raccoons and Aesan Protector

beats.text: Zetdivx starts with a Krustallan Archer to bait Veiling Breeze and holds Expel the Departed, Fracturize and the second Reforging. But Jett's Aesan Protector, Bandit and Protector Raccoon block float, and Dream Fairy locks Cheshire Cat.

Jett uses Aesan Protector to reclaim his raccoons and Windmill Engineer. Zetdivx plays a Seeker's Aetherwing to remove the Dream Fairy, but Skirting Step prevents the damage, and Zetdivx never gets a glimpse.
Jett gets Razorgale Calling off Fairy Whispers. Zetdivx has 14 damage and Jett holds 12 cards. Tariff Ring taxes attacks, and Zetdivx concedes.

games.summary: Jett wins — Essence Crucible with three counters and double Razorgale

beats.text: Bandit finds Bandit with a one-in-six scavenge. Jett denies Zetdivx's float again and strips Backup Charger lines. Shademist Priestess stops Razorgale pings for a while, and Jett needs Dream Fairy to remove it.

Zetdivx trades Weaving Manastream and Krustallan Archer for Aesan Protector, builds Ranger Strides, Inert Sword and Quickstep Treads, and plays Nullifying Mirror to turn off Veiling Breeze. Jett's Fluffy Shopkeep keeps Zetdivx's Cheshire Cat from connecting. Zetdivx uses Drown in Aether on a rested Bandit.

Jett plays Essence Crucible, brews Distilled Water potions through Ingredient Pouch for three counters and a second Razorgale from Fairy Whispers. Each wind card now deals eight damage. Zetdivx's two Shademist Priestesses recover, but Jett responds to each trigger and a Fairy Whispers finishes the game.

matches.round: Grand Finals — Apex Players Guild against TM32, both already qualified for Worlds

players.name: Quarax
players.deck: Water Aetherwing Diana (Apex build: Cheshire Cat, Krustallan Archer, Seeker's Aetherwing, Aetheric Reforging, Nullifying Mirror)

players.name: Jett
players.deck: Razorgale Arisanna (raccoon package, Essence Crucible, Viridian Protective Trinket, Tariff Ring)

matches.result: Jett wins 2-1 and is the North American Nationals 2026 champion

sideboardNotes.text: The casters recommend Expel the Departed, Aetheric Reforging, Nullifying Mirror and Shademist Priestess for Quarax. Mirror appears in game two; Priestess and Expel are seen in game three, when Expel removes Razorgale Calling.

The casters suggest Obscured Offering and another Zephyr, with Fluffy Shopkeep and Stifling Gyre as possibilities. Topsy Decree is later identified in Jett’s game-two hand; the full boarding package is not confirmed.

games.summary: Jett wins — Purifying Thurible and Protector Raccoon deny the float, then two Razorgales

beats.text: Jett opens with Purifying Thurible (not Censer of Restful Peace) and holds Protector Raccoon. Quarax's Krustallan Archer attack is answered by Protector Raccoon banishing the Charge the Soul float, so no card is drawn. Jett waits for the last moment to respond.

Bandit scavenges into a third raccoon. Fluffy Shopkeep, an animal, is protected by Protector Raccoon, and Viridian Protective Trinket makes Quarax's water cards cost two more. Quarax's Cheshire Cat kills the Fluffy Shopkeep and the Raccoon.

Jett plays two Razorgales and brews a Speed Potion in Essence Crucible. Quarax's Fracturize removes the Crucible (Jett has no Obscured Offering). Dream Fairy kills the Cheshire Cat, and Aesan Protector returns it to hand. Razorgale pings, Cyclical Breeze and Tariff Ring leave Quarax with one damage from death.
Calming Breeze prevents the final Razorgale trigger damage. Quarax has no way to deal the last damage to Jett or stop the board, and scoops. Jett leads 1-0.

games.summary: Quarax wins — Krustallan Archer with a float and Jett cannot imbue Skirting Step

beats.text: Quarax goes first and passes. He levels Diana on turn two with Backstep and Aquamirage Whisper, then hits with Nullifying Mirror in play, so Veiling Breeze is unavailable to Jett.

Jett plays Purifying Thurible and a Protector Raccoon, but Quarax Fracturizes the Thurible to force the response. Bandit scavenges six cards and puts two Razorgales and a Dream Fairy at the bottom, which hurts Jett's win conditions.

Quarax finally keeps a float and attacks with Krustallan Archer for four. Jett plays Skirting Step but cannot imbue it, so it prevents nothing, and Jett drops to one life. Jett is forced to level up and Quarax finishes the game.

games.summary: Jett wins — Bandit, Protector Raccoon and Razorgale's pings close out the title

beats.text: Jett goes first and plays Censer of Restful Peace and two Bandits. Quarax tries Frozen Dismissal on the Bandit, but Jett pays four and scavenges into Protector Raccoon with the fifth card. Quarax has no distant enabler and no Aetherwing, so Diana cannot start.

Jett levels to Arisanna with Reclaim and Windmill Engineer, imbues Skirting Step, and plays Razorgale Calling and Dream Fairy on the Cheshire Cat. Quarax finds Seeker's Aetherwing and Prudent Nock, but cannot get damage through the reclaimed Windmill Engineers and Dream Fairy.

Jett plays Essence Crucible. Quarax's Expel the Departed removes the first Razorgale, but Jett brews, Cyclical Breeze brings it back and Quarax has no Reforging. Quarax tries Reposition to become distant, and Jett answers with Veiling Breeze. Quarax is 2 damage short and Jett wins the title.

matches.sourceNote: Cleaned broadcast transcript, North American Nationals 2026 Grand Finals VOD, including a champion's interview with Jett. Casters call Jett "Ali/Ollie/Jet" and Quarax "Korax/Corax". Card names are as called by the casters and may contain minor ASR errors.
